1.29.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
gate sureśvare deve śakre ca sapurohite ..
jagatyāñca prayātāyāṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ .. 1 ..
1.29.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
गते सुरेश्वरे देवे शक्रे च सपुरोहिते ॥
जगत्याञ्च प्रयातायां देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥ 1 ॥
1.29.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When Śakra, the god who is lord of the gods, had gone with his priest, / and the Earth had departed, the god of gods, Maheśvara,

1.29.s:
aṅguṣṭhamātrako bhūtvā gaṅgātoye nyamajjata ..
so'vagāhya svalokasthāṃ gaṅgāṃ sarvagatāṃ nadīm .. 2 ..
1.29.d:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रको भूत्वा गङ्गातोये न्यमज्जत ॥
सोऽवगाह्य स्वलोकस्थां गङ्गां सर्वगतां नदीम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.29.m: having become the size of a thumb, submerged himself in the water of the Gaṅgā. / Having plunged into the all-pervading river Gaṅgā situated in his own world,

1.29.s:
tayohyamānaḥ prayayau vistīrṇaṃ candramaṇḍalam ..
navayojanasāhasro viṣkambho yasya kīrtitaḥ .. 3 ..
1.29.d:
तयोह्यमानः प्रययौ विस्तीर्णं चन्द्रमण्डलम् ॥
नवयोजनसाहस्रो विष्कम्भो यस्य कीर्तितः ॥ 3 ॥
1.29.m: Carried along by it, he reached the vast orb of the moon, / whose diameter is said to be nine thousand yojanas,

1.29.s:
vistārāddviguṇaścaiva pariṇāhaḥ samantataḥ ..
toyasāramayaṃ piṇḍa pitṝṇāṃ dhāmamadhyagam .. 4 ..
1.29.d:
विस्ताराद्द्विगुणश्चैव परिणाहः समन्ततः ॥
तोयसारमयं पिण्ड पितॄणां धाममध्यगम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.29.m: and its circumference all around is twice its width. / Consisting of the essence of water, an orb situated in the midst of the realm of the ancestors,

1.29.s:
prajānāṃ bhāvanaṃ sarvaṃ cādhāraṃ jagatāmapi ..
śarīriṇāṃ śaroreṣu rasaṃ pañcātmakaṃ smṛtam .. 5 ..
1.29.d:
प्रजानां भावनं सर्वं चाधारं जगतामपि ॥
शरीरिणां शरोरेषु रसं पञ्चात्मकं स्मृतम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.29.m: the sustainer of all creatures and the support of the worlds, / it is known as the fivefold bodily fluid in the bodies of embodied beings:

1.29.s:
ālambakaṃ kledakaṃ ca tathā caivāvabodhakam ..
saṃghātakaṃ tarpakañca dehināṃ dehagocaram .. 6 ..
1.29.d:
आलम्बकं क्लेदकं च तथा चैवावबोधकम् ॥
संघातकं तर्पकञ्च देहिनां देहगोचरम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.29.m: supporting, moistening, stimulating perception, / solidifying, and nourishing, operating in the bodies of embodied beings.

1.29.s:
manaḥsarvendriyāṇāñca sarveṣāṃ nāthakaṃ tathā ..
oṣadhīśaṃ jagadyonimamṛtādhāramavyayam .. 7 ..
1.29.d:
मनःसर्वेन्द्रियाणाञ्च सर्वेषां नाथकं तथा ॥
ओषधीशं जगद्योनिममृताधारमव्ययम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.29.m: Likewise it is the mind and the master of all sense organs, / the lord of plants, the source of the world, the imperishable vessel of nectar,

1.29.s:
yaṃ pibanti sadā devāḥ pitaraścāmṛtārthinaḥ ..
yaścakṣurdevadevasya viṣṇorvā sa prakīrtitaḥ ..8..
1.29.d:
यं पिबन्ति सदा देवाः पितरश्चामृतार्थिनः ॥
यश्चक्षुर्देवदेवस्य विष्णोर्वा स प्रकीर्तितः ॥8॥
1.29.m: which the gods and the ancestors, longing for nectar, constantly drink, / and which is proclaimed to be the eye of the god of gods, Viṣṇu.

1.29.s:
havyakavyāśano devo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ ..
praviśya maṇḍalaṃ tasya devadevo maheśvaraḥ .....
tasya yadvyāpakaṃ tejaḥ sūkṣmamannarasaṃ hi tam ..
aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ yaṃ budhāḥ ke śivaṃ viduḥ .. 1.29.10 ..
1.29.d:
हव्यकव्याशनो देवो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
प्रविश्य मण्डलं तस्य देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥॥।
तस्य यद्व्यापकं तेजः सूक्ष्ममन्नरसं हि तम् ॥
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं यं बुधाः के शिवं विदुः ॥ 1.29.10 ॥
1.29.m: The god who partakes of offerings to gods and ancestors, the self of beings, the source of beings, / having entered its orb, the god of gods, the great lord, / [perceived] that pervasive, subtle brilliance of his, which is indeed the essence of food, / that person the size of a thumb, whom some wise men know as Śiva,

1.29.s:
cakṣurgolakamadhyasthā dṛkśaktiriva yaḥ sthitaḥ ..
candragolakamadhyasthaḥ puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 11 ..
1.29.d:
चक्षुर्गोलकमध्यस्था दृक्शक्तिरिव यः स्थितः ॥
चन्द्रगोलकमध्यस्थः पुरुषः स परः स्मृतः ॥ 11 ॥
1.29.m: who abides like the faculty of sight stationed in the middle of the eyeball; / stationed in the middle of the orb of the moon, that person is remembered as the Supreme.

1.29.s:
karmasākṣī sa lokānāṃ sa cādhāraḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
ādityaraśmayaścaṃdre tamaḥsaṃmūrcchitaṃ kṣitau .. 12 ..
1.29.d:
कर्मसाक्षी स लोकानां स चाधारः परः स्मृतः ॥
आदित्यरश्मयश्चंद्रे तमःसंमूर्च्छितं क्षितौ ॥ 12 ॥
1.29.m: He is the witness of the deeds of the worlds, and he is remembered as the supreme support. / The rays of the sun in the moon, [and those] fainting away into darkness upon the earth,

1.29.s:
kṣapayiṣyaṃti yannaiśaṃ śītāṃśustasya tejasī ..
yasya rūpamanirdeśyaṃ yasya tejaḥ suduḥsaham .. 13 ..
1.29.d:
क्षपयिष्यंति यन्नैशं शीतांशुस्तस्य तेजसी ॥
यस्य रूपमनिर्देश्यं यस्य तेजः सुदुःसहम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.29.m: which will destroy the darkness of night—the cold-rayed [moon] abides in his fiery energy. / He whose form is indescribable, whose fiery energy is exceedingly difficult to endure—

1.29.s:
taṃ tu devavaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭāva tripurāntakaḥ ..
īśvara uvāca ..
agnīṣomamayaṃ caitajjagadetatprakīrtitam ..
agnīṣomau jagannāthau devadevo janārdanaḥ .. 14 ..
1.29.d:
तं तु देववरं दृष्ट्वा तुष्टाव त्रिपुरान्तकः ॥
ईश्वर उवाच ॥
अग्नीषोममयं चैतज्जगदेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
अग्नीषोमौ जगन्नाथौ देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥ 14 ॥
1.29.m: beholding that best of gods, the destroyer of Tripura praised him. / The Lord said: / 'This world is proclaimed to be composed of Agni and Soma. / Agni and Soma are the lords of the world, the god of gods, Janārdana.

1.29.s:
tasyāgneyī tanuryā ca so'haṃ sa ca divākaraḥ ..
saumyā tu yā tanustasya sa bhavān sa pitāmahaḥ .. 15 ..
1.29.d:
तस्याग्नेयी तनुर्या च सोऽहं स च दिवाकरः ॥
सौम्या तु या तनुस्तस्य स भवान् स पितामहः ॥ 15 ॥
1.29.m: His fiery body is both I and that maker of the day, / while his gentle body is you and the grandfather [Brahmā].

1.29.s:
tvayedaṃ dhāryate sarvaṃ nānyatpaśyāmi kāraṇam ..
tvadbimbe nirmale pṛthvī saśailavanakānanā 1...
1.29.d:
त्वयेदं धार्यते सर्वं नान्यत्पश्यामि कारणम् ॥
त्वद्बिम्बे निर्मले पृथ्वी सशैलवनकानना 1॥।
1.29.m: All this is upheld by you; I see no other cause. / In your spotless orb, the earth together with its mountains and forests

1.29.s:
śaśākṛtiḥ sadā dṛśyā śaśalakṣmā'si cānagha ..
tenaiva kāraṇena tvamucyase mṛgalāñchanaḥ .. 17..
1.29.d:
शशाकृतिः सदा दृश्या शशलक्ष्माऽसि चानघ ॥
तेनैव कारणेन त्वमुच्यसे मृगलाञ्छनः ॥ 17॥
1.29.m: is always seen in the form of a hare, and you are marked with a hare, O sinless one! / For that very reason you are called the deer-marked one.

1.29.s:
śaśī śaśatvasaṃbandhātsaumyatvātsoma ucyate ..
śītāṃśutvācca śītāṃśuḥ niśeśe tvadvirājanāt .. 18 ..
1.29.d:
शशी शशत्वसंबन्धात्सौम्यत्वात्सोम उच्यते ॥
शीतांशुत्वाच्च शीतांशुः निशेशे त्वद्विराजनात् ॥ 18 ॥
1.29.m: You are called Śaśin from your connection with having a hare; you are called Soma from your gentle nature; / you are Śītāṃśu because your rays are cool; and the lord of the night because you shine in it.

1.29.s:
nakṣatranāthastatsvāmyādrājatvāttvaṃ dvijeśvaraḥ ..
vasanti te pitṛgaṇāḥ pitṛnāthastato bhavān .. 19 ..
1.29.d:
नक्षत्रनाथस्तत्स्वाम्याद्राजत्वात्त्वं द्विजेश्वरः ॥
वसन्ति ते पितृगणाः पितृनाथस्ततो भवान् ॥ 19 ॥
1.29.m: You are the lord of asterisms because of your mastery over them; being a king, you are the lord of the twice-born. / The hosts of your ancestors dwell [in you]; therefore you are the lord of the ancestors.

1.29.s:
bahvarthaścandra ityeṣa dhāturukto manīṣibhiḥ ..
śuklatve hyamṛtatve ca śītatve hrādane'pi ca ..1.29.20..
1.29.d:
बह्वर्थश्चन्द्र इत्येष धातुरुक्तो मनीषिभिः ॥
शुक्लत्वे ह्यमृतत्वे च शीतत्वे ह्रादनेऽपि च ॥1.29.20॥
1.29.m: The verbal root candr- has been declared by the wise to have many meanings: / in the sense of whiteness, immortality, coolness, and also gladdening.

1.29.s:
tena te candratākhyātā satataṃ dharmavatsala! ..
sarve cāhlādamāyanti dṛṣṭe tvayi mahādyute .. 21 ..
1.29.d:
तेन ते चन्द्रताख्याता सततं धर्मवत्सल! ॥
सर्वे चाह्लादमायन्ति दृष्टे त्वयि महाद्युते ॥ 21 ॥
1.29.m: Therefore, O lover of dharma, your nature as the moon is constantly proclaimed; / and everyone attains delight when you are seen, O you of great splendour!

1.29.s:
prajākāryaṃ tvadāyattaṃ tatkuruṣva jagatprabho ..
dattātreyatvamāsādya tvayā dattavaro nṛpaḥ ..22..
1.29.d:
प्रजाकार्यं त्वदायत्तं तत्कुरुष्व जगत्प्रभो ॥
दत्तात्रेयत्वमासाद्य त्वया दत्तवरो नृपः ॥22॥
1.29.m: The business of creatures depends on you; therefore accomplish it, O lord of the world! / Having assumed the state of Dattātreya, a boon was granted by you to the king

1.29.s:
kārtavīryārjuno nāma dānavāstamupāśritāḥ ..
sarve kṣattriyatāṃ prāpya tadvadhe yatnavān bhava ..23..
1.29.d:
कार्तवीर्यार्जुनो नाम दानवास्तमुपाश्रिताः ॥
सर्वे क्षत्त्रियतां प्राप्य तद्वधे यत्नवान् भव ॥23॥
1.29.m: named Kārtavīryārjuna; the Dānavas have taken refuge in him, / all having attained the status of kṣatriyas; exert yourself for his destruction.

1.29.s:
tvayā dattavaraṃ hantuṃ nānyaḥ śaknoti kaścana..
avaśyaṃ ca tvayā kāryaṃ devakāryaṃ sadā vibho .. 24 ..
1.29.d:
त्वया दत्तवरं हन्तुं नान्यः शक्नोति कश्चन॥
अवश्यं च त्वया कार्यं देवकार्यं सदा विभो ॥ 24 ॥
1.29.m: No one else is able to slay one who has been granted a boon by you; / and you must certainly accomplish the task of the gods always, O pervasive one!'

1.29.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
śaṃkareṇaivamuktastu pratipūjya ca śaṃkaram ..
uvāca devadeveśaṃ praṇatārtiharaṃ haram .. 25 ..
1.29.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
शंकरेणैवमुक्तस्तु प्रतिपूज्य च शंकरम् ॥
उवाच देवदेवेशं प्रणतार्तिहरं हरम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.29.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'Addressed thus by Śaṃkara, he worshipped Śaṃkara in return, / and spoke to the lord of the god of gods, Hara, who removes the distress of the bowed:'

1.29.s:
candra uvāca ..
iyaṃ śaṅkara saumyā me tanuḥ suvihitā tava ..
tasmādarkasthitāṃ gaccha sā te kāmaṃ kariṣyati .. 26 ..
1.29.d:
चन्द्र उवाच ॥
इयं शङ्कर सौम्या मे तनुः सुविहिता तव ॥
तस्मादर्कस्थितां गच्छ सा ते कामं करिष्यति ॥ 26 ॥
1.29.m: The Moon said: / 'O Śaṅkara, this gentle body of mine has been well arranged for you. / Therefore, go to that [body of mine] abiding in the sun; it will accomplish your desire.'

1.29.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktastripurāntakārī somena rājñā parameśvareṇa ..
saṃpūjya devaṃ prayayau sa śīghraṃ tejomayaṃ maṃḍalamāśu rājan .. 27 ..
1.29.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्तस्त्रिपुरान्तकारी सोमेन राज्ञा परमेश्वरेण ॥
संपूज्य देवं प्रययौ स शीघ्रं तेजोमयं मंडलमाशु राजन् ॥ 27 ॥
1.29.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'Addressed in this manner by Soma, the king, the supreme lord, the enemy who destroyed Tripura, / having worshipped the god, quickly went, O king, to that orb full of fiery energy.'

1.30.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sa dadarśa tato gatvā vipulaṃ sūryamaṇḍalam ..
candramaṇḍalamānena mānaṃ yasya ca saṃskṛtam .. 1 ..
1.30.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
स ददर्श ततो गत्वा विपुलं सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥
चन्द्रमण्डलमानेन मानं यस्य च संस्कृतम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.30.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'Having gone there, he then saw the vast orb of the sun, / whose measure is perfected according to the measure of the orb of the moon,

1.30.s:
yattatprajvalitaṃ piṇḍaṃ piṇḍitasya vibhāvasoḥ ..
devadevasya yaddhāma vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ .. 2 ..
1.30.d:
यत्तत्प्रज्वलितं पिण्डं पिण्डितस्य विभावसोः ॥
देवदेवस्य यद्धाम वासुदेवस्य धीमतः ॥ 2 ॥
1.30.m: which is that blazing mass of concentrated fire, / which is the realm of the god of gods, wise Vāsudeva.

1.30.s:
tasya dharmaḥ paraṃ piṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍāntaradīpanam ..
āgāraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jaṭharasthaṃ hutāśanam .. 3 ..
1.30.d:
तस्य धर्मः परं पिण्डं ब्रह्माण्डान्तरदीपनम् ॥
आगारं सर्वभूतानां जठरस्थं हुताशनम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.30.m: His supreme mass is dharma, illuminating the interior of the cosmic egg, / the abode of all beings, the fire situated in the belly,

1.30.s:
pañcadhā'vasthitaṃ dehe sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ smṛtaḥ ..
ālocakaḥ pācakaśca rocako gañjakastathā .. 4 ..
1.30.d:
पञ्चधाऽवस्थितं देहे सर्वेषां प्राणिनां स्मृतः ॥
आलोचकः पाचकश्च रोचको गञ्जकस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
1.30.m: which is remembered as situated fivefold in the body of all living beings: / as the perceiver, the digester, the relisher, the extractor,

1.30.s:
bhrājakaśca tathā devaḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā ..
yanmayaṃ dehināṃ cakṣuryaścakṣurdakṣiṇastathā .. 5 ..
1.30.d:
भ्राजकश्च तथा देवः सर्वेषां प्राणिनां तथा ॥
यन्मयं देहिनां चक्षुर्यश्चक्षुर्दक्षिणस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.30.m: and the illuminator—the divine [fire] of all living beings; / of whose nature is the eye of embodied beings, and who is the right eye [of the world].

1.30.s:
sa vai devātidevasya vāsudevasya kīrtitaḥ ..
agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyaṅnityaṃ yatropatiṣṭhate .. 6 ..
1.30.d:
स वै देवातिदेवस्य वासुदेवस्य कीर्तितः ॥
अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यङ्नित्यं यत्रोपतिष्ठते ॥ 6 ॥
1.30.m: He is indeed proclaimed to be [the eye] of Vāsudeva, the god above gods, / where the oblation properly cast into the fire constantly attends.

1.30.s:
yasya dattaṃ sadā tejaḥ sarveṣāmeva tejasā ..
yasmādambudharotpattiryasmādvarṣaṇasambhavaḥ ..7 ..
1.30.d:
यस्य दत्तं सदा तेजः सर्वेषामेव तेजसा ॥
यस्मादम्बुधरोत्पत्तिर्यस्माद्वर्षणसम्भवः ॥7 ॥
1.30.m: From his fiery energy the fiery energy of all things is always given; / from him is the origin of clouds, and from him arises rain;

1.30.s:
yasmātpravartate sarvaṃ kālacakraṃ tathaiva ca ..
auṣadhīnāṃ paraḥ pākaḥ paraṃ yasmānna vidyate .. 8 ..
1.30.d:
यस्मात्प्रवर्तते सर्वं कालचक्रं तथैव च ॥
औषधीनां परः पाकः परं यस्मान्न विद्यते ॥ 8 ॥
1.30.m: from him proceeds the whole wheel of time as well; / he is the supreme ripening of plants, beyond which nothing exists.

1.30.s:
tanmaṇḍalamathāsādya kṛtvā rūpaṃ tu taijasam ..
viveśa maṇḍalaṃ bhittvā tanmadhyaṃ śaṅkarastadā .. 9..
1.30.d:
तन्मण्डलमथासाद्य कृत्वा रूपं तु तैजसम् ॥
विवेश मण्डलं भित्त्वा तन्मध्यं शङ्करस्तदा ॥ 9॥
1.30.m: Then, having reached that orb and assumed a fiery form, / Śaṅkara pierced the orb and entered its centre.

1.30.s:
so'ṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ dṛkśaktimiva veṣṭitam ..
taijasaṃ dṛṣṭavān rudraḥ tuṣṭāva ca mahādyutiḥ .. 1.30.10 ..
1.30.d:
सोऽङ्गुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं दृक्शक्तिमिव वेष्टितम् ॥
तैजसं दृष्टवान् रुद्रः तुष्टाव च महाद्युतिः ॥ 1.30.10 ॥
1.30.m: Rudra, of great splendour, saw that fiery person the size of a thumb, / as if enveloped in the faculty of sight, and praised him.

1.30.s:
rudra uvāca ..
tvāṃ namasyāmi deveśa tejasāṃ tu paraṃ nidhim ..
ārādhyastvaṃ vareṇyastvaṃ sarvabhūtabhavodbhavaḥ .. 11 ..
1.30.d:
रुद्र उवाच ॥
त्वां नमस्यामि देवेश तेजसां तु परं निधिम् ॥
आराध्यस्त्वं वरेण्यस्त्वं सर्वभूतभवोद्भवः ॥ 11 ॥
1.30.m: Rudra said: / 'I bow to you, O lord of gods, the supreme repository of fiery energies! / You are worthy of worship, you are most excellent, the source of the existence of all beings.

1.30.s:
svargadvāraṃ prajādvāraṃ mokṣadvāraṃ tathā bhavān..
anantaścāprameyastvaṃ sūkṣmātsūkṣmatarastathā .. 12 ..
1.30.d:
स्वर्गद्वारं प्रजाद्वारं मोक्षद्वारं तथा भवान्॥
अनन्तश्चाप्रमेयस्त्वं सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मतरस्तथा ॥ 12 ॥
1.30.m: You are the door to heaven, the door to progeny, and likewise the door to liberation; / you are infinite, immeasurable, and subtler than the subtle.

1.30.s:
mayā samarpitaṃ tejaḥ sakalaṃ tvayi bhāskara ..
mattastvaṃ na hi bhinno'si na ca devājjanārdanāt ..13..
1.30.d:
मया समर्पितं तेजः सकलं त्वयि भास्कर ॥
मत्तस्त्वं न हि भिन्नोऽसि न च देवाज्जनार्दनात् ॥13॥
1.30.m: All fiery energy has been deposited in you by me, O Bhāskara! / You are indeed not different from me, nor from the god Janārdana.

1.30.s:
ahaṃ viṣṇurbhavān viṣṇurbrahmā viṣṇuḥ prabhākara ..
asmākaṃ sakalaṃ dhāma tvayi tiṣṭhati bhāskara .. 14 ..
1.30.d:
अहं विष्णुर्भवान् विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा विष्णुः प्रभाकर ॥
अस्माकं सकलं धाम त्वयि तिष्ठति भास्कर ॥ 14 ॥
1.30.m: I am Viṣṇu, you are Viṣṇu, Brahmā is Viṣṇu, O light-maker! / All our light resides in you, O Bhāskara,

1.30.s:
dhāmakāryaṃ hi kriyate yenāsya jagataḥ sadā ..
prajānāṃ tu prasavanātsaviteti nigadyase .. 15 ..
1.30.d:
धामकार्यं हि क्रियते येनास्य जगतः सदा ॥
प्रजानां तु प्रसवनात्सवितेति निगद्यसे ॥ 15 ॥
1.30.m: by which the work of light is constantly performed for this world. / Because you bring forth creatures, you are called Savitṛ.

1.30.s:
rasānāñca tathā dānādravirityabhidhīyase ..
ādityastvaṃ tathā dānānmitrastvaṃ maitrabhāvataḥ ..16 ..
1.30.d:
रसानाञ्च तथा दानाद्रविरित्यभिधीयसे ॥
आदित्यस्त्वं तथा दानान्मित्रस्त्वं मैत्रभावतः ॥16 ॥
1.30.m: Because you bestow fluids, you are named Ravi; / you are Āditya from giving, and Mitra from your friendly disposition.'

1.30.s:
puṣṇāsi sakalām̐llokāṃstena pūṣā nigadyase ..
dhāraṇācca tathā dhātā yamanādaryamā tathā .. 17 ..
1.30.d:
पुष्णासि सकलाम्̐ल्लोकांस्तेन पूषा निगद्यसे ॥
धारणाच्च तथा धाता यमनादर्यमा तथा ॥ 17 ॥
1.30.m: You nourish all worlds, therefore you are called Pūṣan; / and from upholding [them] you are Dhātṛ, and Aryaman because of restraining.

1.30.s:
aṃśustvamaṃśudhāritvādvisargādvaruṇastathā ..
bhavaḥ saubhāgyavācyatvāttvaṣṭā sarvakriyākṛteḥ .. 18 ..
1.30.d:
अंशुस्त्वमंशुधारित्वाद्विसर्गाद्वरुणस्तथा ॥
भवः सौभाग्यवाच्यत्वात्त्वष्टा सर्वक्रियाकृतेः ॥ 18 ॥
1.30.m: You are Aṃśu from possessing rays, and Varuṇa from shedding [light]; / Bhava from being designated auspicious fortune, and Tvaṣṭṛ as the maker of every action.

1.30.s:
sarvajantusamatvācca vivasvānabhidhīyate ..
kramaṇācca tathā viṣṇurīśatvādindra ucyate .. 19 ..
1.30.d:
सर्वजन्तुसमत्वाच्च विवस्वानभिधीयते ॥
क्रमणाच्च तथा विष्णुरीशत्वादिन्द्र उच्यते ॥ 19 ॥
1.30.m: And because of impartiality to all creatures, he is named Vivasvat; / and from striding, [he is] Viṣṇu, and from lordliness, Indra.

1.30.s:
tasmāttvayā prajākāryaṃ kartavyamavicāritam ..
sthāvarairjaṃgamasthairvā bhūmirbhārābhipīḍitā .. 1.30.20 ..
1.30.d:
तस्मात्त्वया प्रजाकार्यं कर्तव्यमविचारितम् ॥
स्थावरैर्जंगमस्थैर्वा भूमिर्भाराभिपीडिता ॥ 1.30.20 ॥
1.30.m: Therefore, the work of the creatures must be done by you without hesitation. / The earth is oppressed by the burden of immovable or moving [beings].

1.30.s:
kadācijaṅgamairbhūmiḥ sūryabhāreṇapīḍitā ..
kadācitsthāvarairadya bhāradvitayapīḍitā .. 21 ..
1.30.d:
कदाचिजङ्गमैर्भूमिः सूर्यभारेणपीडिता ॥
कदाचित्स्थावरैरद्य भारद्वितयपीडिता ॥ 21 ॥
1.30.m: Sometimes the earth is burdened by moving beings, O Sun; / sometimes by immovable ones; today she is burdened by both weights.

1.30.s:
arjune nṛpatau vṛddhiḥ parā bhāskara śākhinām ..
daityāḥ kṣattriyatāṃ prāpya pīḍayanti ca medinīm .. 22 ..
1.30.d:
अर्जुने नृपतौ वृद्धिः परा भास्कर शाखिनाम् ॥
दैत्याः क्षत्त्रियतां प्राप्य पीडयन्ति च मेदिनीम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.30.m: Under king Arjuna, O Sun, the increase of trees is supreme; / and daityas, having attained the rank of kṣatriyas, oppress the earth.

1.30.s:
sūrya uvāca ..
tava darśanakāmena prāgeva na kṛtā mayā ..
sthāvarairjaṅgamaiḥ sarvāṃ prakṛtisthāṃ vasundharām .. 23 ..
1.30.d:
सूर्य उवाच ॥
तव दर्शनकामेन प्रागेव न कृता मया ॥
स्थावरैर्जङ्गमैः सर्वां प्रकृतिस्थां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.30.m: The Sun said: / Desiring the sight of you, I did not previously make / the whole earth restored to its natural state from the immovable and moving [beings].

1.30.s:
yathā pūrvaṃ tathā'dyāhaṃ kariṣyāmi maheśvara ..
sāmprataṃ brāhmaṇo bhūtvā cārjuneneva pādapān ..24..
1.30.d:
यथा पूर्वं तथाऽद्याहं करिष्यामि महेश्वर ॥
साम्प्रतं ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा चार्जुनेनेव पादपान् ॥24॥
1.30.m: As before, so today I will act, O Maheśvara. / Becoming a brahmin right now, by means of Arjuna himself I will destroy

1.30.s:
sarvānvināśayiṣyāmi śāsanena tathārjunam ..
vasiṣṭhādyojayiṣyāmi tatoṃśena vasundharām..25..
1.30.d:
सर्वान्विनाशयिष्यामि शासनेन तथार्जुनम् ॥
वसिष्ठाद्योजयिष्यामि ततोंशेन वसुन्धराम्॥25॥
1.30.m: all the trees, and Arjuna too by an order. / By means of Vasiṣṭha, I will then unite the earth with [my] portion;

1.30.s:
bhṛguvaṃśe kariṣyāmi tato niḥkṣattriyāṃ prajām ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktastripurāntakārī sūryeṇa sadraśmivirājitena ..
jagāma dhāma svamasau bibheti yatsarvalokāñjagatāṃ pradhānaḥ .. 26 ..
1.30.d:
भृगुवंशे करिष्यामि ततो निःक्षत्त्रियां प्रजाम् ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्तस्त्रिपुरान्तकारी सूर्येण सद्रश्मिविराजितेन ॥
जगाम धाम स्वमसौ बिभेति यत्सर्वलोकाञ्जगतां प्रधानः ॥ 26 ॥
1.30.m: in the lineage of Bhṛgu, I will then make the creatures devoid of kṣatriyas. / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been thus addressed by the Sun radiant with splendid rays, / that destroyer of Tripura, the foremost of the worlds of beings whom everyone reveres, went to his own abode.

1.31.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
dvijarūpamathāsthāya devadevo'pi bhāskaraḥ ..
māhiṣmatīṃ yayau śīghraṃ nagarīṃ ratnamālinīm...
sa tatra dadṛkṣe vīraṃ kārtavīryārjunaṃ nṛpam ..
yajamānaṃ sudordaṇḍaṃ kalpavṛkṣamivāparam ..2 ..
1.31.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
द्विजरूपमथास्थाय देवदेवोऽपि भास्करः ॥
माहिष्मतीं ययौ शीघ्रं नगरीं रत्नमालिनीम्॥।
स तत्र ददृक्षे वीरं कार्तवीर्यार्जुनं नृपम् ॥
यजमानं सुदोर्दण्डं कल्पवृक्षमिवापरम् ॥2 ॥
1.31.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, having assumed the form of a twice-born, the Sun, the god of gods, / went swiftly to the city of Māhiṣmatī, garlanded with jewels. / There he saw the heroic king Kārtavīryārjuna / performing sacrifices, with mighty arms, like a second wishing tree.
Honored by the son of Kṛtavīrya, the brahmin spoke to the king:

1.31.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca ..
mahāśanaṃ māṃ jānīhi brāhmaṇaṃ kṣudhayārditam ..
prayaccha tasya me tṛptiṃ tvameko haihayottama .. 4 ..
1.31.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच ॥
महाशनं मां जानीहि ब्राह्मणं क्षुधयार्दितम् ॥
प्रयच्छ तस्य मे तृप्तिं त्वमेको हैहयोत्तम ॥ 4 ॥
1.31.m: The brahmin said: / Know me to be a great eater, a brahmin afflicted with hunger. / You alone, O best of the Haihayas, grant me satisfaction!

1.31.s:
arjuna uvāca ..
kenā'nnena bhavattṛptiḥ kimannaṃ vidadhāmi ta ..
tanmamā''cakṣva bhagavan succhaṃdenaiva mā ciram .. 5 ..
1.31.d:
अर्जुन उवाच ॥
केनाऽन्नेन भवत्तृप्तिः किमन्नं विदधामि त ॥
तन्ममा'ऽचक्ष्व भगवन् सुच्छंदेनैव मा चिरम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.31.m: Arjuna said: / By what food comes your satisfaction? What food may I prepare for you? / Tell me that, O venerable one, according to your pleasure, without delay!

1.31.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca ..
ādityaṃ māṃ vijānīhi sthāvarānbhoktumudyatam ..
prayaccha tāni sarvāṇi mama pārthivapuṃgava .. 6 ..
1.31.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच ॥
आदित्यं मां विजानीहि स्थावरान्भोक्तुमुद्यतम् ॥
प्रयच्छ तानि सर्वाणि मम पार्थिवपुंगव ॥ 6 ॥
1.31.m: The brahmin said: / Know me to be Āditya, ready to consume immovable things. / Grant all of them to me, O bull among kings!

1.31.s:
arjuna uvāca ..
sthāvaraṃ bhūgataṃ dātuṃ śaktirnā'sti mamā'nagha ..
kathaṃ hi sthāvarā dagdhuṃ śakyā mānuṣyatejasā .. 7 ..
1.31.d:
अर्जुन उवाच ॥
स्थावरं भूगतं दातुं शक्तिर्नाऽस्ति ममाऽनघ ॥
कथं हि स्थावरा दग्धुं शक्या मानुष्यतेजसा ॥ 7 ॥
1.31.m: Arjuna said: / I do not have the power to give the immovable things on the earth, O sinless one. / How indeed can immovable things be burned by human power?

1.31.s:
āditya uvāca ..
rathasthaḥ pārthivaśreṣṭha śarānmuṃca yadṛcchayā ..
teṣvahaṃ prajvalanrājanbhakṣayiṣyāmi pādapān .. 8 ..
1.31.d:
आदित्य उवाच ॥
रथस्थः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ शरान्मुंच यदृच्छया ॥
तेष्वहं प्रज्वलन्राजन्भक्षयिष्यामि पादपान् ॥ 8 ॥
1.31.m: Āditya said: / Standing on a chariot, O best of kings, release arrows at will. / Blazing forth in them, O king, I will devour the trees.

1.31.s:
tāvadeva tvayā kāryaṃ nṛpate śaramokṣaṇam ..
yāvanna prajvaliṣyāmi mukteṣvapi śareṣvaham .. 9 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā gate sūrye kalpayitvā rathottamam ..
cikṣepa sa śarānrājā yatra tatra drumotkaram ..1.31.1 0..
te kṣiptā haihayeśena śātakauṃbhojjvalāḥ śarāḥ ..
jajvalannṛpaśārdūla jvalayaṃto vane drumān ..1 1..
1.31.d:
तावदेव त्वया कार्यं नृपते शरमोक्षणम् ॥
यावन्न प्रज्वलिष्यामि मुक्तेष्वपि शरेष्वहम् ॥ 9 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा गते सूर्ये कल्पयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
चिक्षेप स शरान्राजा यत्र तत्र द्रुमोत्करम् ॥1.31.1 0॥
ते क्षिप्ता हैहयेशेन शातकौंभोज्ज्वलाः शराः ॥
जज्वलन्नृपशार्दूल ज्वलयंतो वने द्रुमान् ॥1 1॥
1.31.m:
You must continue the releasing of arrows, O king, only so long / until I no longer blaze, even when arrows are released.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, when the Sun had gone, the king, having prepared an excellent chariot, / shot arrows here and there at the grove of trees.
Those arrows shot by the lord of the Haihayas, gleaming like gold, / blazed, O tiger among kings, setting fire to the trees in the forest.
With the roar of a kettle drum's sound, filled with swarms of sparks, / with surging flames and great swiftness, inspiring terror in all creatures,

1.31.s:
nirdahanvṛkṣapuṃjāni taptakāṃcanasuprabhaḥ ..
jvālāmālī tadā bhāti sarvataḥ pāvakaḥ kṣitau..13..
1.31.d:
निर्दहन्वृक्षपुंजानि तप्तकांचनसुप्रभः ॥
ज्वालामाली तदा भाति सर्वतः पावकः क्षितौ॥13॥
1.31.m: burning massed trees, with the fine lustre of molten gold, / garlanded with flames, the fire then shone everywhere on the earth.

1.31.s:
vaneṣu dahyamāneṣu tāpatṛṣṇārditā mṛgāḥ ..
jalāśayeṣu citreṣu gatacchāyāgnikeṣu ca .. 14 ..
1.31.d:
वनेषु दह्यमानेषु तापतृष्णार्दिता मृगाः ॥
जलाशयेषु चित्रेषु गतच्छायाग्निकेषु च ॥ 14 ॥
1.31.m: As the forests burned, deer, afflicted with heat and thirst, [sought] / the diverse bodies of water and places where shade and fire were absent.

1.31.s:
dadāhāgnistadā vṛkṣānyāvadicchā jagatpateḥ ..
babhūvā'tha praśāṃtārciḥ kṛtvā laghvīṃ vasuṃdharām.. 15..
1.31.d:
ददाहाग्निस्तदा वृक्षान्यावदिच्छा जगत्पतेः ॥
बभूवाऽथ प्रशांतार्चिः कृत्वा लघ्वीं वसुंधराम्॥ 15॥
1.31.m: The fire then burned the trees as long as the lord of the world desired; / then, having made the earth light, its flames were extinguished.

1.31.s:
na jajvāla tathā vahniḥ kārtavīryaśareṣvapi ..
kṛtakāryaṃ tadā gatvā kārtavīryo divākaram .. 16 ..
1.31.d:
न जज्वाल तथा वह्निः कार्तवीर्यशरेष्वपि ॥
कृतकार्यं तदा गत्वा कार्तवीर्यो दिवाकरम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.31.m: The fire no longer blazed even in Kārtavīrya's arrows. / Having accomplished his task then, Kārtavīrya, having gone to the Sun,

1.31.s:
vinivṛtya rathaṃ paścādyāvanmāhiṣmatīṃ purīm ..
sa gacchanneva dadṛśe vasiṣṭhaṃ sarvatejasam .. 17..
1.31.d:
विनिवृत्य रथं पश्चाद्यावन्माहिष्मतीं पुरीम् ॥
स गच्छन्नेव ददृशे वसिष्ठं सर्वतेजसम् ॥ 17॥
1.31.m: and then turned his chariot around towards the city of Māhiṣmatī, / saw while still going Vasiṣṭha, who possessed all splendours.

1.31.s:
tena śapto vane dagdhe svakīye nṛpapuṅgavaḥ ..
yasmāttvayā vanaṃ dagdhaṃ mama pārthivaśāsana! .. 18 ..
1.31.d:
तेन शप्तो वने दग्धे स्वकीये नृपपुङ्गवः ॥
यस्मात्त्वया वनं दग्धं मम पार्थिवशासन! ॥ 18 ॥
1.31.m: When his own forest was burned, the bull among kings was cursed by him: / 'Because a forest belonging to me was burned by you, O king's ruler,

1.31.s:
tasmācecchidyate bāhūn brāhmaṇaḥ śaṃsitavrataḥ ..
tena śāpena viprasya rāmaḥ kṣatriyanandanaḥ .. 19 ..
1.31.d:
तस्माचेच्छिद्यते बाहून् ब्राह्मणः शंसितव्रतः ॥
तेन शापेन विप्रस्य रामः क्षत्रियनन्दनः ॥ 19 ॥
1.31.m: therefore your arms will be cut off by a brahmin of praised vows!' / By that curse of the sage, Rāma, delight of the kṣatriyas,
the descendant of Bhṛgu, cut down all the forest of his arms.

1.31.s:
vajra uvāca ..
rāmastu kasminsa babhūva vaṃśe kathañca rājñastu mahābalasya ..
ciccheda dordaṇḍavanaṃ nṛvīraḥ sarvaṃ mamā''cakṣva bhṛgupradhāna .. 21 ..
1.31.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
रामस्तु कस्मिन्स बभूव वंशे कथञ्च राज्ञस्तु महाबलस्य ॥
चिच्छेद दोर्दण्डवनं नृवीरः सर्वं ममा'ऽचक्ष्व भृगुप्रधान ॥ 21 ॥
1.31.m: Vajra said: / In which lineage was that Rāma born, and how did the heroic warrior / cut down the forest of arm-stems belonging to that mighty king? Tell me everything, O foremost of the Bhṛgus!

1.32.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
sarvadevātidevasya brahmaṇastanayo bhṛguḥ ..
paulomyāṃ janayāmāsa cyavanaṃ bhagavānbhṛguḥ ..1..
1.32.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
सर्वदेवातिदेवस्य ब्रह्मणस्तनयो भृगुः ॥
पौलोम्यां जनयामास च्यवनं भगवान्भृगुः ॥1॥
1.32.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Bhṛgu was the son of Brahmā, the god beyond all gods; / the venerable Bhṛgu begot Cyavana on Paulomī.

1.32.s:
yayātijā sukanyāpi cyavanādbhṛgunandanāt ..
ātmavānaṃ dadhīcañca janayāmāsa dhārmikau ..2 ..
1.32.d:
ययातिजा सुकन्यापि च्यवनाद्भृगुनन्दनात् ॥
आत्मवानं दधीचञ्च जनयामास धार्मिकौ ॥2 ॥
1.32.m: Sukanyā too, daughter of Yayāti, bore from Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu, / the two righteous sons Ātmavāna and Dadhīca.

1.32.s:
ṛṣipatnī mahābhāgā cā''tmavānasya nāhuṣī ..
aurvaṃ saṃjanayāmāsa ṛcīkāparasaṃjñitam .. 3 ..
1.32.d:
ऋषिपत्नी महाभागा चा'ऽत्मवानस्य नाहुषी ॥
और्वं संजनयामास ऋचीकापरसंज्ञितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.32.m: And the illustrious wife of that sage, the daughter of Nahuṣa, / bore to Ātmavāna Aurva, also known as Ṛcīka.

1.32.s:
yena krodhābhibhūtena dṛṣṭo'gnirvaḍavāmukhaḥ ..
tasya satyavatī bhāryā kauśikī gādhijā śubhā .. 4 ..
1.32.d:
येन क्रोधाभिभूतेन दृष्टोऽग्निर्वडवामुखः ॥
तस्य सत्यवती भार्या कौशिकी गाधिजा शुभा ॥ 4 ॥
1.32.m: By him, overcome with anger, the submarine fire of the mare's mouth was seen. / His wife was the auspicious Satyavatī, a Kauśikī, daughter of Gādhi.

1.32.s:
tasyāṃ sañjanayāmāsa putrāṇāṃ śatamūrjitam ..
jamadagniśca vatsaśca teṣāṃ śreṣṭhatamāvubhau .. 5 ..
1.32.d:
तस्यां सञ्जनयामास पुत्राणां शतमूर्जितम् ॥
जमदग्निश्च वत्सश्च तेषां श्रेष्ठतमावुभौ ॥ 5 ॥
1.32.m: Upon her he begot a hundred vigorous sons; / Jamadagni and Vatsa were the two foremost of them.

1.32.s: strīṇāṃ caruviparyāsājjamadagnirajāyata .. 6 ..
1.32.d: स्त्रीणां चरुविपर्यासाज्जमदग्निरजायत ॥ 6 ॥
1.32.m: Through the exchange of sacrificial offerings by the women, Jamadagni was born.

1.32.s:
vajra uvāca ..
kathyatāmme yato brahmanvāḍavasya ca saṃbhavaḥ ..
saṃbhavaṃ jamadagneśca śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .. 7 ..
1.32.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
कथ्यताम्मे यतो ब्रह्मन्वाडवस्य च संभवः ॥
संभवं जमदग्नेश्च श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.32.m: Vajra said: / Tell me, O brahmin, whence the origin of that submarine fire was; / and I wish to hear truly the origin of Jamadagni.

1.32.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhṛgūṇāṃ haihayānāñca vairamāsītsudāruṇam ..
dhanahetostadā pāpairhaihayairbhṛgavo hatāḥ .. 8 ..
1.32.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भृगूणां हैहयानाञ्च वैरमासीत्सुदारुणम् ॥
धनहेतोस्तदा पापैर्हैहयैर्भृगवो हताः ॥ 8 ॥
1.32.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There was a very terrible enmity between the Bhṛgus and the Haihayas. / For the sake of wealth, the Bhṛgus were then slain by the sinful Haihayas.

1.32.s:
ye'pi garbhagatā bālāste'pi taiviniṣūditāḥ ..
garbheṣu hanyamāneṣu ṛṣiḥ paramaduḥkhitaḥ .. 9 ..
1.32.d:
येऽपि गर्भगता बालास्तेऽपि तैविनिषूदिताः ॥
गर्भेषु हन्यमानेषु ऋषिः परमदुःखितः ॥ 9 ॥
1.32.m: Even the children in the womb were slaughtered by them. / As the embryos were being slain, the sage, deeply grieved,

1.32.s:
aruṇaṃ dhārayāmāsa garbheṣṭaṃ dīptatejasam ..
pūrṇe kāle tadā bāla ūruṃ bhittvā vyajāyata .. 1.32.10 ..
1.32.d:
अरुणं धारयामास गर्भेष्टं दीप्ततेजसम् ॥
पूर्णे काले तदा बाल ऊरुं भित्त्वा व्यजायत ॥ 1.32.10 ॥
1.32.m: held in his thigh the desired embryo, blazing with splendour. / When the full time arrived, the boy was born, having torn open the thigh.

1.32.s:
jātamātrastu cukrodha devatānāṃ mahātapā ..
haihayairhanyamānānāṃ bandhūnāṃ sumahātmanām .. 11 ..
1.32.d:
जातमात्रस्तु चुक्रोध देवतानां महातपा ॥
हैहयैर्हन्यमानानां बन्धूनां सुमहात्मनाम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.32.m: As soon as he was born, the great ascetic was enraged at the gods: / 'When your kinsmen of exalted soul were being slain by the Haihayas,

1.32.s:
bhavadbhirna kṛtaṃ trāṇaṃ tasmātsarvāñśapāmyaham ..
taṃ kruddhaṃ pitaro hantuṃ vārayāmāsurojasā ..12..
1.32.d:
भवद्भिर्न कृतं त्राणं तस्मात्सर्वाञ्शपाम्यहम् ॥
तं क्रुद्धं पितरो हन्तुं वारयामासुरोजसा ॥12॥
1.32.m: no protection was given by you; therefore I curse you all!' / As he was enraged to destroy them, the ancestors restrained him by their power:

1.32.s:
krodhaḥ putra na kartavyaḥ sa hi śatrurnṛṇāṃ sadā ..
vayaṃ sarve jitakrodhāḥ kṣatriyairvinipātitāḥ ..13..
1.32.d:
क्रोधः पुत्र न कर्तव्यः स हि शत्रुर्नृणां सदा ॥
वयं सर्वे जितक्रोधाः क्षत्रियैर्विनिपातिताः ॥13॥
1.32.m: 'Anger must not be indulged, son; it is ever the enemy of men. / We, having all conquered anger, were struck down by the kṣatriyas.

1.32.s:
asmākaṃ na vadhe śaktāḥ kṣatriyā haihayādhipāḥ ..
evamuktaḥ pitṛgaṇairṛcīkastānathā'bravīt .. 14 ..
1.32.d:
अस्माकं न वधे शक्ताः क्षत्रिया हैहयाधिपाः ॥
एवमुक्तः पितृगणैरृचीकस्तानथाऽब्रवीत् ॥ 14 ॥
1.32.m: The kṣatriyas, the lords of the Haihayas, were not capable of slaying us.' / Addressed thus by the company of ancestors, Ṛcīka then said to them:

1.32.s:
na hi me śāmyati krodho yuṣmannidhanakāritaḥ ..
tasmāddevagaṇānsarvānnihaniṣyāmi tejasā ..15..
1.32.d:
न हि मे शाम्यति क्रोधो युष्मन्निधनकारितः ॥
तस्माद्देवगणान्सर्वान्निहनिष्यामि तेजसा ॥15॥
1.32.m: 'My anger, caused by your slaughter, does not subside; / therefore I will destroy all the hosts of gods with my fiery energy!'

1.32.s:
etasminneva kāle tu mahītoyasamākulā ..
jagāma śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvabhūtabhavodbhavam .. .. 16 ..
1.32.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु महीतोयसमाकुला ॥
जगाम शरणं विष्णुं सर्वभूतभवोद्भवम् ॥ ॥ 16 ॥
1.32.m: At that very time, the earth, overwhelmed with waters, / went for refuge to Viṣṇu, the source of the birth and existence of all beings.

1.32.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
devānprati samutpannaṃ krodhamaurvasya yacchubham ..
taṃ praviśya grasiṣyāmi toyaṃ sarvaṃ vasundhare..17..
1.32.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
देवान्प्रति समुत्पन्नं क्रोधमौर्वस्य यच्छुभम् ॥
तं प्रविश्य ग्रसिष्यामि तोयं सर्वं वसुन्धरे॥17॥
1.32.m: The Holy One said: / 'The anger born of Aurva against the gods, which is auspicious— / entering that, I shall swallow all the water, O Earth!'

1.32.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
ityevamuktvā vasudhāmaurvaṃ krodhaṃ samāviśat ..
bhūtvā ca vaḍavāvaktrastaccharīrādvinissṛtaḥ .. 18 ..
1.32.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वसुधामौर्वं क्रोधं समाविशत् ॥
भूत्वा च वडवावक्त्रस्तच्छरीराद्विनिस्सृतः ॥ 18 ॥
1.32.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus to the earth, he entered Aurva's anger, / and having become mare-faced, he emerged from that body.

1.32.s:
na trātāro bhaviṣyanti putra sarve divaukasaḥ ..
krodhaścā'yaṃ tava vṛthā na bhaviṣyati putraka .. 19 ..
1.32.d:
न त्रातारो भविष्यन्ति पुत्र सर्वे दिवौकसः ॥
क्रोधश्चाऽयं तव वृथा न भविष्यति पुत्रक ॥ 19 ॥
1.32.m: 'All the celestials will not be protectors, son, / nor will this anger of yours be in vain, dear child.'

1.32.s:
evamuktastu bhṛguṇā ṛcīkā'gnimabhāṣata ..
pūrvottare samāsādya samudre vasa putraka .. 1.32.20 ...
1.32.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु भृगुणा ऋचीकाऽग्निमभाषत ॥
पूर्वोत्तरे समासाद्य समुद्रे वस पुत्रक ॥ 1.32.20 ॥।
1.32.m: Addressed thus by Bhṛgu, Ṛcīka spoke to the fire: / 'Having reached the ocean in the northeast, dwell there, dear child,

1.32.s:
pibam̐statra sadā vegamambhasāṃ sumahādyute ..
asmākaṃ tu kule bhāvī kṣatradharmā dvijottamaḥ .. 21 ..
1.32.d:
पिबम्̐स्तत्र सदा वेगमम्भसां सुमहाद्युते ॥
अस्माकं तु कुले भावी क्षत्रधर्मा द्विजोत्तमः ॥ 21 ॥
1.32.m: ever drinking the force of the waters there, O one of immense radiance! / In our family, moreover, there will be a foremost twice-born of kṣatriya duty,

1.32.s:
kṣatriyāṇāṃ samucchedaṃ yaḥ kariṣyatyanekaśaḥ ...
evamuktastu pitrā vai pibanmāsāṣṭakaṃ jalam .. 22 ..
1.32.d:
क्षत्रियाणां समुच्छेदं यः करिष्यत्यनेकशः ॥।
एवमुक्तस्तु पित्रा वै पिबन्मासाष्टकं जलम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.32.m: who will bring about the destruction of the kṣatriyas many times.' / Addressed thus by his father, drinking water for eight months,

1.32.s:
caitramāsaṃ samārabhya nityamāste sukhī jale ..
pītaṃ māsāṣṭakaṃ toyaṃ jaṭhare bhasmasādgatam ... .. 23 ..
1.32.d:
चैत्रमासं समारभ्य नित्यमास्ते सुखी जले ॥
पीतं मासाष्टकं तोयं जठरे भस्मसाद्गतम् ॥॥। 23 ॥
1.32.m: beginning with the month of Caitra, he remains ever happy in the water. / The water drunk for eight months is reduced to ash in his belly.

1.32.s:
kṛtkṛtya māsām̐ścaturaḥ śiśirākhye mahītale ..
nityaṃ himoghaṃ sṛjati tasmādapi samīraṇaḥ ..24 ..
1.32.d:
कृत्कृत्य मासाम्̐श्चतुरः शिशिराख्ये महीतले ॥
नित्यं हिमोघं सृजति तस्मादपि समीरणः ॥24 ॥
1.32.m: Having done this for four months, on the surface of the earth called the cold season, / he constantly emits a flood of snow; and from that also the wind,

1.32.s:
himācale pātayati pravāho nāma pārthiva ..
eṣā toyāddhimotpattirhimatau yasya saṃbhavaḥ .. 25 ..
1.32.d:
हिमाचले पातयति प्रवाहो नाम पार्थिव ॥
एषा तोयाद्धिमोत्पत्तिर्हिमतौ यस्य संभवः ॥ 25 ॥
1.32.m: named Pravāha, casts it down upon the Himācala, O king. / This is the origin of snow from water, whose generation is in the cold season;

1.32.s: vṛddhikṣayavihīnasya kathitaṃ tava dhārmika .. 26 ..
1.32.d: वृद्धिक्षयविहीनस्य कथितं तव धार्मिक ॥ 26 ॥
1.32.m: it has been told to you, O righteous one, devoid of increase and decay.

1.32.s:
utpattireṣā tava vāḍavāgneḥ proktā mayā bhūmipatipradhāna ..
śrutvā'pi yāṃ muñcati mohajālaṃ saṃsārajāteśca yathā prabuddhaḥ .. 27 ..
1.32.d:
उत्पत्तिरेषा तव वाडवाग्नेः प्रोक्ता मया भूमिपतिप्रधान ॥
श्रुत्वाऽपि यां मुञ्चति मोहजालं संसारजातेश्च यथा प्रबुद्धः ॥ 27 ॥
1.32.m: This origin of the mare-faced submarine fire has been told to you by me, foremost of kings; / even hearing which, one casts off the snare of delusion and the cycle of worldly existence like an awakened man.

1.33.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
aurvasya bhāryā dharmajñā nāmnā satyavatī śubhā ..
vane paryacaradbhaktyā gādhijā bhṛgunandanam .. 1 ..
1.33.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
और्वस्य भार्या धर्मज्ञा नाम्ना सत्यवती शुभा ॥
वने पर्यचरद्भक्त्या गाधिजा भृगुनन्दनम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.33.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Aurva's wife was knower of dharma, named auspicious Satyavatī; / born of Gādhi, she attended upon the delight of the Bhṛgus in the forest with devotion.

1.33.s:
tasyā paramayā bhaktyā bhartā toṣamupāgataḥ ..
uvāca tāṃ varārohāmṛcīko bhṛgunandanaḥ .. 2 ..
1.33.d:
तस्या परमया भक्त्या भर्ता तोषमुपागतः ॥
उवाच तां वरारोहामृचीको भृगुनन्दनः ॥ 2 ॥
1.33.m: Her husband came to be pleased by her supreme devotion; / Ṛcīka, the delight of the Bhṛgus, spoke to that woman of lovely hips:

1.33.s:
.. ṛcīka uvāca .. ..
varaṃ varaya suśroṇi yatte manasi vartate ..
toṣito'haṃ tvayā bhadre vane śuśrūṣayā vada .. 3 ..
1.33.d:
॥ ऋचीक उवाच ॥ ॥
वरं वरय सुश्रोणि यत्ते मनसि वर्तते ॥
तोषितोऽहं त्वया भद्रे वने शुश्रूषया वद ॥ 3 ॥
1.33.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'Choose a boon, O woman of beautiful hips, whatever is in your mind! / I am pleased by you through your service in the forest, O gentle one; speak!'

1.33.s:
satyavatyuvāca ..
mātuḥ prayaccha me putraṃ bhagavanvīryavattaram..
putraṃ mama ca dharmajñaṃ yutaṃ brāhmaṇatejasā .. 4 ..
1.33.d:
सत्यवत्युवाच ॥
मातुः प्रयच्छ मे पुत्रं भगवन्वीर्यवत्तरम्॥
पुत्रं मम च धर्मज्ञं युतं ब्राह्मणतेजसा ॥ 4 ॥
1.33.m: Satyavatī said: / 'Grant a son of greater valor to my mother, O lord, / and a son to me, a knower of dharma endowed with brahminical radiance.'

1.33.s:
ṛcīka uvāca ..
carudvayaṃ kariṣyāmi māturarthe tathā tava ..
yasya saṃprāśanātputraṃ tvaṃ caiva janayiṣyasi .. 5 ..
1.33.d:
ऋचीक उवाच ॥
चरुद्वयं करिष्यामि मातुरर्थे तथा तव ॥
यस्य संप्राशनात्पुत्रं त्वं चैव जनयिष्यसि ॥ 5 ॥
1.33.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'I shall prepare two offerings of boiled rice, for your mother's sake and for yours, / by the eating of which you and she shall bear a son.'

1.33.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā tadā cakre ṛcīkastu carudvayam ..
ekasminsakalaṃ kṣātraṃ tejaścakre savaiṣṇavam .. 6 ..
1.33.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा तदा चक्रे ऋचीकस्तु चरुद्वयम् ॥
एकस्मिन्सकलं क्षात्रं तेजश्चक्रे सवैष्णवम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.33.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, Ṛcīka then made the two offerings of boiled rice; / into one he placed all the martial power along with the Vaiṣṇava power.

1.33.s:
śvaśrvarthe taṃ caruṃ kṛtvā dvitīye sa nyaveśayat ..
brāhmaṃ raudrañca yattejaḥ patnyarthe kṛtavāñcarum ..7..
1.33.d:
श्वश्र्वर्थे तं चरुं कृत्वा द्वितीये स न्यवेशयत् ॥
ब्राह्मं रौद्रञ्च यत्तेजः पत्न्यर्थे कृतवाञ्चरुम् ॥7॥
1.33.m: Having made that boiled rice for his mother-in-law, into the second he deposited / the power belonging to Brahmā and Rudra; he made that boiled rice for his wife.

1.33.s:
ṛcīka uvāca ..
ayaṃ prāśyastvayā bhadre tvayaṃ mātrā carustava ..
aśvatthāliṅganaṃ kāryaṃ mātrā tatra tadā śubhe .. 8...
1.33.d:
ऋचीक उवाच ॥
अयं प्राश्यस्त्वया भद्रे त्वयं मात्रा चरुस्तव ॥
अश्वत्थालिङ्गनं कार्यं मात्रा तत्र तदा शुभे ॥ 8॥।
1.33.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'This is to be eaten by you, O gentle one, and this your offering by your mother; / an embracing of the sacred fig tree is to be performed by your mother at that time, O auspicious one,

1.33.s: tathaivaudumbarasyā'pi tvayā rājīvalocane .. 9 ..
1.33.d: तथैवौदुम्बरस्याऽपि त्वया राजीवलोचने ॥ 9 ॥
1.33.m: and likewise that of the cluster fig tree by you, O lotus-eyed one.'

1.33.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktā tato gatvā mātre sarvaṃ nyavedayat .. 1.33.10 ..
1.33.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्ता ततो गत्वा मात्रे सर्वं न्यवेदयत् ॥ 1.33.10 ॥
1.33.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed thus, she then went and reported everything to her mother.

1.33.s:
tatastāmabravīnmātā gādheḥ patnī yaśasvinī ..
dhruvaṃ bhagavatā putrastava putracikīrṣayā .. 11 ..
1.33.d:
ततस्तामब्रवीन्माता गाधेः पत्नी यशस्विनी ॥
ध्रुवं भगवता पुत्रस्तव पुत्रचिकीर्षया ॥ 11 ॥
1.33.m: Then her mother, the illustrious wife of Gādhi, said to her: / 'Surely, with the desire to make your son prominent, the lord

1.33.s:
śreṣṭhena tejasā yuktaścarureṣa kṛtaḥ śubhe ..
tasmāccaruviparyāsaṃ madarthe kuru mā ciram..12..
1.33.d:
श्रेष्ठेन तेजसा युक्तश्चरुरेष कृतः शुभे ॥
तस्माच्चरुविपर्यासं मदर्थे कुरु मा चिरम्॥12॥
1.33.m: has prepared this boiled rice endowed with superior power, O auspicious one; / therefore, make an exchange of the boiled rice for my sake without delay!

1.33.s:
aliṅgane viparyāsaṃ drumayoḥ kriyatāṃ tathā ..
sā māturvacanaṃ sarvaṃ cakre gauravayantritā ..13..
1.33.d:
अलिङ्गने विपर्यासं द्रुमयोः क्रियतां तथा ॥
सा मातुर्वचनं सर्वं चक्रे गौरवयन्त्रिता ॥13॥
1.33.m: Likewise let an exchange be made in the embracing of the two trees.' / Bound by respect, she did all according to her mother's word.

1.33.s: sagarbhāṃ sa gate kāle bhartā vacanamabravīt .. 14 ..
1.33.d: सगर्भां स गते काले भर्ता वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 14 ॥
1.33.m: When time had passed, her husband spoke this word to her who was pregnant:

1.33.s:
ṛcīka uvāca ..
dhruvaṃ caruviparyāso drumayośca tvayā kṛtam ..
yena tvamasitāpāṅgi yuktā kṣatriyatejasā .. 15 ..
1.33.d:
ऋचीक उवाच ॥
ध्रुवं चरुविपर्यासो द्रुमयोश्च त्वया कृतम् ॥
येन त्वमसितापाङ्गि युक्ता क्षत्रियतेजसा ॥ 15 ॥
1.33.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'Surely an exchange of the boiled rice and of the two trees was made by you, / whereby you are endowed with kṣatriya power, O dark-eyed one!

1.33.s:
brāhmeṇa tejasā yuktaṃ kṛtavānasmi te carum ..
mātuste cārusarvāṃgi tathā kṣattriyatejasā .. 16 ..
1.33.d:
ब्राह्मेण तेजसा युक्तं कृतवानस्मि ते चरुम् ॥
मातुस्ते चारुसर्वांगि तथा क्षत्त्रियतेजसा ॥ 16 ॥
1.33.m: I prepared your boiled rice endowed with brahminical power, / and your mother's, O lovely-limbed one, with kṣatriya power.

1.33.s:
kṛtaṃ caruviparyāsaṃ sā vipraṃ janayiṣyati ..
kṣatradharmarataṃ putraṃ vipraṃ tvaṃ janayiṣyasi ..17..
1.33.d:
कृतं चरुविपर्यासं सा विप्रं जनयिष्यति ॥
क्षत्रधर्मरतं पुत्रं विप्रं त्वं जनयिष्यसि ॥17॥
1.33.m: An exchange of the boiled rice having been made, she will give birth to a brahmin, / while you will give birth to a brahmin son devoted to kṣatriya duty.'

1.33.s:
satyavatyuvāca.. māturmatātkṛtamidaṃ bhagavankṣantumarhasi ..
kṣatradharmarataḥ putro na me bhavitumarhati .. .. 18 ..
1.33.d:
सत्यवत्युवाच॥ मातुर्मतात्कृतमिदं भगवन्क्षन्तुमर्हसि ॥
क्षत्रधर्मरतः पुत्रो न मे भवितुमर्हति ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
1.33.m: Satyavatī said: / 'This was done at my mother's opinion, O lord; you ought to forgive me. / My son ought not to be devoted to kṣatriya duty.'

1.33.s:
ṛcīka uvāca ..
evamastu na te putraḥ kṣatradharmā bhaviṣyati ..
pautrastvavaśyaṃ bhavitā bhāvyarthavidhicoditaḥ .. 19 ..
1.33.d:
ऋचीक उवाच ॥
एवमस्तु न ते पुत्रः क्षत्रधर्मा भविष्यति ॥
पौत्रस्त्ववश्यं भविता भाव्यर्थविधिचोदितः ॥ 19 ॥
1.33.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'So be it; your son will not follow kṣatriya duty; / but your grandson will inevitably become so, impelled by the decree of destiny.'

1.33.s:
satyavatyuvāca ..
sarveśvaratvaṃ bhagavankimarthaṃ pautrasya me kṣatriyabhāvamugram..
nivartituṃ necchasi mātulena vadasva tanme yadi te na guhyam .. 1.33.20 ..
1.33.d:
सत्यवत्युवाच ॥
सर्वेश्वरत्वं भगवन्किमर्थं पौत्रस्य मे क्षत्रियभावमुग्रम्॥
निवर्तितुं नेच्छसि मातुलेन वदस्व तन्मे यदि ते न गुह्यम् ॥ 1.33.20 ॥
1.33.m: Satyavatī said: / 'O lord of all, why do you not wish the fierce nature of a kṣatriya to be averted / from my grandson along with his maternal uncle? Tell me that, if it is not a secret to you.'

1.34.s:
ṛcīka uvāca ..
brahmaṇo'triḥ sutaḥ saumyaḥ sutastasyā'pi candramāḥ ..
somasya tu budhaḥ putro budhaputraḥ purūravāḥ .. 1 ..
1.34.d:
ऋचीक उवाच ॥
ब्रह्मणोऽत्रिः सुतः सौम्यः सुतस्तस्याऽपि चन्द्रमाः ॥
सोमस्य तु बुधः पुत्रो बुधपुत्रः पुरूरवाः ॥ 1 ॥
1.34.m: Ṛcīka said: / 'The gentle son of Brahmā is Atri; his son also is the Moon. / The son of Soma is Budha; Budha's son is Purūravas.

1.34.s:
śrutāyustanayastasya putrastasyāpi nagnajit ..
tasyā'pi kāñcanaḥ putraḥ suhotrastasya cā''tmajaḥ .. 2 ..
1.34.d:
श्रुतायुस्तनयस्तस्य पुत्रस्तस्यापि नग्नजित् ॥
तस्याऽपि काञ्चनः पुत्रः सुहोत्रस्तस्य चा'ऽत्मजः ॥ 2 ॥
1.34.m: Śrutāyus is his son; his son also is Nagnajit. / His son is Kāñcana; and Suhotra is his son.

1.34.s:
tasya jahnuḥ smṛtaḥ śrīmānyena gaṅgā tu jāhnavī ..
suvratastanayastasya cālarkastasya cātmajaḥ .. 3 ..
1.34.d:
तस्य जह्नुः स्मृतः श्रीमान्येन गङ्गा तु जाह्नवी ॥
सुव्रतस्तनयस्तस्य चालर्कस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥ 3 ॥
1.34.m: His [son] is remembered as glorious Jahnu, through whom the Gaṅgā became Jāhnavī. / His son is Suvrata; and Alarka is his son.

1.34.s:
tasya putro balākaśca kuśikastasya cā''tmajaḥ ..
mahodayapuravare sa tu nityaṃ kṛtālayaḥ .. 4 ..
1.34.d:
तस्य पुत्रो बलाकश्च कुशिकस्तस्य चा'ऽत्मजः ॥
महोदयपुरवरे स तु नित्यं कृतालयः ॥ 4 ॥
1.34.m: His son is Balāka, and Kuśika is his son; / he made his permanent residence in the excellent city of Mahodaya.'

1.34.s:
etasminneva kāle tu śvasuraḥ cyavanastava ..
svavaṃśasaṃkaraṃ buddhvā kuśikebhyo mahāyaśāḥ ..5..
1.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु श्वसुरः च्यवनस्तव ॥
स्ववंशसंकरं बुद्ध्वा कुशिकेभ्यो महायशाः ॥5॥
1.34.m:
At that very time, Cyavana, your father-in-law,
having understood the intermixture of his lineage from the Kuśikas, O highly renowned one,

1.34.s:
kuśikānāṃ samucchityai kuśikaṃ nṛpatiṃ yayau ..
pūjitaḥ kuśikenāpi kuśikaṃ vākyamabravīt..6..
1.34.d:
कुशिकानां समुच्छित्यै कुशिकं नृपतिं ययौ ॥
पूजितः कुशिकेनापि कुशिकं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥6॥
1.34.m:
went to King Kuśika in order to exterminate the Kuśikas.
Being honored by Kuśika, he spoke these words to Kuśika:

1.34.s:
rājanvakṣyāmi kāryaṃ te yadi śuśrūṣasenagha ..
sabhāryeṇa ca kartavyaṃ rājañchuśrūṣaṇaṃ tvayā ..7..
1.34.d:
राजन्वक्ष्यामि कार्यं ते यदि शुश्रूषसेनघ ॥
सभार्येण च कर्तव्यं राजञ्छुश्रूषणं त्वया ॥7॥
1.34.m:
"O king, I will tell you what is to be done, if you wish to serve, O sinless one.
And service must be performed by you together with your wife, O king."

1.34.s:
kuśika uvāca ..
svamevedaṃ tava gṛhaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ vasa bhārgava..
śaktitastava śuśrūṣāṃ kariṣye bhāryayā saha..8..
1.34.d:
कुशिक उवाच ॥
स्वमेवेदं तव गृहं यथेष्टं वस भार्गव॥
शक्तितस्तव शुश्रूषां करिष्ये भार्यया सह॥8॥
1.34.m:
Kuśika said:
"This house of yours is indeed your own; dwell here as you please, O Bhārgava.
Together with my wife, I shall perform your service to the best of my ability."

1.34.s:
ṛcīka uvāca..
gṛhoṣitaṃ taṃ cyavanaṃ śuśrūṣuranahaṃkṛtaḥ ..
pūjayāmāsa satataṃ sarvakāmasamṛddhibhiḥ..9..
1.34.d:
ऋचीक उवाच॥
गृहोषितं तं च्यवनं शुश्रूषुरनहंकृतः ॥
पूजयामास सततं सर्वकामसमृद्धिभिः॥9॥
1.34.m:
Ṛcīka said:
Desiring to serve that Cyavana who was residing in his home, free from egotism,
he continuously honored him with an abundance of all desired objects.

1.34.s:
bahusaṃkhyāndinagaṇāṃścyavano nāvabuddhyati ..
nirāhāraḥ sabhāryastaṃ paryupāste mahīpatiḥ .. 1.34.10 ..
1.34.d:
बहुसंख्यान्दिनगणांश्च्यवनो नावबुद्ध्यति ॥
निराहारः सभार्यस्तं पर्युपास्ते महीपतिः ॥ 1.34.10 ॥
1.34.m:
For hosts of days without number, Cyavana did not wake up.
Without food, together with his wife, the ruler of the earth attended upon him.

1.34.s:
akāle prāśayatyannaṃ kadācidapi dularbham ..
kṛtamityeva tadrājā nivedayati satvaram ..11..
1.34.d:
अकाले प्राशयत्यन्नं कदाचिदपि दुलर्भम् ॥
कृतमित्येव तद्राजा निवेदयति सत्वरम् ॥11॥
1.34.m:
At an improper time, he would make him eat food that was at times even hard to obtain;
the king would promptly offer it, saying merely, 'It is prepared.'

1.34.s:
kadācidbahu bhuṅktennaṃ na bhuṅkte divasānbahūn ..
dhanena ca tadīyena tarpayāmāsa vai dvijān .. 12 ..
1.34.d:
कदाचिद्बहु भुङ्क्तेन्नं न भुङ्क्ते दिवसान्बहून् ॥
धनेन च तदीयेन तर्पयामास वै द्विजान् ॥ 12 ॥
1.34.m:
Sometimes he would eat much food, and for many days he would not eat at all;
and with his wealth he satisfied the twice-born.

1.34.s:
kadāciddīpayatyeva vahniṃ tātagṛhodbhavam ..
kadācicca rathe yuktaṃ sabhāryo rājapuṅgavam .. 13 ..
1.34.d:
कदाचिद्दीपयत्येव वह्निं तातगृहोद्भवम् ॥
कदाचिच्च रथे युक्तं सभार्यो राजपुङ्गवम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.34.m:
Sometimes he would even kindle a fire produced in his father's house;
and sometimes he yoked that bull among kings together with his wife to a chariot,

1.34.s:
rājamārge pratodena tudanyati yathecchayā..
tasyā'sau hitamevedaṃ karmaṇā manasā girā .. 14 ..
1.34.d:
राजमार्गे प्रतोदेन तुदन्यति यथेच्छया॥
तस्याऽसौ हितमेवेदं कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ॥ 14 ॥
1.34.m:
and struck him at will with a goad on the royal highway.
Yet the king did only what was beneficial to him in deed, thought, and speech,

1.34.s:
samācarati yatnena bhārgavapriyakāmyayā ..
yadā na vṛjinaṃ kiṃciddṛṣṭavāṃstasya bhārgava .. 15 ..
1.34.d:
समाचरति यत्नेन भार्गवप्रियकाम्यया ॥
यदा न वृजिनं किंचिद्दृष्टवांस्तस्य भार्गव ॥ 15 ॥
1.34.m:
acting with exertion out of a desire to please the Bhārgava.
When the Bhārgava saw no crookedness at all in him,

1.34.s: tadā tasya varaṃ prādādvaraṃ yanmanasepsitam .. 16 ..
1.34.d: तदा तस्य वरं प्रादाद्वरं यन्मनसेप्सितम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.34.m: then he granted him a boon—whatever boon his mind desired.

1.34.s:
cyavana uvāca ..
vara varaya bhadraṃ te prasanno'haṃ tavānagha ..
nirvyājaṃ te'nayā rājassevayā'naghayā sadā .. 17 ..
1.34.d:
च्यवन उवाच ॥
वर वरय भद्रं ते प्रसन्नोऽहं तवानघ ॥
निर्व्याजं तेऽनया राजस्सेवयाऽनघया सदा ॥ 17 ॥
1.34.m:
Cyavana said:
"Choose a boon, may good fortune be yours; I am pleased with you, O sinless one,
at all times by this sincere, faultless service of yours, O king."

1.34.s:
kuśika uvāca ..
yadi me tvaṃ prasanno'si bhṛgūṇāṃ vaṃśavardhana ..
vaṃśo brāhmaṇatāṃ yātu varametadvṛṇomyaham .. 18 ..
1.34.d:
कुशिक उवाच ॥
यदि मे त्वं प्रसन्नोऽसि भृगूणां वंशवर्धन ॥
वंशो ब्राह्मणतां यातु वरमेतद्वृणोम्यहम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.34.m:
Kuśika said:
"If you are pleased with me, O increaser of the lineage of the Bhṛgus,
let my lineage attain brahminhood; this is the boon I choose."

1.34.s:
cyavana uvāca ..
etadeva dhruvaṃ bhāvī nanmāṃ varayase nṛpa ..
asmadvaṃśānuvaṃśasya brāhmaṇyaṃ te bhaviṣyati..19..
1.34.d:
च्यवन उवाच ॥
एतदेव ध्रुवं भावी नन्मां वरयसे नृप ॥
अस्मद्वंशानुवंशस्य ब्राह्मण्यं ते भविष्यति॥19॥

1.34.s:
tava vaṃśakṛto'smākaṃ kṣatradharmmo dvijottamaḥ..
bhaviṣyati narendrendra caitatsuviditaṃ mama .. 1.34.20 ..
1.34.d:
तव वंशकृतोऽस्माकं क्षत्रधर्म्मो द्विजोत्तमः॥
भविष्यति नरेन्द्रेन्द्र चैतत्सुविदितं मम ॥ 1.34.20 ॥
1.34.m:
The foremost of twice-born [born] of our [lineage] will take up the duty of a kṣatriya because of your lineage,
O ruler of kings, and this is well known to me.

1.34.s:
etajjñātvā samutsedhaṃ cikīrṣuḥ svakulasya te ..
vikāraiḥ krodhanārthaṃ te gṛhe'hamavasaṃ ciram .. 21..
1.34.d:
एतज्ज्ञात्वा समुत्सेधं चिकीर्षुः स्वकुलस्य ते ॥
विकारैः क्रोधनार्थं ते गृहेऽहमवसं चिरम् ॥ 21॥
1.34.m:
Knowing this, desiring to bring about the destruction of your family
through provocative behavior to anger you, I lived in your house for a long time.

1.34.s:
vikāraṃ na tato dṛṣṭaṃ mayā bhāvyarthacoditam ..
tasmānmātusvayā prāptaṃ varametatsudurlabham ..22..
1.34.d:
विकारं न ततो दृष्टं मया भाव्यर्थचोदितम् ॥
तस्मान्मातुस्वया प्राप्तं वरमेतत्सुदुर्लभम् ॥22॥
1.34.m:
Yet no agitation was seen in you by me, impelled as you were by what is destined to be;
therefore, by you this boon, so difficult to obtain, has been gained.

1.34.s:
kuśāsyanāmā putrastu bhavitā'ti svadhārmikaḥ ..
tasyāpi bhavitā putro gādhirityeva viśrutaḥ .. 23 ..
1.34.d:
कुशास्यनामा पुत्रस्तु भविताऽति स्वधार्मिकः ॥
तस्यापि भविता पुत्रो गाधिरित्येव विश्रुतः ॥ 23 ॥
1.34.m:
You will have a son named Kuśāśva, who will be exceedingly righteous;
and he too will have a son famous as Gādhi.

1.34.s:
viśvāmitraḥ sutastasya brāhmaṇyamupalapsyati ..
kṛtvā vairaṃ vasiṣṭhena tapasā mahatā nṛpa .. 24 ..
1.34.d:
विश्वामित्रः सुतस्तस्य ब्राह्मण्यमुपलप्स्यति ॥
कृत्वा वैरं वसिष्ठेन तपसा महता नृप ॥ 24 ॥
1.34.m:
His son Viśvāmitra will attain brahminhood,
having made enmity with Vasiṣṭha, through great asceticism, O king.

1.34.s:
strīṇāṃ caruviparyāsādviśvāmitrasya saṃbhavaḥ ..
asmadvaṃśānubhavitā nirvṛtto bhava pārthiva .. 25..
1.34.d:
स्त्रीणां चरुविपर्यासाद्विश्वामित्रस्य संभवः ॥
अस्मद्वंशानुभविता निर्वृत्तो भव पार्थिव ॥ 25॥
1.34.m:
Because of the exchange of sacrificial caru by the women, the birth of Viśvāmitra
will be experienced from our lineage; be at peace, O ruler of the earth.

1.34.s:
yatte vināśitaṃ dagdhaṃ bhavitā tadviśeṣavat ..
bhāryayā sahitaścaiva jarāhīno bhaviṣyasi ..26..
1.34.d:
यत्ते विनाशितं दग्धं भविता तद्विशेषवत् ॥
भार्यया सहितश्चैव जराहीनो भविष्यसि ॥26॥
1.34.m:
Whatever of yours has been destroyed or burnt will become even better;
and together with your wife, you will become free from old age."

1.34.s:
evamuktvā gate vipre rājā pūrṇamanorathaḥ ..
uvāca sumukhīṃ bhadre jarāśoka vivarjitām ..27 ..
1.34.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गते विप्रे राजा पूर्णमनोरथः ॥
उवाच सुमुखीं भद्रे जराशोक विवर्जिताम् ॥27 ॥
1.34.m:
When the brahmin had departed after speaking thus, the king, his desires fulfilled,
spoke to that fair-faced lady, O auspicious one, who was freed from old age and grief:

1.34.s:
etatsunetre cyavasya vākyaṃ kasyā'sti śaktirbhuvi mānavasya ..
kartuṃ mṛṣā tena varorumadhye pautrastavogro bhavitā nṛloke .. .. 28 ..
1.34.d:
एतत्सुनेत्रे च्यवस्य वाक्यं कस्याऽस्ति शक्तिर्भुवि मानवस्य ॥
कर्तुं मृषा तेन वरोरुमध्ये पौत्रस्तवोग्रो भविता नृलोके ॥ ॥ 28 ॥
1.34.m:
"This was the word of Cyavana, O fair-eyed one; what human on earth has the power
to make it false? Therefore, O lady with lovely thighs, your grandson will be fierce in the world of men."

1.35.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktā satyavatī kāle pūrṇe dvijottamam ..
janayāmāsa dharmajñaṃ jamadagniṃ tapodhanam .. 1 ..
1.35.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्ता सत्यवती काले पूर्णे द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
जनयामास धर्मज्ञं जमदग्निं तपोधनम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.35.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed, Satyavatī, when the time was complete,
gave birth to a foremost of the twice-born, Jamadagni, who knew dharma and possessed ascetic wealth.

1.35.s:
tataśca janayāmāsa vātsyaṃ bhṛgukulodvaham ..
tatoṣṭanavatiṃ putrāngotrakārānpṛthakpṛthak .. 2 ..
1.35.d:
ततश्च जनयामास वात्स्यं भृगुकुलोद्वहम् ॥
ततोष्टनवतिं पुत्रान्गोत्रकारान्पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 2 ॥
1.35.m:
And then she gave birth to Vātsya, who exalted the family of the Bhṛgus,
and after that ninety-eight sons, each an originator of a gotra.

1.35.s:
gādherapi tadā bhāryā janayāmāsa putrakam ..
viśvāmitramiti khyātaṃ yutaṃ brāhmaṇatejasā .. 3 ..
1.35.d:
गाधेरपि तदा भार्या जनयामास पुत्रकम् ॥
विश्वामित्रमिति ख्यातं युतं ब्राह्मणतेजसा ॥ 3 ॥
1.35.m:
Then the wife of Gādhi also gave birth to a son
famous as Viśvāmitra, endowed with the splendor of a brahmin.

1.35.s:
jito yuddhe vasiṣṭhena manyunā yaḥ sa pārthivaḥ ..
brāhmaṇyaṃ tapasā lebhe dharmātmā saṃśitavrataḥ ..4..
1.35.d:
जितो युद्धे वसिष्ठेन मन्युना यः स पार्थिवः ॥
ब्राह्मण्यं तपसा लेभे धर्मात्मा संशितव्रतः ॥4॥
1.35.m:
That righteous king of firm vows, defeated in battle by Vasiṣṭha,
attained brahminhood through asceticism out of indignation.

1.35.s:
rājā prasenajinnāma sutāṃ tasyā'tha reṇukām ..
patnyarthe pratijagrāha jamadagnirmahātapāḥ .. 5 ..
1.35.d:
राजा प्रसेनजिन्नाम सुतां तस्याऽथ रेणुकाम् ॥
पत्न्यर्थे प्रतिजग्राह जमदग्निर्महातपाः ॥ 5 ॥
1.35.m:
There was a king named Prasenajit; his daughter, Reṇukā,
Jamadagni of great austerities accepted as his wife.

1.35.s:
sā taṃ vanagataṃ bhaktyā nityaṃ paryacaradvane ..
kadācidatha gharmartau madhyaṃ prāpte divākare .. .. 6 ..
1.35.d:
सा तं वनगतं भक्त्या नित्यं पर्यचरद्वने ॥
कदाचिदथ घर्मर्तौ मध्यं प्राप्ते दिवाकरे ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
1.35.m:
With devotion she constantly attended upon him when he went into the forest.
Then once, in the hot season, when the sun had reached the meridian,

1.35.s:
krīḍārthaṃ prāsyati ciraṃ jamadagnirmahātapāḥ ..
kṣiptāḥkṣiptāḥ śarāstena reṇukā cārulocanā ..7 ..
1.35.d:
क्रीडार्थं प्रास्यति चिरं जमदग्निर्महातपाः ॥
क्षिप्ताःक्षिप्ताः शरास्तेन रेणुका चारुलोचना ॥7 ॥
1.35.m:
Jamadagni of great austerities shot arrows for a long time in play;
and as the arrows were shot one by one by him, the lovely-eyed Reṇukā,

1.35.s:
ānayāmāsa dharmajñā bharturvacanakāriṇī ..
athā'rkatāpasaṃtaptā dahyamānāṃghripaṅkajā .. 8 ..
1.35.d:
आनयामास धर्मज्ञा भर्तुर्वचनकारिणी ॥
अथाऽर्कतापसंतप्ता दह्यमानांघ्रिपङ्कजा ॥ 8 ॥
1.35.m:
knowing dharma and doing the bidding of her husband, brought them back.
Then, scorched by the heat of the sun, her lotus-feet burning,

1.35.s:
puṣpitasya ca vṛkṣasya chāyāmāsādya viṣṭhitā ..
viśramya tu muhūrtaṃ sā bharturninye śarottamam ..9..
1.35.d:
पुष्पितस्य च वृक्षस्य छायामासाद्य विष्ठिता ॥
विश्रम्य तु मुहूर्तं सा भर्तुर्निन्ये शरोत्तमम् ॥9॥
1.35.m:
having reached the shade of a flowering tree, she stood still;
and resting for a moment, she brought the excellent arrow to her husband.

1.35.s:
tāṃ prāptāṃ kupito bhartā jamadagnirabhāṣata ..
krīḍato me śarairbhadre vighnaṃ kiṃ kṛtavatyasi ..1 0..
1.35.d:
तां प्राप्तां कुपितो भर्ता जमदग्निरभाषत ॥
क्रीडतो मे शरैर्भद्रे विघ्नं किं कृतवत्यसि ॥1 0॥
1.35.m:
When she arrived, her husband Jamadagni, enraged, said:
"Why have you caused an obstacle to me while I was playing with arrows, O auspicious one?

1.35.s: na bibheṣi ca māṃ bhadre tvatha vāpyavamanyase .. 11 ..
1.35.d: न बिभेषि च मां भद्रे त्वथ वाप्यवमन्यसे ॥ 11 ॥
1.35.m: Do you not fear me, O auspicious one, or do you despise me?"

1.35.s:
reṇukovāca ..
arkāgnitāpasaṃtaptā kṣaṇamātraṃ mahāvrata ..
apārayaṃtī viśrānto tasmāttvaṃ kṣantumarhasi .. 12 ..
1.35.d:
रेणुकोवाच ॥
अर्काग्नितापसंतप्ता क्षणमात्रं महाव्रत ॥
अपारयंती विश्रान्तो तस्मात्त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि ॥ 12 ॥
1.35.m:
Reṇukā said:
"Tormented by the heat of the fire of the sun, O you of great vows,
I, being unable [to proceed], rested for just a moment; therefore you ought to forgive me."

1.35.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
reṇukāyā vacaḥ śrutvā jamadagnirmahātapāḥ ..
jātaroṣastadā sūrye sāyakānkṣeptumudyataḥ .. 13 ..
1.35.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
रेणुकाया वचः श्रुत्वा जमदग्निर्महातपाः ॥
जातरोषस्तदा सूर्ये सायकान्क्षेप्तुमुद्यतः ॥ 13 ॥
1.35.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Hearing the words of Reṇukā, Jamadagni of great austerities,
having become enraged, was then prepared to shoot arrows at the sun.

1.35.s:
etasminneva kāle tu viprarūpo divākaraḥ ..
śīghramāgamya tejasvī jamadagnimabhāṣata .. 14 ..
1.35.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु विप्ररूपो दिवाकरः ॥
शीघ्रमागम्य तेजस्वी जमदग्निमभाषत ॥ 14 ॥
1.35.m:
At that very time, the radiant sun, assuming the form of a brahmin,
came quickly and spoke to Jamadagni.

1.35.s:
sūrya uvāca .. ..
svabhāva eṣa me brahman yadahaṃ dahanātmakaḥ ..
vartataśca svabhāvena na me tvaṃ kroddhumarhasi .. 15 ..
1.35.d:
सूर्य उवाच ॥ ॥
स्वभाव एष मे ब्रह्मन् यदहं दहनात्मकः ॥
वर्ततश्च स्वभावेन न मे त्वं क्रोद्धुमर्हसि ॥ 15 ॥

1.35.s:
putraste'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi tvasyāmeva dvijottama ..
surakāryaṃ kariṣyāmi lokānāñca hitaṃ mahat .. 16 ..
1.35.d:
पुत्रस्तेऽहं भविष्यामि त्वस्यामेव द्विजोत्तम ॥
सुरकार्यं करिष्यामि लोकानाञ्च हितं महत् ॥ 16 ॥
1.35.m:
I shall become your son through this very woman, O foremost of the twice-born;
I will accomplish the purpose of the gods and great welfare for the worlds.

1.35.s:
iyañca patnī dharmajñā reṇukā tava sāṃpratam ..
chatropānahametanme gṛhṇātu varavarṇinī .. 17 ..
1.35.d:
इयञ्च पत्नी धर्मज्ञा रेणुका तव सांप्रतम् ॥
छत्रोपानहमेतन्मे गृह्णातु वरवर्णिनी ॥ 17 ॥
1.35.m:
And now, this righteous wife of yours, Reṇukā,
let this fair-complexioned lady receive an umbrella and sandals from me.

1.35.s:
tasyā'nukampayā chatraṃ tathā brahmanmupānahau ..
mayā sṛṣṭau jagatyasminnityameva bhaviṣyataḥ .. 18 ..
1.35.d:
तस्याऽनुकम्पया छत्रं तथा ब्रह्मन्मुपानहौ ॥
मया सृष्टौ जगत्यस्मिन्नित्यमेव भविष्यतः ॥ 18 ॥
1.35.m:
Out of compassion for her, an umbrella and sandals, O brahmin,
have been created by me; they shall exist perpetually in this world.

1.35.s:
chatropānahayordānaṃ loke śreṣṭhaṃ bhaviṣyati..
chatropānahadānena naraḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyati .. 19 ..
1.35.d:
छत्रोपानहयोर्दानं लोके श्रेष्ठं भविष्यति॥
छत्रोपानहदानेन नरः स्वर्गं गमिष्यति ॥ 19 ॥
1.35.m:
The gift of an umbrella and sandals will be the highest in the world;
by the gift of an umbrella and sandals, a person will go to heaven."

1.35.s:
evamuktastu sūryeṇa jamadagnirmahātapāḥ ..
saṃpūjya sūryaṃ jagrāha savituḥ sakalaṃ vacaḥ .. 20 ..
1.35.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु सूर्येण जमदग्निर्महातपाः ॥
संपूज्य सूर्यं जग्राह सवितुः सकलं वचः ॥ 20 ॥
1.35.m: Addressed thus by the sun, Jamadagni of great austerities / worshipped the sun and accepted all the words of Savitṛ.

1.35.s:
tataḥ sūrye gate devī sūryaputrā purā satī ..
putraṃ kanīyasaṃ rāmaṃ janayāmāsa reṇukā ..
tamanvāvasuṣeṇaśca vasurviśvāvasustathā .. 21 ..
1.35.d:
ततः सूर्ये गते देवी सूर्यपुत्रा पुरा सती ॥
पुत्रं कनीयसं रामं जनयामास रेणुका ॥
तमन्वावसुषेणश्च वसुर्विश्वावसुस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.35.m: Then, after the sun had departed, the noble lady Reṇukā, the daughter of the sun, / gave birth of old to a younger son, Rāma. / Following him were Vasuṣeṇa, Vasu, and Viśvāvasu.

1.35.s: teṣāṃ jaghanyajo rāmo viṣṇurmānuṣarūpadhṛk .. 22 ..
1.35.d: तेषां जघन्यजो रामो विष्णुर्मानुषरूपधृक् ॥ 22 ॥
1.35.m: The youngest of them was Rāma, Viṣṇu wearing a human form.

1.35.s:
aṃśena jāte bhuvi devadeve sunirvṛtā bhūmiratho babhūva ..
hṛtāñca mene ditijaprajātāṃ pīḍāṃ nṛṇāṃ svasya ca sā dharitrī .. 23 ..
1.35.d:
अंशेन जाते भुवि देवदेवे सुनिर्वृता भूमिरथो बभूव ॥
हृताञ्च मेने दितिजप्रजातां पीडां नृणां स्वस्य च सा धरित्री ॥ 23 ॥
1.35.m: When the god of gods was born on earth by a portion of himself, the earth became deeply content; / and that earth considered the distress of men and of herself, born from the sons of Diti, to have been removed.

1.36.s:
mārkaṃḍeya uvāca .. ..
atha bālyaṃ samuttīrṇo rāmo bhṛgukulodvahaḥ ..
śuśrūṣamāṇaḥ pitaraṃ nityamāste mahāyaśāḥ .. 1 ..
1.36.d:
मार्कंडेय उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ बाल्यं समुत्तीर्णो रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः ॥
शुश्रूषमाणः पितरं नित्यमास्ते महायशाः ॥ 1 ॥
1.36.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now, having passed beyond childhood, Rāma, the uplifter of the family of Bhṛgu, / of great renown, continually remained serving his father.

1.36.s:
etasminneva kāle tu rāme vanagate tadā ..
ājagāma mahātejā rājā citrāṅgado vanam .. 2 ..
1.36.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रामे वनगते तदा ॥
आजगाम महातेजा राजा चित्राङ्गदो वनम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.36.m: At that very time, while Rāma had gone to the forest, / King Citrāṅgada of great majesty came to the forest,

1.36.s:
vihartuṃ saha rāmābhirdevarājasamadyutiḥ ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā reṇukā cakre spṛhāṃ bhogeṣu bhāminī .. 3 ..
1.36.d:
विहर्तुं सह रामाभिर्देवराजसमद्युतिः ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा रेणुका चक्रे स्पृहां भोगेषु भामिनी ॥ 3 ॥
1.36.m: To sport with lovely women, having a splendor equal to the king of the gods. / Seeing him, the passionate Reṇukā felt desire for [worldly] pleasures.

1.36.s:
jagāma manasā taṃ sā rājānaṃ kāmasannibham ..
tasminneva kṣaṇe sā tu bhraṣṭā brāhmaṇatejasā .. 4 ..
1.36.d:
जगाम मनसा तं सा राजानं कामसन्निभम् ॥
तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे सा तु भ्रष्टा ब्राह्मणतेजसा ॥ 4 ॥
1.36.m: In her mind she went to that king, who resembled the god of love. / At that very moment, she fell [from grace], stripped of her brahminical luster.

1.36.s:
gataśriyaṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā jamadagnirmahātapāḥ ..
putrānuvāca tānkrodhāddhanyatāṃ jananīṃ svakāṃ .. 5 ..
1.36.d:
गतश्रियं तु तां दृष्ट्वा जमदग्निर्महातपाः ॥
पुत्रानुवाच तान्क्रोधाद्धन्यतां जननीं स्वकां ॥ 5 ॥
1.36.m: Seeing her deprived of her splendor, Jamadagni of great austerities / spoke to his sons in anger: 'Let your mother be slain!'

1.36.s:
te vicārya tataḥ sarve māturgauravamuttamam ..
naiva cakruḥ piturvākyaṃ tāñchaśāpa sa bhārgavaḥ .. 6 ..
1.36.d:
ते विचार्य ततः सर्वे मातुर्गौरवमुत्तमम् ॥
नैव चक्रुः पितुर्वाक्यं ताञ्छशाप स भार्गवः ॥ 6 ॥
1.36.m: Then, having considered the supreme dignity of a mother, they all / did not carry out their father's command; so that Bhārgava cursed them:

1.36.s:
yūyaṃ tiryaksadharmāṇo naṣṭasaṃjñā bhaviṣyatha ..
idhmabhāramupādāya rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ .. .. 7 ..
1.36.d:
यूयं तिर्यक्सधर्माणो नष्टसंज्ञा भविष्यथ ॥
इध्मभारमुपादाय रामो रतिकरः पितुः ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
1.36.m: 'You shall share the nature of beasts, devoid of consciousness!' / Then Rāma, bringing a load of firewood, who gave delight to his father,

1.36.s:
athā''śramamanuprāptaḥ pitā taṃ samacodayat ..
jahīmāṃ mātaraṃ kṣudrāṃ rāma mā tvaṃ ciraṃ kṛthāḥ .. 8 ..
1.36.d:
अथा'ऽश्रममनुप्राप्तः पिता तं समचोदयत् ॥
जहीमां मातरं क्षुद्रां राम मा त्वं चिरं कृथाः ॥ 8 ॥
1.36.m: Arrived at the hermitage. His father urged him: / 'Kill this vile mother, Rāma; do not delay!'

1.36.s:
evamuktaḥ sa pitrā tu tadvākya samanantaram ..
śiraściccheda tīkṣṇena rāmaḥ paraśunā tadā .. 9 ..
1.36.d:
एवमुक्तः स पित्रा तु तद्वाक्य समनन्तरम् ॥
शिरश्चिच्छेद तीक्ष्णेन रामः परशुना तदा ॥ 9 ॥
1.36.m: Addressed thus by his father, immediately upon his words, / Rāma then cut off her head with his sharp axe.

1.36.s: tutoṣātha pitā tasya tato dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .. . 10 ..
1.36.d: तुतोषाथ पिता तस्य ततो धर्मभृतां वरः ॥ । 10 ॥
1.36.m: Then his father, the best among upholders of dharma, was pleased.

1.36.s:
jamadagniruvāca ..
svacchandamaraṇaṃ putra tuṣṭe tvaṃ mayi lapsyase ..
yāvacca vaiṣṇavaṃ tejastvayi tiṣṭhati putraka..11..
1.36.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच ॥
स्वच्छन्दमरणं पुत्र तुष्टे त्वं मयि लप्स्यसे ॥
यावच्च वैष्णवं तेजस्त्वयि तिष्ठति पुत्रक॥11॥
1.36.m: Jamadagni said: / 'Son, since I am pleased, you shall obtain death at will, / and as long as the Vaiṣṇava luster remains in you, my child,

1.36.s:
tāvadaiva na te yuddhe kaścijjetā bhaviṣyati..
bhaviṣyati ca dharmātmā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ ..
raghuvaṃśe samutpanno viṣṇurmānuṣarūpadhṛk .. 12 ..
1.36.d:
तावदैव न ते युद्धे कश्चिज्जेता भविष्यति॥
भविष्यति च धर्मात्मा रामो दशरथात्मजः ॥
रघुवंशे समुत्पन्नो विष्णुर्मानुषरूपधृक् ॥ 12 ॥
1.36.m: For that long indeed no one shall be your conqueror in battle. / And there will be the righteous Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, / born in the lineage of Raghu, Viṣṇu wearing a human form.

1.36.s:
yadā sameṣyate tena tadā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
kṛtakarmā vimuktastvaṃ sa ca yukto bhaviṣyati .. 13 ..
1.36.d:
यदा समेष्यते तेन तदा वैष्णवतेजसा ॥
कृतकर्मा विमुक्तस्त्वं स च युक्तो भविष्यति ॥ 13 ॥
1.36.m: When he joins with that Vaiṣṇava luster, / then you, your deed accomplished, will be freed [from it], and he will be endowed [with it].

1.36.s:
tataḥ paraṃ tvayā putra na kāryaṃ śastradhāraṇam ..
ārtatrāṇamṛte vīra strībrāhmaṇakṛte'tha vā ..
yathepsitaṃ cā'pyaparaṃ varaṃ varaya putraka .. 14 ..
1.36.d:
ततः परं त्वया पुत्र न कार्यं शस्त्रधारणम् ॥
आर्तत्राणमृते वीर स्त्रीब्राह्मणकृतेऽथ वा ॥
यथेप्सितं चाऽप्यपरं वरं वरय पुत्रक ॥ 14 ॥
1.36.m: After that, my son, you must not bear arms, / except for the protection of the distressed, O hero, or for the sake of women and brahmins. / Choose also another boon according to your desire, my child.'

1.36.s:
rāma uvāca ..
guruśreṣṭha samutthānaṃ jananyāḥ kathayāmyaham ..
asmṛtiñca tathā tasyāṃ bhrātṝṇāñca tathā 'smṛtim ..15..
1.36.d:
राम उवाच ॥
गुरुश्रेष्ठ समुत्थानं जनन्याः कथयाम्यहम् ॥
अस्मृतिञ्च तथा तस्यां भ्रातॄणाञ्च तथा ऽस्मृतिम् ॥15॥
1.36.m: Rāma said: / 'O best of elders, I ask for the resurrection of my mother / and also her lack of memory [of the event], and likewise the lack of memory of my brothers.'

1.36.s:
jamadagniruvāca ..
evamastu mahābhāga tapasā mahatā tathā ..
samārādhaya deveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ nīlalohitam..16 ..
1.36.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच ॥
एवमस्तु महाभाग तपसा महता तथा ॥
समाराधय देवेशं शङ्करं नीललोहितम्॥16 ॥
1.36.m: Jamadagni said: / 'So be it, O fortunate one! And likewise, by great austerity, / worship the lord of gods, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita.'

1.36.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamukte samuttasthau reṇukā cāruhāsinī ..
rāmasya bhrātaraḥ sarve muktaśāpāstathaiva te ..17..
1.36.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्ते समुत्तस्थौ रेणुका चारुहासिनी ॥
रामस्य भ्रातरः सर्वे मुक्तशापास्तथैव ते ॥17॥
1.36.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When this was spoken, Reṇukā of lovely smile stood up, / and all the brothers of Rāma were likewise freed from the curse.

1.36.s:
pitrā rāmastathoktastu himavatyacalottame ..
tapastepe mahātejā rudrārādhanakāmyayā .. 18 ..
1.36.d:
पित्रा रामस्तथोक्तस्तु हिमवत्यचलोत्तमे ॥
तपस्तेपे महातेजा रुद्राराधनकाम्यया ॥ 18 ॥
1.36.m: Addressed thus by his father, Rāma of great majesty / practiced austerity on the Himavat, the best of mountains, desiring to propitiate Rudra.

1.36.s:
etasminneva kāle tu devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ ..
saiṃhikeyabhayatrastāḥ śaṅkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 19 ..
1.36.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवाः सेन्द्रपुरोगमाः ॥
सैंहिकेयभयत्रस्ताः शङ्करं शरणं गताः ॥ 19 ॥
1.36.m: At that very time, the gods, led by Indra, / terrified by fear of the Saiṃhikeyas, went to Śaṅkara for refuge.

1.36.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
bhagavan devadeveśa praṇatārtivināśana ..
saiṃhikeyairvayaṃ sarvaiḥ sthānebhyastvavaropitāḥ .. 20 ..
1.36.d:
॥ देवा ऊचुः ॥ ॥
भगवन् देवदेवेश प्रणतार्तिविनाशन ॥
सैंहिकेयैर्वयं सर्वैः स्थानेभ्यस्त्ववरोपिताः ॥ 20 ॥
1.36.m: The gods said: / 'O Lord, lord of the gods of gods, destroyer of the distress of those who bow [to you], / we have all been driven from our places by the Saiṃhikeyas.

1.36.s:
saiṃhikeyānathā''śritya daityāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ ..
sarve vasanti satataṃ teṣāṃ yatnaṃ vadhe kuru .. 21 ..
1.36.d:
सैंहिकेयानथा'ऽश्रित्य दैत्याः शतसहस्रशः ॥
सर्वे वसन्ति सततं तेषां यत्नं वधे कुरु ॥ 21 ॥
1.36.m: Depending upon the Saiṃhikeyas, daityas by hundreds of thousands / dwell constantly; make an effort for their destruction!'

1.36.s:
.. mahādeva uvāca .. ..
śṛṇvantu devatāḥ sarvā dānavā devakaṇṭakāḥ ..
rāmeṇā''haṃ vadhiṣyāmi narabuddhyā yatastu tān .. 22 ..
1.36.d:
॥ महादेव उवाच ॥ ॥
शृण्वन्तु देवताः सर्वा दानवा देवकण्टकाः ॥
रामेणा'ऽहं वधिष्यामि नरबुद्ध्या यतस्तु तान् ॥ 22 ॥
1.36.m: Mahādeva said: / 'Let all the deities listen: since the dānavas are a thorn to the gods, / I shall slay them by means of Rāma, through [their] regarding him as a mere man.'

1.36.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
gateṣu devasaṃgheṣu devadevaḥ pinākabhṛt ..
āhūya bhārgavaṃ rāmamidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 23 ..
1.36.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
गतेषु देवसंघेषु देवदेवः पिनाकभृत् ॥
आहूय भार्गवं राममिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 23 ॥
1.36.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the hosts of gods had departed, the god of gods who bears the Pināka, / having summoned the Bhārgava Rāma, spoke these words:

1.36.s:
mahādeva uvāca ..
saiṃhikeyāndurācārānasurāñjahi putraka ..
samarthastānbhavānhantuṃ nā'nyaḥ kaścana vidyate .. 24 ..
1.36.d:
महादेव उवाच ॥
सैंहिकेयान्दुराचारानसुराञ्जहि पुत्रक ॥
समर्थस्तान्भवान्हन्तुं नाऽन्यः कश्चन विद्यते ॥ 24 ॥
1.36.m: Mahādeva said: / 'Slay the wicked asuras, the Saiṃhikeyas, my child! / You are capable of slaying them; no other exists.'

1.36.s:
rāma uvāca ..
astragrāmaṃ samagraṃ me prayaccha bhagasūdana ..
yena tānsudurācārānghātayiṣyāmi dānavān .. 25 ..
1.36.d:
राम उवाच ॥
अस्त्रग्रामं समग्रं मे प्रयच्छ भगसूदन ॥
येन तान्सुदुराचारान्घातयिष्यामि दानवान् ॥ 25 ॥
1.36.m: Rāma said: / 'Grant me the entire collection of supernatural weapons, O destroyer of Bhaga, / by which I shall cause those utterly wicked dānavas to be slain.'

1.36.s:
mahādeva uvāca ..
kiṃ tavāstrairbhūguśreṣṭha viṣṇustvaṃ nāsi mānuṣaḥ ..
vyastrasyā'pi na te śaktā yoddhuṃ pramukhatastava ..26..
1.36.d:
महादेव उवाच ॥
किं तवास्त्रैर्भूगुश्रेष्ठ विष्णुस्त्वं नासि मानुषः ॥
व्यस्त्रस्याऽपि न ते शक्ता योद्धुं प्रमुखतस्तव ॥26॥
1.36.m: Mahādeva said: / 'What need have you of weapons, O best of the Bhṛgus? You are Viṣṇu, you are not a mortal! / Even if you are weaponless, they are not able to fight facing you.'

1.36.s:
rāma uvāca ..
ghātayiṣyāmyahaṃ sarvānsaiṃhikeyāndurāsadān ..
tripurāre mahābhāga tvadājñāparibṛṃhitaḥ .. 27 ..
1.36.d:
राम उवाच ॥
घातयिष्याम्यहं सर्वान्सैंहिकेयान्दुरासदान् ॥
त्रिपुरारे महाभाग त्वदाज्ञापरिबृंहितः ॥ 27 ॥
1.36.m: Rāma said: / 'I shall slay all the unassailable Saiṃhikeyas, / O enemy of Tripura, O fortunate one, strengthened by your command.'

1.36.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktastripurāntakena rāmastrinetrapratima prabhāvaḥ ..
ādāya tīkṣṇaṃ paraśuṃ jagāma yatra sthitāste ca ripupradhānāḥ .. 28 ..
1.36.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्तस्त्रिपुरान्तकेन रामस्त्रिनेत्रप्रतिम प्रभावः ॥
आदाय तीक्ष्णं परशुं जगाम यत्र स्थितास्ते च रिपुप्रधानाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.36.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Spoken to in this way by the destroyer of Tripura, Rāma, whose power equaled that of the Three-Eyed One, / took his sharp axe and went where those chief enemies were staying.

1.37.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
etasminneva kāle tu kāṣṭhodarkāḥ sudāruṇāḥ ..
babhūvuḥ sumahotpātāḥ saiṃhikeyaniveśane .. 1 ..
1.37.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु काष्ठोदर्काः सुदारुणाः ॥
बभूवुः सुमहोत्पाताः सैंहिकेयनिवेशने ॥ 1 ॥
1.37.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / At that very time, exceedingly dreadful portents, / bearing consequences up to the ends of the quarters, arose in the dwelling of the Saiṃhikeyas.

1.37.s:
cacāla śabdaṃ kurvāṇā mahī savanakānanā ..
papāta mahatī colkā madhyenā''dityamaṇḍalāt .. 2 ..
1.37.d:
चचाल शब्दं कुर्वाणा मही सवनकानना ॥
पपात महती चोल्का मध्येना'ऽदित्यमण्डलात् ॥ 2 ॥
1.37.m: The earth with its groves and forests shook, making a sound; / and a great meteor fell right through the orb of the sun.

1.37.s:
aparvaṇi śaśāṅkārkau saṃchannau tamasā tathā ..
pravṛṣṭāśca tathā raktaṃ bhūri meghā bhayāvaham .. 3 ..
1.37.d:
अपर्वणि शशाङ्कार्कौ संछन्नौ तमसा तथा ॥
प्रवृष्टाश्च तथा रक्तं भूरि मेघा भयावहम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.37.m: Out of season, the moon and the sun were covered with darkness, / and clouds rained down abundant, fearsome blood.
Weapons repeatedly emitted smoke, as did horses with tears [in their eyes]. / The sun was surrounded at both twilights by a halo

1.37.s:
pariviṣṭa ubhe sandhye candraśca sakalāṃ niśam ..
saiṃhikeyo vipatnyopi sālvasya sumahātmanaḥ .. 5 ..
1.37.d:
परिविष्ट उभे सन्ध्ये चन्द्रश्च सकलां निशम् ॥
सैंहिकेयो विपत्न्योपि साल्वस्य सुमहात्मनः ॥ 5 ॥
1.37.m: Having the color of a rainbow, and the moon for the entire night. / The great planet Ketu, hostile to the wives of the Saiṃhikeyas,

1.37.s:
ākramyajanmana kṣatraṃ ketustasthau mahāgrahaḥ ..
vavustīkṣṇā mahāvātāḥ kṣobhayanto diśo daśa .. 6 ..
1.37.d:
आक्रम्यजन्मन क्षत्रं केतुस्तस्थौ महाग्रहः ॥
ववुस्तीक्ष्णा महावाताः क्षोभयन्तो दिशो दश ॥ 6 ॥
1.37.m: Stationed itself, assailing the birth-star of the high-souled Sālva. / Fierce, great winds blew, agitating the ten directions.

1.37.s:
bhānuścā''sītkabandhāṅgo mṛgāścāsannasasvanāḥ ..
nyalīyanta dhvajāgreṣu dānavānāṃ durātmanām ..7..
1.37.d:
भानुश्चा'ऽसीत्कबन्धाङ्गो मृगाश्चासन्नसस्वनाः ॥
न्यलीयन्त ध्वजाग्रेषु दानवानां दुरात्मनाम् ॥7॥
1.37.m: The sun became headless-bodied, and beasts cried out with unmelodious sounds. / [Birds of ill omen] settled on the banner-tips of the evil-minded dānavas.

1.37.s:
kravyādapakṣisaṃghātā hyapasavyaṃ bhayānakāḥ ..
śuṣkendhanasamṛddho'pi na jajvāla hutāśanaḥ ..8..
1.37.d:
क्रव्यादपक्षिसंघाता ह्यपसव्यं भयानकाः ॥
शुष्केन्धनसमृद्धोऽपि न जज्वाल हुताशनः ॥8॥
1.37.m: Flocks of carnivorous birds, truly terrifying, flew toward the left, / and fire did not burn even when supplied with dry fuel.

1.37.s:
vapūṃṣi dānavendrāṇāṃ na prākāśaṃta yādava ..
uṣṇaśītaviparyāsa ṛtūnāmapyadṛśyata .. 9 ..
1.37.d:
वपूंषि दानवेन्द्राणां न प्राकाशंत यादव ॥
उष्णशीतविपर्यास ऋतूनामप्यदृश्यत ॥ 9 ॥
1.37.m: The bodies of the lords of the dānavas lost their radiance, O Yādava, / and an inversion of heat and cold was seen in the seasons.

1.37.s:
prasusravurdrumā raktaṃ vyaśīryanta ca bhūṣaṇāḥ ..
kharā goṣu vyajāyanta mārjārā mūṣikāsu ca .. 10 ..
1.37.d:
प्रसुस्रवुर्द्रुमा रक्तं व्यशीर्यन्त च भूषणाः ॥
खरा गोषु व्यजायन्त मार्जारा मूषिकासु च ॥ 10 ॥
1.37.m: Trees oozed blood, ornaments shattered, / donkeys were born from cows, and cats from mice.

1.37.s:
akāle puṣpitā vṛkṣā akāle phalitā drumāḥ ..
vinā varṣaṃ mahānadyaḥ pratīpaṃ jagmurojasā .. 11 ..
1.37.d:
अकाले पुष्पिता वृक्षा अकाले फलिता द्रुमाः ॥
विना वर्षं महानद्यः प्रतीपं जग्मुरोजसा ॥ 11 ॥
1.37.m: Trees blossomed out of season, and trees bore fruit out of season; / without rain, the great rivers flowed backwards with force.

1.37.s:
bhayānakāñjātabhayaḥ sughorānutpātasaṃghānprasamīkṣya rājā ..
sālvaḥ samāhūya bhṛgostastanūjaṃ daityaiḥ sameto'tha cakāra mantram .. 12 ..
1.37.d:
भयानकाञ्जातभयः सुघोरानुत्पातसंघान्प्रसमीक्ष्य राजा ॥
साल्वः समाहूय भृगोस्तस्तनूजं दैत्यैः समेतोऽथ चकार मन्त्रम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.37.m: Terrified on beholding these dreadful and most frightful hosts of omens, / King Sālva summoned the son of Bhṛgu and, together with the daityas, took counsel.

1.38.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
ratnacitrāṃ suvipulāṃ samāsādya sabhāṃ tadā ..
siṃhikātanayaḥ sālvaḥ śukraṃ vacanamabravīt .. 1 ..
1.38.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
रत्नचित्रां सुविपुलां समासाद्य सभां तदा ॥
सिंहिकातनयः साल्वः शुक्रं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.38.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having then entered the very vast assembly hall adorned with gems, / Sālva, the son of Siṃhikā, spoke these words to Śukra.

1.38.s:
sālva uvāca ..
dṛśyanta ete bhagavannutpātā ghoradarśanāḥ ..
ācakṣāṇā mahāyuddhaṃ vināśamapi dāruṇam .. 2 ..
1.38.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
दृश्यन्त एते भगवन्नुत्पाता घोरदर्शनाः ॥
आचक्षाणा महायुद्धं विनाशमपि दारुणम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.38.m: Sālva said: / 'O venerable one, these portents of terrible appearance are seen, / foretelling a great war and also terrible destruction.

1.38.s:
ripuṃ na caiva paśyāmo yena yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati ..
sarvajñatvādbhavānvetti tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām .. 3 ..
1.38.d:
रिपुं न चैव पश्यामो येन युद्धं भविष्यति ॥
सर्वज्ञत्वाद्भवान्वेत्ति तन्नः प्रब्रूहि पृच्छताम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.38.m: Yet we do not see an enemy with whom there will be war. / Because you are omniscient, you know it; tell that to us who are asking.'

1.38.s:
śukra uvāca ..
ārādhya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ tapasā siṃhikā purā ..
tridaśebhyo hyavadhyatvaṃ svasutānāmalabdha sā .. 4 ..
1.38.d:
शुक्र उवाच ॥
आराध्य देवं ब्रह्माणं तपसा सिंहिका पुरा ॥
त्रिदशेभ्यो ह्यवध्यत्वं स्वसुतानामलब्ध सा ॥ 4 ॥
1.38.m: Śukra said: / 'Formerly, having propitiated the god Brahmā with austerities, / Siṃhikā obtained invulnerability from the gods for her sons.

1.38.s:
varadānakṛtotsāhairbhavadbhirvidyayā mama ..
nirjitāstridaśāḥ sarve śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 5 ..
1.38.d:
वरदानकृतोत्साहैर्भवद्भिर्विद्यया मम ॥
निर्जितास्त्रिदशाः सर्वे शंकरं शरणं गताः ॥ 5 ॥
1.38.m: Filled with energy by the granting of that boon and through my knowledge, / all the gods were conquered by you and went to Śaṃkara for refuge.

1.38.s:
tena yuṣmadvadhārthāya viṣṇurmānuṣarūpadhṛk ..
jamadagnisuto rāmaḥ preṣito raṇakarkaśaḥ .. 6 ..
1.38.d:
तेन युष्मद्वधार्थाय विष्णुर्मानुषरूपधृक् ॥
जमदग्निसुतो रामः प्रेषितो रणकर्कशः ॥ 6 ॥
1.38.m: For the purpose of slaying you, he has sent Viṣṇu, who has assumed human form: / Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, fierce in battle.

1.38.s:
sadā devo mahātejā mānuṣaṃ sa tu sāmpratam ..
manuṣyācca bhayaṃ ghoraṃ yuddhyasvā'surasattama .. 7 ..
1.38.d:
सदा देवो महातेजा मानुषं स तु साम्प्रतम् ॥
मनुष्याच्च भयं घोरं युद्ध्यस्वाऽसुरसत्तम ॥ 7 ॥
1.38.m: Always a god of great splendour, he is now a human being; / and terrible fear [comes] from a mortal! Fight, O best of asuras!'

1.38.s:
sālva uvāca ..
bhagavansarvadevānāmīśvaro madhusūdanaḥ ..
tasmātparataraṃ devaṃ nā'nyaṃ kañcana śuśruma .. 8 ..
1.38.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
भगवन्सर्वदेवानामीश्वरो मधुसूदनः ॥
तस्मात्परतरं देवं नाऽन्यं कञ्चन शुश्रुम ॥ 8 ॥
1.38.m: Sālva said: / 'O venerable one, Madhusūdana is the lord of all the gods; / we have heard of no other god higher than him.

1.38.s:
kimarthaṃ sa mahātejāḥ śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ ..
ājñākārī bhṛguśreṣṭha saiṃhikeyaṃ jighāṃsati ..9..
1.38.d:
किमर्थं स महातेजाः शंकरस्य महात्मनः ॥
आज्ञाकारी भृगुश्रेष्ठ सैंहिकेयं जिघांसति ॥9॥
1.38.m: Why would that one of great splendour, carrying out the command / of the great-souled Śaṃkara, wish to slay the son of Siṃhikā, O best of the Bhṛgus?'

1.38.s:
śukra uvāca ..
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati dānava ..
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadā''tmānaṃ sṛjatyasau ..10..
1.38.d:
शुक्र उवाच ॥
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति दानव ॥
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदा'ऽत्मानं सृजत्यसौ ॥10॥
1.38.m: Śukra said: / 'Whenever there is a decline of dharma, O dānava, / and an uprising of adharma, then he manifests himself.

1.38.s:
kadāciddaityadeveṣu kadācinmanujeṣu ca ..
kadācidatha tiryakṣu jñātvā kāryabalābalam .. 11 ..
1.38.d:
कदाचिद्दैत्यदेवेषु कदाचिन्मनुजेषु च ॥
कदाचिदथ तिर्यक्षु ज्ञात्वा कार्यबलाबलम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.38.m: Sometimes among daityas and gods, sometimes among human beings, / and sometimes among animals, after discerning the strengths and weaknesses of the task.

1.38.s:
yadā bhavati deveṣu devavacceṣṭate tadā ..
