tiryakṣu ca yadā devastiryagvacceṣṭate tadā ..
yadā bhavati mānuṣye tadā bhavati martyavat..
mānuṣyaṃ rūpamāsādya tapasā tripurāntakam..13..
1.38.d:
यदा भवति देवेषु देववच्चेष्टते तदा ॥
तिर्यक्षु च यदा देवस्तिर्यग्वच्चेष्टते तदा ॥
यदा भवति मानुष्ये तदा भवति मर्त्यवत्॥
मानुष्यं रूपमासाद्य तपसा त्रिपुरान्तकम्॥13॥
1.38.m: When he is among gods, he acts like a god; / and when the god is among animals, he acts like an animal. / When he is in a human state, he is like a mortal; / having assumed human form, through asceticism [he propitiated] the destroyer of Tripura.

1.38.s:
ārādhayāmāsa haraṃ svadehe paramaṃ nṛpa ..
sa tu devavarasyājñāṃ puraskṛtya mahātapāḥ .. 14 ..
1.38.d:
आराधयामास हरं स्वदेहे परमं नृप ॥
स तु देववरस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य महातपाः ॥ 14 ॥
1.38.m: Within his own body, O king, he worshipped Hara as supreme; / and he, of great austerity, placing first the command of the best of gods,

1.38.s:
yuṣmadvadhārthamāyāti rāmeṇa kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ ..
tasmācchakreṇa saṃdhānaṃ bhavato mama rocate .. 15 ..
1.38.d:
युष्मद्वधार्थमायाति रामेण कृतलक्षणः ॥
तस्माच्छक्रेण संधानं भवतो मम रोचते ॥ 15 ॥
1.38.m: comes to slay you, designated under the name of Rāma. / Therefore, making peace with Śakra pleases me for you.

1.38.s:
triviṣṭapañca devānāṃ bhavatvasurasattama ..
pātālanilayā yūyaṃ nivasadhvaṃ gatajvarāḥ .. 16 ..
1.38.d:
त्रिविष्टपञ्च देवानां भवत्वसुरसत्तम ॥
पातालनिलया यूयं निवसध्वं गतज्वराः ॥ 16 ॥
1.38.m: Let the three worlds belong to the gods, O best of asuras; / dwell free from anxiety with the netherworld as your abode.

1.38.s:
ahaṃ nivārayiṣyāmi śaṃkareṇa ca bhārgavam ..
anyathā niviśadhvaṃ ca manuṣyeṇa nirākṛtāḥ .. 17 ..
1.38.d:
अहं निवारयिष्यामि शंकरेण च भार्गवम् ॥
अन्यथा निविशध्वं च मनुष्येण निराकृताः ॥ 17 ॥
1.38.m: Through Śaṃkara, I will ward off the descendant of Bhṛgu; / otherwise, enter [it] having been defeated by a mortal.'

1.38.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktāstu śukreṇa buddhvā daiteyadānavāḥ ..
ūcurvākyaṃ susaṃrabdhāḥ śukraṃ bhṛgukulodvaham ..18 ..
1.38.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तास्तु शुक्रेण बुद्ध्वा दैतेयदानवाः ॥
ऊचुर्वाक्यं सुसंरब्धाः शुक्रं भृगुकुलोद्वहम् ॥18 ॥
1.38.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been spoken to thus by Śukra, and having understood, the daityas and dānavas, / greatly enraged, spoke words to Śukra, the bearer of the lineage of Bhṛgu.

1.38.s:
daityā ūcuḥ .. ekatrā'dhiṣṭhitaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam ..
yadyasmātpratiyudhyeta na bhīstatrā'pi vidyate ..19..
1.38.d:
दैत्या ऊचुः ॥ एकत्राऽधिष्ठितं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजंगमम् ॥
यद्यस्मात्प्रतियुध्येत न भीस्तत्राऽपि विद्यते ॥19॥
1.38.m: The daityas said: 'Even if the entire world of moving and unmoving beings stood on one side / and fought against us, even then there would be no fear.

1.38.s:
te kathaṃ mānuṣādbhītā nākaṃ tyakṣyāma śatrave ..
śaṃkaraṃ taṃ vijeṣyāmo yenā'sau preṣito dvijaḥ .. 20 ..
1.38.d:
ते कथं मानुषाद्भीता नाकं त्यक्ष्याम शत्रवे ॥
शंकरं तं विजेष्यामो येनाऽसौ प्रेषितो द्विजः ॥ 20 ॥
1.38.m: How should we, afraid of a mortal, surrender heaven to our enemy? / We shall conquer that Śaṃkara by whom this twice-born has been sent!'

1.38.s:
śukra uvāca ..
ekatra piṃḍitaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam ..
ekatra bhagavānviṣṇurjagataḥ so'tiricyate .. 21 ..
1.38.d:
शुक्र उवाच ॥
एकत्र पिंडितं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजंगमम् ॥
एकत्र भगवान्विष्णुर्जगतः सोऽतिरिच्यते ॥ 21 ॥
1.38.m: Śukra said: / 'Gather the entire world of moving and unmoving beings on one side; / on the other is the blessed Viṣṇu, who outweighs the world.

1.38.s:
sa na śakyo yudhā jetuṃ naiva devo maheśvaraḥ ..
te yūyaṃ prākṛtīṃ buddhiṃ tyaktvā sarve mahāsurāḥ ..
saṃdhiṃ kuruta devena śakreṇā'mitraghātinā .. 22 ..
1.38.d:
स न शक्यो युधा जेतुं नैव देवो महेश्वरः ॥
ते यूयं प्राकृतीं बुद्धिं त्यक्त्वा सर्वे महासुराः ॥
संधिं कुरुत देवेन शक्रेणाऽमित्रघातिना ॥ 22 ॥
1.38.m: He cannot be conquered in battle, nor can the god Maheśvara. / Giving up your common intellect, all of you great asuras / make peace with the god Śakra, the slayer of his foes.

1.38.s:
śakrakārye sadodyukto devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
yena daityā vinihatāḥ pūrve pūrvatarāśca ye .. 23 ..
1.38.d:
शक्रकार्ये सदोद्युक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
येन दैत्या विनिहताः पूर्वे पूर्वतराश्च ये ॥ 23 ॥
1.38.m: Janārdana, the god of gods, is ever zealous in the work of Śakra; / by him the daityas of earlier times, and those earlier still, were slain:

1.38.s:
śaṃbaro namuciḥ śambuḥ kārtavīryaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ ..
hiraṇyakaśipuḥ keśī hiraṇyākṣo madotkaṭaḥ .. 24 ..
1.38.d:
शंबरो नमुचिः शम्बुः कार्तवीर्यः कृतागमः ॥
हिरण्यकशिपुः केशी हिरण्याक्षो मदोत्कटः ॥ 24 ॥
1.38.m: Śambara, Namuci, Śambu, Kārtavīrya proficient in scriptures, / Hiraṇyakaśipu, Keśin, Hiraṇyākṣa intoxicated with pride,

1.38.s:
madhuśca kaiṭabhaścaiva viṭo dhūmo'ti'kopanaḥ ..
hayagrīvo nisundaśca sundaścandrārkalocanaḥ .. 25 ..'
1.38.d:
मधुश्च कैटभश्चैव विटो धूमोऽतिऽकोपनः ॥
हयग्रीवो निसुन्दश्च सुन्दश्चन्द्रार्कलोचनः ॥ 25 ॥'
1.38.m: and Madhu and Kaiṭabha, Viṭa, Dhūma who was exceedingly wrathful, / Hayagrīva, Nisunda, Sunda, Candrārkalocana,

1.38.s:
candrārkamardanaścaiva candrahartā raṇapriyaḥ ..
sūryaśatrurjitāmitro yajñahā yajñatāpanaḥ .. 26 ..
1.38.d:
चन्द्रार्कमर्दनश्चैव चन्द्रहर्ता रणप्रियः ॥
सूर्यशत्रुर्जितामित्रो यज्ञहा यज्ञतापनः ॥ 26 ॥
1.38.m: Candrārkamardana, Candrahartṛ fond of battle, / Sūryaśatru, Jitāmitra, Yajñahan, Yajñatāpana,

1.38.s:
meghanādo mahāromā meghavādo bhayānakaḥ ..
daśagrīvaḥ śatagrīvo mahāgrīvaśca dānavaḥ ..27..
1.38.d:
मेघनादो महारोमा मेघवादो भयानकः ॥
दशग्रीवः शतग्रीवो महाग्रीवश्च दानवः ॥27॥
1.38.m: Meghanāda, Mahāroman, Meghavāda, Bhayānaka, / Daśagrīva, Śatagrīva, and the dānava Mahāgrīva,

1.38.s:
kālakaḥ kālakeyaśca kālanemi sulocanaḥ ..
kālaśca kālakalpaśca makarākṣo janāntakaḥ .. 28 ..
1.38.d:
कालकः कालकेयश्च कालनेमि सुलोचनः ॥
कालश्च कालकल्पश्च मकराक्षो जनान्तकः ॥ 28 ॥
1.38.m: Kālaka, Kālakeya, Kālanemi, Sulocana, / Kāla, Kālakalpa, Makarākṣa, Janāntaka,

1.38.s:
antaḥ keśamano bhīmo devāntakanarāntakau ..
krodhahā bahunetraśca mahākālo jalāntakaḥ ..29..
1.38.d:
अन्तः केशमनो भीमो देवान्तकनरान्तकौ ॥
क्रोधहा बहुनेत्रश्च महाकालो जलान्तकः ॥29॥
1.38.m: Antaḥ, Keśamanas, Bhīma, Devāntaka and Narāntaka, / Krodhahan, Bahunetra, Mahākāla, Jalāntaka,

1.38.s:
ekalavyaḥ sa cādhāro durmukho durdharo vaḍiḥ ..
indutāpanarambho ca raṇacaṇḍaharapriyau .. 30 ..
1.38.d:
एकलव्यः स चाधारो दुर्मुखो दुर्धरो वडिः ॥
इन्दुतापनरम्भो च रणचण्डहरप्रियौ ॥ 30 ॥
1.38.m: Ekalavya, and Ādhāra, Durmukha, Durdhara, Vaḍi, / Indutāpana, Rambha, Raṇacaṇḍa, Harapriya,

1.38.s:
kirīṭī gajavaktraśca mahāsālo vilohitaḥ ..
hrādānuhrādaprahrādavṛkṣarakṣaradāruṇāḥ .. 31 ..
1.38.d:
किरीटी गजवक्त्रश्च महासालो विलोहितः ॥
ह्रादानुह्रादप्रह्रादवृक्षरक्षरदारुणाः ॥ 31 ॥
1.38.m: Kirīṭin, Gajavaktra, Mahāsāla, Vilohita, / Hrāda, Anuhrāda, Prahrāda, Vṛkṣa, Rakṣas, and Dāruṇa,

1.38.s:
śatabhaḥ śalabhaścaiva kūpanaśca mahāsuraḥ ..
vipracittiḥ śivaḥ śaṅkarayaḥ śaṅkustathaiva ca .. 32 ..
1.38.d:
शतभः शलभश्चैव कूपनश्च महासुरः ॥
विप्रचित्तिः शिवः शङ्करयः शङ्कुस्तथैव च ॥ 32 ॥
1.38.m: Śatabha, Śalabha, and the great asura Kūpana, / Vipracitti, Śiva, Śaṅkaraya, and Śaṅku,

1.38.s:
ayaḥśirā aśvaśirā bhīmadakṣo guhāśayaḥ ..
vegavānketumānugraḥ sogravigro mahāsuraḥ .. 33 ..
1.38.d:
अयःशिरा अश्वशिरा भीमदक्षो गुहाशयः ॥
वेगवान्केतुमानुग्रः सोग्रविग्रो महासुरः ॥ 33 ॥
1.38.m: Ayaḥśiras, Aśvaśiras, Bhīmadakṣa, Guhāśaya, / Vegavat, Ketumat, Ugra, and the great asura Ugravigra,

1.38.s:
puṣkaraḥ puṣkalaścaiva sālvośvapatireva ca ..
kumbho nikumbhaḥ śatadā saṃgraho gaganapriyaḥ .. 34 ..
1.38.d:
पुष्करः पुष्कलश्चैव साल्वोश्वपतिरेव च ॥
कुम्भो निकुम्भः शतदा संग्रहो गगनप्रियः ॥ 34 ॥
1.38.m: Puṣkara, Puṣkala, Sālva, and Aśvapati, / Kumbha, Nikumbha, Śatadā, Saṃgraha, Gaganapriya —

1.38.s:
ete cā'nye ca vikhyātā daiteyā samaroddhatāḥ ..
sarve labdhavarāḥ śūrāḥ sarve ca gatamanyavaḥ .. 35 ..
1.38.d:
एते चाऽन्ये च विख्याता दैतेया समरोद्धताः ॥
सर्वे लब्धवराः शूराः सर्वे च गतमन्यवः ॥ 35 ॥
1.38.m: these and other renowned daiteyas arrogant in battle, / all of whom had obtained boons, were heroic, and were devoid of grief,

1.38.s:
sarvaistridaśarājyāni kāritāni baloddhataiḥ ..
te hatāstena devena vāsavapriyakāmyayā .. 36 ..
1.38.d:
सर्वैस्त्रिदशराज्यानि कारितानि बलोद्धतैः ॥
ते हतास्तेन देवेन वासवप्रियकाम्यया ॥ 36 ॥
1.38.m: by all of whom the realms of the thirty gods had been subjected when swollen with power: / they were slain by that god desiring what is dear to Vāsava.

1.38.s:
kecinmanuṣyarūpeṇa tiryagrūpeṇa cā'pare ..
kecicca devarūpeṇa nihatā bhūritejasā .. 37 ..
1.38.d:
केचिन्मनुष्यरूपेण तिर्यग्रूपेण चाऽपरे ॥
केचिच्च देवरूपेण निहता भूरितेजसा ॥ 37 ॥
1.38.m: Some in human form, others in animal form, / and some in divine form, were slain by him of vast splendour.

1.38.s:
sālva uvāca ..
jānāmi tasya māhātmyaṃ devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ ..
ahaṃ svamaraṇaṃ matvā tena yotsyāmi bhārgava .. 38 ..
1.38.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
जानामि तस्य माहात्म्यं देवदेवस्य शार्ङ्गिणः ॥
अहं स्वमरणं मत्वा तेन योत्स्यामि भार्गव ॥ 38 ॥
1.38.m:
Sālva said:
I know the majesty of that god of gods who holds the Śārṅga bow.
Knowing my death [is certain], I shall fight with him, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.38.s:
viśiṣṭānmaraṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ na hīnādvijayo raṇe ..
viṣṇoḥ karavinaṣṭānāṃ bhūyo rājyaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 39 ..
1.38.d:
विशिष्टान्मरणं श्रेष्ठं न हीनाद्विजयो रणे ॥
विष्णोः करविनष्टानां भूयो राज्यं भविष्यति ॥ 39 ॥
1.38.m:
Death at the hands of a superior is better; victory over an inferior in battle is not.
Those destroyed by the hand of Viṣṇu will have kingship again.

1.38.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktastvasurādhipena bhṛgupradhāno bhagavān sa śukraḥ ..
jñātvā sa daityānsakalānvinaṣṭāñjagāma kāṣṭhāmaparāmabhīṣṭām .. 40 ..
1.38.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्तस्त्वसुराधिपेन भृगुप्रधानो भगवान् स शुक्रः ॥
ज्ञात्वा स दैत्यान्सकलान्विनष्टाञ्जगाम काष्ठामपरामभीष्टाम् ॥ 40 ॥
1.38.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Addressed thus by the ruler of the asuras, that venerable Śukra, foremost of the Bhṛgus,
knowing all the daityas were destroyed, went to another, desired direction.

1.39.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā gate śukre gaviṣṭho vākyamabravīt ..
rājañchukrasya vacanaṃ kriyatāmavicārayan..1..
1.39.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा गते शुक्रे गविष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
राजञ्छुक्रस्य वचनं क्रियतामविचारयन्॥1॥
1.39.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When Śukra had departed after speaking thus, Gaviṣṭha spoke these words:
‘O king, let the word of Śukra be carried out without hesitation.

1.39.s:
svapnā hi sumahāghorā dṛśyante bhayavardhanāḥ .'
bhavatāṃ hi vināśāya rātryante satataṃ vibho ..2..
1.39.d:
स्वप्ना हि सुमहाघोरा दृश्यन्ते भयवर्धनाः ।'
भवतां हि विनाशाय रात्र्यन्ते सततं विभो ॥2॥
1.39.m:
For exceedingly terrible dreams that increase fear are seen,
portending your destruction, constantly at the end of the night, O mighty lord.

1.39.s:
bhavānsvapne mayā dṛṣṭo rakta sraganulepanaḥ ..
uṣṭreṇa śiśumāreṇa varāheṇa tathā vrajan..3..
1.39.d:
भवान्स्वप्ने मया दृष्टो रक्त स्रगनुलेपनः ॥
उष्ट्रेण शिशुमारेण वराहेण तथा व्रजन्॥3॥
1.39.m:
You were seen by me in a dream, adorned with red garlands and unguent,
going upon a camel, a dolphin, and a boar;

1.39.s:
tailāktāścāpare daityāḥ kharayānamupāśritāḥ ..
patantaḥ parvatā dṛṣṭā rājam̐ste bhayakāraṇam..4..
1.39.d:
तैलाक्ताश्चापरे दैत्याः खरयानमुपाश्रिताः ॥
पतन्तः पर्वता दृष्टा राजम्̐स्ते भयकारणम्॥4॥
1.39.m:
and other daityas, smeared with oil, mounted on donkey-chariots.
Mountains were seen falling, O king, a cause of terror for you.

1.39.s:
kecitkṛṣṇāṃbaradharāḥ kecitkṛsarabhojinaḥ..
kecitpaṅkagatā dṛṣṭāḥ kecidbhasmaśayā gatāḥ..5..
1.39.d:
केचित्कृष्णांबरधराः केचित्कृसरभोजिनः॥
केचित्पङ्कगता दृष्टाः केचिद्भस्मशया गताः॥5॥
1.39.m:
Some wore black clothes, some were eating rice with pulse;
some were seen sunk in mud, some had gone to a bed of ashes;

1.39.s:
kecidvivastrayā nāryā kṛṣyante dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ..
kācidraktāmbarā nārī nīyate dakṣiṇāṃ diśam..6..
1.39.d:
केचिद्विवस्त्रया नार्या कृष्यन्ते दक्षिणां दिशम् ॥
काचिद्रक्ताम्बरा नारी नीयते दक्षिणां दिशम्॥6॥
1.39.m:
some were dragged toward the southern direction by a naked woman;
a certain woman dressed in red garments was being led toward the southern direction;

1.39.s:
kecinnṛtyanti bhūpālā hasanti ca tathā'pare ..
kecinmuṇḍā mayā dṛṣṭāḥ kecitkāṣāyavāsasaḥ .. 7..
1.39.d:
केचिन्नृत्यन्ति भूपाला हसन्ति च तथाऽपरे ॥
केचिन्मुण्डा मया दृष्टाः केचित्काषायवाससः ॥ 7॥
1.39.m:
some kings were dancing and others were laughing;
some were seen by me with shaven heads, some in ochre robes;

1.39.s:
caṇḍālaskandhagāḥ kecitkecitkiṃśukasaṃsthitāḥ ..
gajāśvapattisainyena sarveṇa ca bhavānyutaḥ .. 8 ..
1.39.d:
चण्डालस्कन्धगाः केचित्केचित्किंशुकसंस्थिताः ॥
गजाश्वपत्तिसैन्येन सर्वेण च भवान्युतः ॥ 8 ॥
1.39.m:
some were mounted on the shoulders of caṇḍālas, some standing among kiṃśuka trees;
and you, accompanied by your entire army of elephants, horses, and foot soldiers,

1.39.s:
vāpīṃ sukaluṣāṃ prāpya nimagno gomaye hrade ..
rājaśrīśca mayā dṛṣṭā śakrāliṅganatatparā .. 9 ..
1.39.d:
वापीं सुकलुषां प्राप्य निमग्नो गोमये ह्रदे ॥
राजश्रीश्च मया दृष्टा शक्रालिङ्गनतत्परा ॥ 9 ॥
1.39.m:
having reached an exceedingly foul step-well, were plunged into a pool of cow dung;
and the royal fortune was seen by me devoted to embracing Śakra.

1.39.s:
tasya me rocate sandhistava śakreṇa pārthiva ..
prāṇānrakṣata bho rājañjīvanbhadrāṇyupāśnute .. 10 ..
1.39.d:
तस्य मे रोचते सन्धिस्तव शक्रेण पार्थिव ॥
प्राणान्रक्षत भो राजञ्जीवन्भद्राण्युपाश्नुते ॥ 10 ॥
1.39.m:
Therefore, a treaty with Śakra pleases me, O ruler of the earth.
Protect your life, O king! He who lives experiences good fortune.’

1.39.s:
sālva uvāca ..
yadaiva bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śrutaḥ śatrurmayā'nagha ..
tatraiva deva tacchrutvā rājyaṃ tyaktaṃ tathā mayā .. 11 ..
1.39.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
यदैव भगवान्विष्णुः श्रुतः शत्रुर्मयाऽनघ ॥
तत्रैव देव तच्छ्रुत्वा राज्यं त्यक्तं तथा मया ॥ 11 ॥
1.39.m:
Sālva said:
‘As soon as the venerable Viṣṇu was heard by me to be my enemy, O sinless one,
at that very moment, hearing that, I abandoned the kingdom, O lord.

1.39.s:
iṣṭaṃ yajñaistapastaptaṃ rājyaṃ kṛtamakaṇṭakam ..
mūrdhni sthitamamitrāṇāṃ suhṛdaḥ paripālitāḥ .. 12 ..
1.39.d:
इष्टं यज्ञैस्तपस्तप्तं राज्यं कृतमकण्टकम् ॥
मूर्ध्नि स्थितममित्राणां सुहृदः परिपालिताः ॥ 12 ॥
1.39.m:
I have sacrificed with sacrifices, practiced austerities, and made the kingdom free of thorns;
I have stood upon the heads of my enemies, and my friends have been protected;

1.39.s:
dhṛto bhṛtyajanaḥ sarvaḥ kṛtakṛtyāstato vayam ..
govindānmaraṇaṃ prāpya bhūyo rājyaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 13 ..
1.39.d:
धृतो भृत्यजनः सर्वः कृतकृत्यास्ततो वयम् ॥
गोविन्दान्मरणं प्राप्य भूयो राज्यं भविष्यति ॥ 13 ॥
1.39.m:
all my servants have been maintained; thus we have accomplished our purpose.
Meeting death from Govinda, kingship will be mine again.’

1.39.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityeva vākyaṃ tu niśamya rājño mene tadāyuktatamaṃ gaviṣṭhaḥ ..
tūṣṇīṃ babhūvā'tha suniścitātmā mene ca daityānsamare vinaṣṭān .. 14 ..
1.39.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येव वाक्यं तु निशम्य राज्ञो मेने तदायुक्ततमं गविष्ठः ॥
तूष्णीं बभूवाऽथ सुनिश्चितात्मा मेने च दैत्यान्समरे विनष्टान् ॥ 14 ॥
1.39.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard these words of the king, Gaviṣṭha then considered it most inappropriate.
With a firmly resolved mind, he then fell silent, and regarded the daityas as already destroyed in battle.

1.40.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
etasminneva kāle tu sālvasya ca mahātmanaḥ ..
śīrṣamātrāvaśiṣṭastu dadṛśe cāgrajasya ca .. 1 ..
1.40.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु साल्वस्य च महात्मनः ॥
शीर्षमात्रावशिष्टस्तु ददृशे चाग्रजस्य च ॥ 1 ॥
1.40.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
At that very time, the elder brother of the great-souled Sālva,
with only his head remaining, was seen.

1.40.s:
rāhurityeva vikhyātaḥ pūjayāmāsa taṃ nṛpaḥ ..
yathārhaṃ pūjito rājñā niṣaṇṇo vākyamabravīt .. 2 ..
1.40.d:
राहुरित्येव विख्यातः पूजयामास तं नृपः ॥
यथार्हं पूजितो राज्ञा निषण्णो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 2 ॥
1.40.m:
He was renowned as Rāhu. The king worshipped him.
Worshipped suitably by the king, he sat down and spoke these words:

1.40.s:
rāhuruvāca..
na hi me rocate vairaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā..
yasya krodhādanaṅgohaṃ jātaḥ parabalārdanaḥ..3..
1.40.d:
राहुरुवाच॥
न हि मे रोचते वैरं विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना॥
यस्य क्रोधादनङ्गोहं जातः परबलार्दनः॥3॥

1.40.s:
prasādācca tathā yasya grahatvamupalabdhavān ..
kimanyaiḥ kīrtitaistasya karmabhiste'surātmaja .. 4 ..
1.40.d:
प्रसादाच्च तथा यस्य ग्रहत्वमुपलब्धवान् ॥
किमन्यैः कीर्तितैस्तस्य कर्मभिस्तेऽसुरात्मज ॥ 4 ॥
1.40.m:
and by whose grace I attained the status of a planet.
Why should his other deeds be recounted to you, O son of an asura?

1.40.s:
sālva uvāca ..
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi kathaṃ tena mahātmanā ..
anaṃgastvaṃ kṛto vīra graheśaśca kathaṃ kṛtaḥ .. 5 ..
1.40.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि कथं तेन महात्मना ॥
अनंगस्त्वं कृतो वीर ग्रहेशश्च कथं कृतः ॥ 5 ॥
1.40.m:
Sālva said:
O venerable one, I wish to hear how you were made bodiless by that great-souled one,
O hero, and how you were made a lord of the planets.

1.40.s:
rāhuruvāca ..
amaratvamabhīpsaṃtaḥ purā devā savāsavāḥ
keśavaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 6 ..
1.40.d:
राहुरुवाच ॥
अमरत्वमभीप्संतः पुरा देवा सवासवाः
केशवं शरणं गताः ॥ 6 ॥
1.40.m:
Rāhu said:
In ancient times, the gods accompanied by Vāsava, desiring immortality,
went to Keśava for refuge.

1.40.s:
devā ūcuḥ ..
bhagavan devadeveśa jagatāmārtināśana ..
nirviśeṣā vayaṃ martyaistrātā tatrāstu no bhavān .. 7 ..
1.40.d:
देवा ऊचुः ॥
भगवन् देवदेवेश जगतामार्तिनाशन ॥
निर्विशेषा वयं मर्त्यैस्त्राता तत्रास्तु नो भवान् ॥ 7 ॥
1.40.m:
The gods said:
O venerable one, lord of the god of gods, destroyer of the distress of the worlds!
We are no different from mortals; let you be our protector in this matter.

1.40.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
kṣīrodamathane yatnaṃ tridaśāḥ kartumarhatha ..
dānavaiḥ sahitā bhūtvā tataḥ śreyo'pyavāpsyatha .. 8 ..
1.40.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
क्षीरोदमथने यत्नं त्रिदशाः कर्तुमर्हथ ॥
दानवैः सहिता भूत्वा ततः श्रेयोऽप्यवाप्स्यथ ॥ 8 ॥

1.40.s:
rāhuruvāca ..
evamuktāḥ surāḥ sarve devadevena śārṅgiṇā ..
dānavaiḥ sahitā bhūtvā mamanthurvaruṇālayam .. 9 ..
1.40.d:
राहुरुवाच ॥
एवमुक्ताः सुराः सर्वे देवदेवेन शार्ङ्गिणा ॥
दानवैः सहिता भूत्वा ममन्थुर्वरुणालयम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.40.m:
Rāhu said:
Addressed thus by the god of gods who holds the Śārṅga bow, all the gods,
joined with the dānavas, churned the abode of Varuṇa.

1.40.s:
sāhāyyamakarotteṣāṃ tatra karmaṇi pārthiva ..
vinā viṣṇusahāyena na śaktāḥ sasurāsurāḥ .. 1.40.10 ..
1.40.d:
साहाय्यमकरोत्तेषां तत्र कर्मणि पार्थिव ॥
विना विष्णुसहायेन न शक्ताः ससुरासुराः ॥ 1.40.10 ॥
1.40.m:
He gave them assistance in that task, O ruler of the earth;
without the help of Viṣṇu, neither the gods nor the asuras were capable.

1.40.s:
anantaḥ sa tato bhūtvā cāṃśaḥ saṃkarṣaṇasya ca ..
utpāṭya maṃdiraṃ dorbhyāṃ cikṣepa payasāṃ nidhau .. 11 ..
1.40.d:
अनन्तः स ततो भूत्वा चांशः संकर्षणस्य च ॥
उत्पाट्य मंदिरं दोर्भ्यां चिक्षेप पयसां निधौ ॥ 11 ॥
1.40.m:
Then, having become Ananta, a portion of Saṃkarṣaṇa,
he uprooted Mount Mandara with both arms and cast it into the ocean of waters.

1.40.s:
akūpāre tato bhūtvā kūrmarūpī janārdanaḥ ..
mandaraṃ dhārayāmāsa kṣīrābdhigatamañjasā .. 12 ..
1.40.d:
अकूपारे ततो भूत्वा कूर्मरूपी जनार्दनः ॥
मन्दरं धारयामास क्षीराब्धिगतमञ्जसा ॥ 12 ॥
1.40.m:
Then Janārdana, having assumed the form of a tortoise in the deep ocean,
swiftly supported Mandara as it entered the Ocean of Milk.

1.40.s:
svanaiva tejasā nāgaṃ tathā saṃyojya vāsukim ..
cakre sa netratāṃ tatra tatra karmaṇi dānava .. 13 ..
1.40.d:
स्वनैव तेजसा नागं तथा संयोज्य वासुकिम् ॥
चक्रे स नेत्रतां तत्र तत्र कर्मणि दानव ॥ 13 ॥
1.40.m:
And attaching the serpent Vāsuki with his own radiance,
he made him the churning-rope for that task, O dānava.

1.40.s:
tato mamanthuḥ sahasā samudraṃ devadānavāḥ ..
yato mukhaṃ tato daityā yataḥ pucchaṃ tataḥ surāḥ .. 14 ..
1.40.d:
ततो ममन्थुः सहसा समुद्रं देवदानवाः ॥
यतो मुखं ततो दैत्या यतः पुच्छं ततः सुराः ॥ 14 ॥
1.40.m:
Then the gods and dānavas quickly churned the ocean;
where the mouth was, there were the daityas; where the tail was, there were the gods.

1.40.s:
vāsukerabhavaddaityā mathyamāne mahodadhau ..
mukhaśca nāgarājasya kareṇa dhṛtavānsvayam .. 15 ..
1.40.d:
वासुकेरभवद्दैत्या मथ्यमाने महोदधौ ॥
मुखश्च नागराजस्य करेण धृतवान्स्वयम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.40.m:
As the great ocean was being churned, the daityas were at Vāsuki’s [mouth],
and he himself held the mouth of the king of serpents with his hand.

1.40.s:
ākāśābhimukhaṃ kṛtvā devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
mukhe niḥśvāsavātena saviṣeṇa hi bhūpate .. 16 ..
1.40.d:
आकाशाभिमुखं कृत्वा देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
मुखे निःश्वासवातेन सविषेण हि भूपते ॥ 16 ॥
1.40.m:
Turning it toward the sky, the god of gods, Janārdana,
[warded off] the breath of the wind from the mouth, full of poison, O king;

1.40.s:
anyathā daityasaṃghānāṃ vināśamabhaviṣyata ..
himācalābhāḥ kāllolāḥ kṣīrābdhergaganaspṛśaḥ .. 17 ..
1.40.d:
अन्यथा दैत्यसंघानां विनाशमभविष्यत ॥
हिमाचलाभाः काल्लोलाः क्षीराब्धेर्गगनस्पृशः ॥ 17 ॥
1.40.m:
otherwise, destruction would have come upon the hosts of daityas.
Surges from the Ocean of Milk, resembling the Himālaya, touching the sky,

1.40.s: utpeturmathyamānasya balibhidevadānavaiḥ .. 18 ..
1.40.d: उत्पेतुर्मथ्यमानस्य बलिभिदेवदानवैः ॥ 18 ॥
1.40.m: flew up as it was being churned by the slayer of Bala, the gods, and the dānavas.

1.40.s:
śṛṅgāṇi nipatanti sma mandarasya mahodadhau ..
ratnacitrāṇi ramyāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 19 ..
1.40.d:
शृङ्गाणि निपतन्ति स्म मन्दरस्य महोदधौ ॥
रत्नचित्राणि रम्याणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 19 ॥
1.40.m:
Peaks of Mount Mandara, delightful and variegated with jewels,
fell down into the great ocean by the hundreds and thousands.

1.40.s:
drumāśca śataśaḥ peturmṛgāḥ petuḥ sahasraśaḥ ..
trailokyaṃ pūrayannādai rarāsa payasāṃ nidhiḥ .. 1.40.20 ..
1.40.d:
द्रुमाश्च शतशः पेतुर्मृगाः पेतुः सहस्रशः ॥
त्रैलोक्यं पूरयन्नादै ररास पयसां निधिः ॥ 1.40.20 ॥
1.40.m:
Trees fell by the hundreds, and wild beasts fell by the thousands;
filling the three worlds with roaring sounds, the ocean of waters resounded.

1.40.s:
kṣīrakallolavasanaḥ śvetameghakṛtāṃśukaḥ ..
rājate mandarādrissa nānādhātuvibhūṣitaḥ .. 21 .
1.40.d:
क्षीरकल्लोलवसनः श्वेतमेघकृतांशुकः ॥
राजते मन्दराद्रिस्स नानाधातुविभूषितः ॥ 21 ।
1.40.m:
Clothed in garments of milk-surges, having upper garments made of white clouds,
that Mount Mandara shone, adorned with various minerals.

1.40.s:
calanmeghāṃśuko ghūrṇannatyarthaṃ vāyupūritaiḥ ..
guhāmukhaiḥ sapraṇataṃ girirmattairivārṇavaḥ ..22 ..
1.40.d:
चलन्मेघांशुको घूर्णन्नत्यर्थं वायुपूरितैः ॥
गुहामुखैः सप्रणतं गिरिर्मत्तैरिवार्णवः ॥22 ॥
1.40.m:
With moving garments of clouds, reeling exceedingly, through its cave-mouths
filled with wind, the bowed mountain was like an intoxicated ocean.

1.40.s:
nirjharāśrurmahānādaḥ śṛṅgocchritamahābhujaḥ ..
aniśaṃ sa giriśreṣṭhaḥ sthānahānyeva roditi .. 23 ..
1.40.d:
निर्झराश्रुर्महानादः शृङ्गोच्छ्रितमहाभुजः ॥
अनिशं स गिरिश्रेष्ठः स्थानहान्येव रोदिति ॥ 23 ॥
1.40.m:
With waterfalls as tears, uttering a great roar, with raised mountain-peaks as its great arms,
that foremost of mountains constantly wept, as if at the loss of its place.

1.40.s:
devopabhogyānsakalānmahānta iti cintayan ..
vādyatsu devavādyeṣu nṛtyatīva sa mandaraḥ .. 24 ..
1.40.d:
देवोपभोग्यान्सकलान्महान्त इति चिन्तयन् ॥
वाद्यत्सु देववाद्येषु नृत्यतीव स मन्दरः ॥ 24 ॥
1.40.m:
Thinking, ‘All these great things are to be enjoyed by the gods,’
as divine musical instruments played, that Mandara seemed to dance.

1.40.s:
evaṃ hi mathyamānasya kṣīrābdheḥ sumahātmanaḥ ..
prādurbhūtaṃ viṣaṃ ghoraṃ kālānalasamaprabham .. 25 ..
1.40.d:
एवं हि मथ्यमानस्य क्षीराब्धेः सुमहात्मनः ॥
प्रादुर्भूतं विषं घोरं कालानलसमप्रभम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.40.m: As that great ocean of milk was thus being churned, / a terrible poison arose, equal in brilliance to the fire of cosmic dissolution.

1.40.s:
yena prodbhūtamātreṇa viṣaṇṇā devadānavāḥ ..
tatpapau bhagavāñchaṃbhustrailokyahitakāmyayā ..26..
1.40.d:
येन प्रोद्भूतमात्रेण विषण्णा देवदानवाः ॥
तत्पपौ भगवाञ्छंभुस्त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया ॥26॥
1.40.m: As soon as it sprang forth, the gods and Dānavas grew despondent; / [then] the blessed Sambhu drank it, desiring the welfare of the three worlds.

1.40.s:
viṣe kaṇṭhamanuprāpte nīlakaṇṭhatvamāgataḥ ..
dhārayāmāsa tatkaṇṭhe śobhārthaṃ suravāritaḥ .. 27 ..
1.40.d:
विषे कण्ठमनुप्राप्ते नीलकण्ठत्वमागतः ॥
धारयामास तत्कण्ठे शोभार्थं सुरवारितः ॥ 27 ॥
1.40.m: When the poison reached his throat, he acquired blueness of the neck; / restrained by the gods, he kept it in his throat for decoration.

1.40.s:
tataścandrakalā jātā trailokyasyaiva sundarī ..
jaṭājūṭena tāṃ cakre devadevo maheśvaraḥ .. 28 ..
1.40.d:
ततश्चन्द्रकला जाता त्रैलोक्यस्यैव सुन्दरी ॥
जटाजूटेन तां चक्रे देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥ 28 ॥
1.40.m: Then the crescent moon was born, lovely to the three worlds; / Maheśvara, the god of gods, placed it upon his matted hair.

1.40.s:
raśmijvālāvalīpuñjavibhāsitajagattrayam ..
vaiḍūryakaustubhaṃ jātaṃ yaṃ babhāra hṛdā hariḥ .. 29 ..
1.40.d:
रश्मिज्वालावलीपुञ्जविभासितजगत्त्रयम् ॥
वैडूर्यकौस्तुभं जातं यं बभार हृदा हरिः ॥ 29 ॥
1.40.m: The cat's-eye Kaustubha gem was born, illuminating the three worlds / with a mass of flaming rays; Hari bore it upon his heart.

1.40.s:
vātaraṃho mahākāyaḥ śaśāṅkasadṛśacchaviḥ ..
uccaiśravāhayo jātassa ca devānupāśritaḥ .. 1.40.30 ..
1.40.d:
वातरंहो महाकायः शशाङ्कसदृशच्छविः ॥
उच्चैश्रवाहयो जातस्स च देवानुपाश्रितः ॥ 1.40.30 ॥
1.40.m: With the speed of the wind, a gigantic body, and the radiance of the moon, / the horse named Uccaiḥśravas was born, and he took refuge with the gods.

1.40.s:
tataḥ surā samutpannā sā ca pītā mahāsuraiḥ ..
tatastvapsaraso jātā devarāmā manoramāḥ .. 31 ..
1.40.d:
ततः सुरा समुत्पन्ना सा च पीता महासुरैः ॥
ततस्त्वप्सरसो जाता देवरामा मनोरमाः ॥ 31 ॥
1.40.m: Then wine arose, and it was drunk by the great asuras; / then arose the apsarases, the charming women of the gods.

1.40.s: devī lakṣmīstato jātā rūpeṇā'pratimā śubhā..32..
1.40.d: देवी लक्ष्मीस्ततो जाता रूपेणाऽप्रतिमा शुभा॥32॥
1.40.m: Then the goddess Lakṣmī was born, auspicious and incomparable in beauty.

1.40.s:
yasyāḥ śubhau tāmarasaprakāśau pādāmbujau spṛṣṭatalāṅgulīkau ..
jaṅghe śubhe romavivarjite ca gūḍhāsthikaṃ jānuyugaṃ suramyam .. 33 ..
1.40.d:
यस्याः शुभौ तामरसप्रकाशौ पादाम्बुजौ स्पृष्टतलाङ्गुलीकौ ॥
जङ्घे शुभे रोमविवर्जिते च गूढास्थिकं जानुयुगं सुरम्यम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.40.m: Her auspicious lotus feet shone like red water lilies, the toes touching the soles; / her shanks were auspicious and free of hair, and her knees lovely, with concealed bones.

1.40.s:
suvarṇadaṇḍapratimau tathorū cābhogyaramyaṃ jaghanaṃ ghanaṃ ca ..
madhyaṃ suvṛttaṃ kuliśodarābhaṃ valitrayaṃ cāru śubhaṃ dadhānam ..34 ..
1.40.d:
सुवर्णदण्डप्रतिमौ तथोरू चाभोग्यरम्यं जघनं घनं च ॥
मध्यं सुवृत्तं कुलिशोदराभं वलित्रयं चारु शुभं दधानम् ॥34 ॥
1.40.m: Her thighs were like golden rods, and her expansive hips were lovely and solid; / her waist was well rounded, resembling the hollow of a vajra, bearing three lovely, auspicious folds.

1.40.s:
uttuṅgamābhogi samaṃ viśālaṃ stanadvayaṃ cārusuvarṇavarṇam ..
bāhū suvṛttāvatikomalau ca karadvayaṃ padmadalāgrakānti .. 35 ..
1.40.d:
उत्तुङ्गमाभोगि समं विशालं स्तनद्वयं चारुसुवर्णवर्णम् ॥
बाहू सुवृत्तावतिकोमलौ च करद्वयं पद्मदलाग्रकान्ति ॥ 35 ॥
1.40.m: Her pair of breasts was elevated, expansive, symmetrical, broad, and the colour of fine gold; / her arms were well rounded and very tender, and her hands had the lustre of lotus petals.

1.40.s:
kaṇṭhañca śaṅkhāgranibhaṃ suramyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ samaṃ cāru sirāvihīnam ..
karṇau śubhau cāruśubhapramāṇau sampūrṇacandrapratimañca vaktram .. 36 ..
1.40.d:
कण्ठञ्च शङ्खाग्रनिभं सुरम्यं पृष्ठं समं चारु सिराविहीनम् ॥
कर्णौ शुभौ चारुशुभप्रमाणौ सम्पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमञ्च वक्त्रम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.40.m: Her lovely neck resembled the tip of a conch shell; her back was even, beautiful, and devoid of visible veins; / her auspicious ears were of fine and auspicious proportion, and her face resembled the full moon.

1.40.s:
kundendutulyā daśanāstathoṣṭhau pravālakānāṃ pratipakṣabhūtau ..
spaṣṭā ca nāsā cibukaṃ ca ramyaṃ kapolayugmaṃ śaśitulyakānti .. 37 ..
1.40.d:
कुन्देन्दुतुल्या दशनास्तथोष्ठौ प्रवालकानां प्रतिपक्षभूतौ ॥
स्पष्टा च नासा चिबुकं च रम्यं कपोलयुग्मं शशितुल्यकान्ति ॥ 37 ॥
1.40.m: Her teeth were like jasmine buds and the moon; her lips rivalled corals; / her nose was well defined, her chin lovely, and her two cheeks possessed radiance equal to the moon.

1.40.s:
unnidranīlotpalasannikāśaṃ trivarṇamākarṇikamakṣiyugmam ..
śiroruhāḥ kuñcitanīladīrghā vīṇeva vāṇī madhurā śubhā ca .. 38 ..
1.40.d:
उन्निद्रनीलोत्पलसन्निकाशं त्रिवर्णमाकर्णिकमक्षियुग्मम् ॥
शिरोरुहाः कुञ्चितनीलदीर्घा वीणेव वाणी मधुरा शुभा च ॥ 38 ॥
1.40.m: Her two eyes, extending to her ears, had three colours and resembled blooming blue lotuses; / her hair was curly, black, and long, and her voice was sweet and auspicious like a vīṇā.

1.40.s:
vastre susūkṣme vimale dadhānā candrāṃśutulye'timanobhirāme ..
śrotradvayenāpyatha kuṇḍale ca saṃtānakānāṃ śirasā ca mālām .. 39 ..
1.40.d:
वस्त्रे सुसूक्ष्मे विमले दधाना चन्द्रांशुतुल्येऽतिमनोभिरामे ॥
श्रोत्रद्वयेनाप्यथ कुण्डले च संतानकानां शिरसा च मालाम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.40.m: Wearing two extremely fine, spotless garments resembling moonlight and exceedingly enchanting to the mind, / she wore two earrings in her ears and a garland of saṃtānaka flowers on her head.

1.40.s:
gaṅgāpravāhapratimañca hāraṃ kaṇṭhena śubhraṃ dadhatī suvṛttam .. 40 ..
tathāṅgadau ratnasahasracitrau haṃsasvanau cā'pyatha nūpūrau ca ..1.40.40..
1.40.d:
गङ्गाप्रवाहप्रतिमञ्च हारं कण्ठेन शुभ्रं दधती सुवृत्तम् ॥ 40 ॥
तथाङ्गदौ रत्नसहस्रचित्रौ हंसस्वनौ चाऽप्यथ नूपूरौ च ॥1.40.40॥
1.40.m:
Around her neck she wore a white, well-rounded necklace / that resembled the flow of the Ganges.
Likewise, [she wore] armlets bright with thousands of jewels, / and anklets that sounded like swans.

1.40.s:
kareṇa padmaṃ bhramaropagītaṃ vaiḍūryanālañca śubhaṃ gṛhītvā ..
svarūpamūḍheṣu surāsureṣu dṛṣṭiṃ dadau cārumanobhirāmā ..41..
1.40.d:
करेण पद्मं भ्रमरोपगीतं वैडूर्यनालञ्च शुभं गृहीत्वा ॥
स्वरूपमूढेषु सुरासुरेषु दृष्टिं ददौ चारुमनोभिरामा ॥41॥
1.40.m: Holding in her hand an auspicious lotus with a lapis stem, sung to by bees, / she, enchanting and captivating to the mind, cast her gaze upon the gods and asuras who were bewildered by her form.

1.40.s:
sā devasaṃghānasurāṃśca dṛṣṭvā dadarśa devaṃ jagatāṃ pradhānam ..
devāsurebhyastvatiriktarūpaṃ sūryāyutābhaṃ bhuvaneṣvajeyam ..42 ..
1.40.d:
सा देवसंघानसुरांश्च दृष्ट्वा ददर्श देवं जगतां प्रधानम् ॥
देवासुरेभ्यस्त्वतिरिक्तरूपं सूर्यायुताभं भुवनेष्वजेयम् ॥42 ॥
1.40.m: Looking upon the hosts of gods and asuras, she saw the god, the foremost of the worlds, / surpassing the gods and asuras in beauty, radiant as ten thousand suns, invincible across the worlds.

1.40.s:
unnidranīlanalinadyuticāruvarṇaṃ saṃtaptahāṭakanibhe vasane vasānam ..
dṛṣṭvaiva jātapulakodgamamātrakampā kṣīrābdhijā madanabāṇavaśaṃ jagāma .. 43..
1.40.d:
उन्निद्रनीलनलिनद्युतिचारुवर्णं संतप्तहाटकनिभे वसने वसानम् ॥
दृष्ट्वैव जातपुलकोद्गममात्रकम्पा क्षीराब्धिजा मदनबाणवशं जगाम ॥ 43॥
1.40.m: Having seen him whose lovely complexion had the brilliance of a blooming blue lotus, who was clad in garments resembling heated gold, / the ocean-born [goddess], trembling merely from the rising of goosebumps that arose [in her], fell under the sway of Love’s arrows.

1.41.s:
rāhuruvāca ..
sā kāmabāṇābhihatā samīkṣya madhusūdanam ..
svayaṃ vṛtavatī nāthaṃ bhartāramaparājitam ..1..
1.41.d:
राहुरुवाच ॥
सा कामबाणाभिहता समीक्ष्य मधुसूदनम् ॥
स्वयं वृतवती नाथं भर्तारमपराजितम् ॥1॥
1.41.m: Rāhu said: / Struck by Love's arrows upon beholding Madhusūdana, / she herself chose the lord, the unconquered husband.

1.41.s:
prakṛtissā vinirdiṣṭā puruṣaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ..
tayā viyujyate nā'sau kadācidapi śatruhā ..2..
1.41.d:
प्रकृतिस्सा विनिर्दिष्टा पुरुषः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
तया वियुज्यते नाऽसौ कदाचिदपि शत्रुहा ॥2॥
1.41.m: She is designated as Prakṛti, and the Cosmic Person is Puruṣottama; / never is he, the slayer of foes, separated from her.

1.41.s:
śaṃkaraḥ puruṣaḥ proktaḥ prakṛtiḥ pārvatī smṛtā ..
puruṣaḥ pākahā proktaḥ prakṛtiśca tathā śacī ..3.
1.41.d:
शंकरः पुरुषः प्रोक्तः प्रकृतिः पार्वती स्मृता ॥
पुरुषः पाकहा प्रोक्तः प्रकृतिश्च तथा शची ॥3.
1.41.m: Śaṃkara is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and Pārvatī is remembered as Prakṛti; / the slayer of Pāka is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and likewise Śacī is Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
hutāśanaśca puruṣaḥ svāhā ca prakṛtiḥ smṛtā ..
yamaśca puruṣaḥ prokto dhūmorṇā prakṛtiḥ smṛtā .. 4 ..
1.41.d:
हुताशनश्च पुरुषः स्वाहा च प्रकृतिः स्मृता ॥
यमश्च पुरुषः प्रोक्तो धूमोर्णा प्रकृतिः स्मृता ॥ 4 ॥
1.41.m: The fire-consumer is the Cosmic Person, and Svāhā is remembered as Prakṛti; / Yama is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and Dhūmorṇā is remembered as Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
virūpākṣaśca puruṣaḥ prakṛtirnirṛtiḥ smṛtā ..
varuṇaḥ puruṣaḥ prokto gaurī ca prakṛtistathā .. 5 ..
1.41.d:
विरूपाक्षश्च पुरुषः प्रकृतिर्निरृतिः स्मृता ॥
वरुणः पुरुषः प्रोक्तो गौरी च प्रकृतिस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.41.m: Virūpākṣa is the Cosmic Person, and Nirṛti is remembered as Prakṛti; / Varuṇa is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and likewise Gaurī is Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
vāyuśca puruṣo jñeyaḥ prakṛtiśca tathā śivā ..
puruṣaśca dharmo vṛkṣastadviśvaprakṛtiḥ smṛtā .. 6 ..
1.41.d:
वायुश्च पुरुषो ज्ञेयः प्रकृतिश्च तथा शिवा ॥
पुरुषश्च धर्मो वृक्षस्तद्विश्वप्रकृतिः स्मृता ॥ 6 ॥
1.41.m: Vāyu is to be known as the Cosmic Person, and Śivā is likewise Prakṛti; / Dharma is the tree as the Cosmic Person, and the entire universe is remembered as Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
candramā puruṣaḥ prokto jyotsnā ca prakṛtistathā..
dharmaśca puruṣaḥ proktaḥ prakṛtiśca karīṣiṇī.. 7 ..
1.41.d:
चन्द्रमा पुरुषः प्रोक्तो ज्योत्स्ना च प्रकृतिस्तथा॥
धर्मश्च पुरुषः प्रोक्तः प्रकृतिश्च करीषिणी॥ 7 ॥
1.41.m: The moon is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and moonlight is likewise Prakṛti; / Dharma is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and Karīṣiṇī is Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
yajñaśca puruṣaḥ prokto dakṣiṇā prakṛtistathā ..
divasaḥ puruṣaḥ prokto prakṛtiśca tathā niśā .. 8 ..
1.41.d:
यज्ञश्च पुरुषः प्रोक्तो दक्षिणा प्रकृतिस्तथा ॥
दिवसः पुरुषः प्रोक्तो प्रकृतिश्च तथा निशा ॥ 8 ॥
1.41.m: Sacrifice is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and dakṣiṇā is likewise Prakṛti; / the day is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and night is likewise Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
ākāśaḥ puruṣaḥ proktaḥ prakṛtiśca tathā mahī ..
oṃkāraḥ puruṣaḥ proktaḥ sāvitrī prakṛtiḥ smṛtāḥ ..9..
1.41.d:
आकाशः पुरुषः प्रोक्तः प्रकृतिश्च तथा मही ॥
ओंकारः पुरुषः प्रोक्तः सावित्री प्रकृतिः स्मृताः ॥9॥
1.41.m: The sky is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and the earth is likewise Prakṛti; / the Praṇava is declared to be the Cosmic Person, and Sāvitrī is remembered as Prakṛti.

1.41.s:
prakṛtiḥ sā śubhā lakṣmīrviṣṇuḥ puruṣa ucyate ..
sā sadehā videhā sā saguṇā nirguṇā ca sā .. 1.41.10 ..
1.41.d:
प्रकृतिः सा शुभा लक्ष्मीर्विष्णुः पुरुष उच्यते ॥
सा सदेहा विदेहा सा सगुणा निर्गुणा च सा ॥ 1.41.10 ॥
1.41.m: The auspicious Lakṣmī is Prakṛti, and Viṣṇu is called the Cosmic Person; / she is embodied and disembodied, endowed with qualities and free of qualities.

1.41.s:
tayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ..
sā kāntiḥ sā dhṛtiḥ sā śrīḥ sā prabhā ca sanātanī .. 11 ..
1.41.d:
तया सर्वमिदं व्याप्तं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
सा कान्तिः सा धृतिः सा श्रीः सा प्रभा च सनातनी ॥ 11 ॥
1.41.m: By her all this three worlds, moving and unmoving, is pervaded; / she is splendour, she is resolve, she is fortune, and she is eternal radiance.

1.41.s:
sā nidrā sā śubhā vāṇī sā ca devī sarasvatī ..
ratiḥ prītiḥ kṣitirdyauśca sā gaṃgā sā sarasvatī .. 12 ..
1.41.d:
सा निद्रा सा शुभा वाणी सा च देवी सरस्वती ॥
रतिः प्रीतिः क्षितिर्द्यौश्च सा गंगा सा सरस्वती ॥ 12 ॥
1.41.m: She is sleep, she is auspicious speech, and she is the goddess Sarasvatī; / [she is] pleasure, affection, earth, and heaven; she is the Ganges and she is Sarasvatī.

1.41.s:
tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirvapuḥ prajñā svadhā medhā sarasvatī ..
saiva nadyaḥ śubhā sarvāḥ saiva devī vanaspatī .. 13 ..
1.41.d:
तुष्टिः पुष्टिर्वपुः प्रज्ञा स्वधा मेधा सरस्वती ॥
सैव नद्यः शुभा सर्वाः सैव देवी वनस्पती ॥ 13 ॥
1.41.m: Contentment, nourishment, bodily form, wisdom, the ancestral oblation, intelligence, Sarasvatī— / she alone is all the auspicious rivers, and she is the goddess of trees.

1.41.s:
sā vāstudevatā dīkṣā sā bhaktirvaiṣṇavī smṛtā ..
buddhirlajjā dhṛtiḥ śāntiḥ sudhā śobhā jayā tvirā .. 14 ..
1.41.d:
सा वास्तुदेवता दीक्षा सा भक्तिर्वैष्णवी स्मृता ॥
बुद्धिर्लज्जा धृतिः शान्तिः सुधा शोभा जया त्विरा ॥ 14 ॥
1.41.m: She is the deity of the dwelling, initiation, and she is remembered as Vaiṣṇava devotion; / discernment, shame, resolve, peace, nectar, splendour, Jayā, and Irā.

1.41.s:
sinīvālī kuhū rākā tvevaṃ cānumatiḥ śubhā ..
kātyāyanī bhadrakālī suprabhā vijayā tathā .. .. 15 ..
1.41.d:
सिनीवाली कुहू राका त्वेवं चानुमतिः शुभा ॥
कात्यायनी भद्रकाली सुप्रभा विजया तथा ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
1.41.m: Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, and likewise auspicious Anumati; / Kātyāyanī, Bhadrakālī, Suprabhā, and likewise Vijayā;

1.41.s:
aditirditirdanuḥ kālā snāyuḥ siṃhikā muniḥ ..
kadrū krodhā tvirā prāvā vinatā surabhiḥ khagā .. 16 ..
1.41.d:
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुः काला स्नायुः सिंहिका मुनिः ॥
कद्रू क्रोधा त्विरा प्रावा विनता सुरभिः खगा ॥ 16 ॥
1.41.m: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālā, Snāyu, Siṃhikā, Muni, / Kadrū, Krodhā, Irā, Prāvā, Vinatā, Surabhi, Khagā;

1.41.s:
kīrtirlakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhā kṣamā śraddhā kriyā ratiḥ ..
anasūyā satī bhūtirvibhūtirvāruṇī tathā .. 17 ..
1.41.d:
कीर्तिर्लक्ष्मीर्धृतिर्मेधा क्षमा श्रद्धा क्रिया रतिः ॥
अनसूया सती भूतिर्विभूतिर्वारुणी तथा ॥ 17 ॥
1.41.m: Fame, fortune, resolve, intelligence, patience, faith, action, pleasure, / Anasūyā, Satī, prosperity, abundance, and likewise Vāruṇī;

1.41.s:
arundhatī vasurjāmī lobhā bhānurarundhatī ..
saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā tathaiva ca .. 18 ..
1.41.d:
अरुन्धती वसुर्जामी लोभा भानुररुन्धती ॥
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वा तथैव च ॥ 18 ॥
1.41.m: Arundhatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lobhā, Bhānu, Arundhatī, / Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and likewise Viśvā;

1.41.s:
mṛgā ca mṛgamandā ca haribhadrā yuvā tviḍā ..
bhūtā ca kapilā daṃṣṭrī saramā suramā tathā .. 19 ..
1.41.d:
मृगा च मृगमन्दा च हरिभद्रा युवा त्विडा ॥
भूता च कपिला दंष्ट्री सरमा सुरमा तथा ॥ 19 ॥
1.41.m: Mṛgā, Mṛgamandā, Haribhadrā, Yuvā, Iḍā, / Bhūtā, Kapilā, Daṃṣṭrī, Saramā, and likewise Suramā.

1.41.s:
rājaśrīrbhūmipālānāṃ brahmaśrīstadvidāṃ śubhā ..
puṣpaśrīḥ kānanānāṃ sā jayaśrīrjayināṃ raṇe .. 1.41.20 ..
1.41.d:
राजश्रीर्भूमिपालानां ब्रह्मश्रीस्तद्विदां शुभा ॥
पुष्पश्रीः काननानां सा जयश्रीर्जयिनां रणे ॥ 1.41.20 ॥
1.41.m: She is the royal fortune of kings, the auspicious fortune of sacred lore among those who know it, / the floral fortune of forests, and the fortune of victory for victors in battle.

1.41.s:
svargaśrīḥ svargatānāṃ sā dīkṣā sā yajñayājinām ..
buddhirbuddhimatāṃ devī kṣamā devī kṣamāvatām .. 21 ..
1.41.d:
स्वर्गश्रीः स्वर्गतानां सा दीक्षा सा यज्ञयाजिनाम् ॥
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतां देवी क्षमा देवी क्षमावताम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.41.m: She is the heavenly fortune of those who have reached heaven; she is the initiation of sacrifice-performers; / she is the goddess of discernment among the discerning, and the goddess of forgiveness among the forgiving.

1.41.s:
śikhā vahnau prabhā sūrye jyotsnā candre prakīrtitā ..
kāntistārāgaṇasyoktā sā siddhiḥ sarvakarmaṇām .. 22 ..
1.41.d:
शिखा वह्नौ प्रभा सूर्ये ज्योत्स्ना चन्द्रे प्रकीर्तिता ॥
कान्तिस्तारागणस्योक्ता सा सिद्धिः सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.41.m: She is proclaimed as the flame in fire, radiance in the sun, moonlight in the moon, / the splendour of the stars, and the success of all undertakings.

1.41.s:
sahasranetrajā dṛṣṭiḥ sahasranayanasya sā ..
upatyakā parvatānāṃ phalaśrīḥ sā ca śākhinām .. 23 ..
1.41.d:
सहस्रनेत्रजा दृष्टिः सहस्रनयनस्य सा ॥
उपत्यका पर्वतानां फलश्रीः सा च शाखिनाम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.41.m: She is the thousand-eyed vision of the thousand-eyed [Indra], / the valley of mountains, and the wealth of fruit on trees.

1.41.s:
mahodadheśca sā velā nakṣatrāṇāñca kṛttikā ..
dhanurlatā ca mantrāṇāṃ hetīnāṃ cāpyaserlatā .. 24 ..
1.41.d:
महोदधेश्च सा वेला नक्षत्राणाञ्च कृत्तिका ॥
धनुर्लता च मन्त्राणां हेतीनां चाप्यसेर्लता ॥ 24 ॥
1.41.m: She is the shore of the great ocean and the Kṛttikās among constellations, / the slender bow of mantras, and the creeping blade of swords among weapons.

1.41.s:
gāndhārī sarvavidyānāṃ vṛṣṭiḥ sā jagatītale ..
kārṣakāṇāṃ tathā sītā sasya śobhā mahītale .. 25 ..
1.41.d:
गान्धारी सर्वविद्यानां वृष्टिः सा जगतीतले ॥
कार्षकाणां तथा सीता सस्य शोभा महीतले ॥ 25 ॥
1.41.m: She is the Gāndhārī among all sciences, the rain upon the surface of the earth, / the furrow of farmers, and the beauty of crops on the ground.

1.41.s:
madalekhā ca nāgānāṃ bhogināñca phaṇāvalī ..
ratnāvalī ca śeṣasya dhṛtirbhūmaṇḍalasya sā .. 26 ..
1.41.d:
मदलेखा च नागानां भोगिनाञ्च फणावली ॥
रत्नावली च शेषस्य धृतिर्भूमण्डलस्य सा ॥ 26 ॥
1.41.m: She is the rutting streak of elephants, the row of hoods of serpents, / the row of jewels of Śeṣa, and the support of the earthly orb.

1.41.s:
sā sthitā satataṃ candre bilve nīlotpale vṛṣe ..
kuñjare turage siṃhe khaṅge ca vimale śubhe .. 27 ..
1.41.d:
सा स्थिता सततं चन्द्रे बिल्वे नीलोत्पले वृषे ॥
कुञ्जरे तुरगे सिंहे खङ्गे च विमले शुभे ॥ 27 ॥
1.41.m: She is ever present in the moon, the bilva tree, the blue lotus, the bull, / the elephant, the horse, the lion, and the spotless, auspicious sword;

1.41.s:
cāmare vyajane chatre bhṛṃgāre gomaye vane ..
sahasrakiraṇe sūrye śakre vaiśravaṇe yame .. 28 ..
1.41.d:
चामरे व्यजने छत्रे भृंगारे गोमये वने ॥
सहस्रकिरणे सूर्ये शक्रे वैश्रवणे यमे ॥ 28 ॥
1.41.m: in the fly-whisk, the fan, the umbrella, the water-jar, cow dung, the forest, / in the thousand-rayed sun, Śakra, Vaiśravaṇa, and Yama;

1.41.s:
kamale rajate hemni śaṃkhe bhadrāsane śubhe ..
gomūtre sarpiṣi kṣīre dadhi kṣīraphaleṣu ca .. 29 ..
1.41.d:
कमले रजते हेम्नि शंखे भद्रासने शुभे ॥
गोमूत्रे सर्पिषि क्षीरे दधि क्षीरफलेषु च ॥ 29 ॥
1.41.m: in the lotus, silver, gold, the conch shell, the auspicious throne, / cow's urine, clarified butter, milk, curd, and milky fruits;

1.41.s:
varuṇe ca jalādhyakṣe samudreṣu jaleṣu ca ..
kusumeṣu ca śukleṣu prāsādeṣu siteṣu ca .. 1.41.30 ..
1.41.d:
वरुणे च जलाध्यक्षे समुद्रेषु जलेषु च ॥
कुसुमेषु च शुक्लेषु प्रासादेषु सितेषु च ॥ 1.41.30 ॥
1.41.m: in Varuṇa, the lord of waters, in the oceans and waters, / in white flowers, and in white palaces;

1.41.s:
hutāśane prajvalite pārthive cāruśobhite ..
ratneṣu ca vicitreṣu tathaivāmalakeṣu ca .. 31 ..
1.41.d:
हुताशने प्रज्वलिते पार्थिवे चारुशोभिते ॥
रत्नेषु च विचित्रेषु तथैवामलकेषु च ॥ 31 ॥
1.41.m: in blazing fire, in a beautifully adorned king, / in multicolored jewels, and likewise in āmalaka fruits.

1.41.s:
yathā vyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ devadevena śārṅgiṇā ..
tathā vyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ rājan kṣīrābdhikanyayā .. 32 ..
1.41.d:
यथा व्याप्तं जगत्सर्वं देवदेवेन शार्ङ्गिणा ॥
तथा व्याप्तं जगत्सर्वं राजन् क्षीराब्धिकन्यया ॥ 32 ॥
1.41.m: Just as the entire universe is pervaded by the god of gods who wields the Śārṅga bow, / so too, O king, is the entire universe pervaded by the daughter of the ocean of milk.

1.41.s:
svāyaṃbhuve'ntare devī bhṛgoḥ sā duhitā smṛtā ..
svārociṣe tathā jātā saiva devī hutāśanāt .. 33 ..
1.41.d:
स्वायंभुवेऽन्तरे देवी भृगोः सा दुहिता स्मृता ॥
स्वारोचिषे तथा जाता सैव देवी हुताशनात् ॥ 33 ॥
1.41.m: In the Svāyambhuva manvantara, that goddess was known as the daughter of Bhṛgu; / and in the Svārociṣa, the same goddess was born from fire.

1.41.s:
auttamasyāntare jātā salilādvimalācchubhā ..
tāmasasyāntare rājan bhūtalātsā samutthitā .. 34 ..
1.41.d:
औत्तमस्यान्तरे जाता सलिलाद्विमलाच्छुभा ॥
तामसस्यान्तरे राजन् भूतलात्सा समुत्थिता ॥ 34 ॥
1.41.m: In the manvantara of Auttama, she was born, pure and auspicious, from water; / in the manvantara of Tāmasa, O king, she arose from the earth.

1.41.s:
bilvātsamutthitā devī raivatasyāntare tathā ..
utphullakamalodbhūtā cākṣuṣe'pi tathāntare .. 35 ..
1.41.d:
बिल्वात्समुत्थिता देवी रैवतस्यान्तरे तथा ॥
उत्फुल्लकमलोद्भूता चाक्षुषेऽपि तथान्तरे ॥ 35 ॥
1.41.m: In the manvantara of Raivata, the goddess arose from a bilva tree; / and likewise in the Cākṣuṣa manvantara, she was born from a blooming lotus.

1.41.s:
vaivasvate'ntare jātā tathaivā'mṛtamanthanāt ..
kṣīrābdhijātāṃ tāṃ prāpya hṛdayena janārdanaḥ .. 36 ..
1.41.d:
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे जाता तथैवाऽमृतमन्थनात् ॥
क्षीराब्धिजातां तां प्राप्य हृदयेन जनार्दनः ॥ 36 ॥
1.41.m: In the Vaivasvata manvantara, she was born from the churning of the nectar. / Having obtained her who was born from the ocean of milk, Janārdana / held her against his chest—

1.41.s:
dadhāra durdharāṃ devīṃ trailokye tamṛte prabhum ..
ādāya sā'mṛtaṃ śuddhaṃ śubhamarkakamaṇḍalum .. 37 ..
1.41.d:
दधार दुर्धरां देवीं त्रैलोक्ये तमृते प्रभुम् ॥
आदाय साऽमृतं शुद्धं शुभमर्ककमण्डलुम् ॥ 37 ॥
1.41.m: the goddess hard to bear in the three worlds by anyone except that Lord. / Holding the pure, auspicious nectar in a sun-bright water-pot,

1.41.s:
etasminnantare jāto vaidyo dhanvantaristathā ..
amṛte jātamātre tu daityasaṃghāḥ samākulāḥ .. .. 38 ..
1.41.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे जातो वैद्यो धन्वन्तरिस्तथा ॥
अमृते जातमात्रे तु दैत्यसंघाः समाकुलाः ॥ ॥ 38 ॥
1.41.m: at that moment the physician Dhanvantari was born. / But as soon as the nectar appeared, the hosts of Daityas were agitated.

1.41.s:
dhanvantarimathonmathya paribhūya ca devatāḥ ..
amṛtaṃ ca samādāya jagmurdaityā niveśanam .. 39 ..
1.41.d:
धन्वन्तरिमथोन्मथ्य परिभूय च देवताः ॥
अमृतं च समादाय जग्मुर्दैत्या निवेशनम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.41.m: Then, having harassed Dhanvantari and overpowered the deities, / the Daityas seized the nectar and departed for their abode.

1.41.s:
hṛtāmṛtāndevagaṇānvipānānāśvāsya devo bhuvanasya goptā ..
sthāne ca vinyasya girīndramukhyaṃ jagāma devo'suranāthaveśma .. 1.41.40 ..
1.41.d:
हृतामृतान्देवगणान्विपानानाश्वास्य देवो भुवनस्य गोप्ता ॥
स्थाने च विन्यस्य गिरीन्द्रमुख्यं जगाम देवोऽसुरनाथवेश्म ॥ 1.41.40 ॥
1.41.m: Comforting the hosts of gods, whose nectar had been stolen and who were denied their drink, / the god who protects the universe, having set the foremost of majestic mountains back in its place, went to the abode of the lord of the Asuras.

1.42.s:
.. rāhuruvāca .. ..
babhūva nārī kalyāṇī sa devo madhusūdanaḥ ..
anirdeśyavayorūpā sarvalakṣaṇapūjitā .. 1 ..
1.42.d:
॥ राहुरुवाच ॥ ॥
बभूव नारी कल्याणी स देवो मधुसूदनः ॥
अनिर्देश्यवयोरूपा सर्वलक्षणपूजिता ॥ 1 ॥
1.42.m: Rāhu said: / That god, the slayer of Madhu, became an auspicious woman / of indescribable youth and form, endowed with every auspicious mark.

1.42.s:
samāṃgulitalau ślakṣṇau raktatuṃganakhā śubhau ..
vibhṛte caraṇau śubhrau gūḍhagulpho manoharau .. .. 2 ..
1.42.d:
समांगुलितलौ श्लक्ष्णौ रक्ततुंगनखा शुभौ ॥
विभृते चरणौ शुभ्रौ गूढगुल्फो मनोहरौ ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
1.42.m: She possessed two feet: charming and fair, with even toes and soles, smooth, / with raised red nails, auspicious, and with ankles concealed.

1.42.s:
jaṃghe manohare śubhre spaṣṭe lomavivarjite ..
gṛhasaṃdhyasthike ślakṣṇe jānunī ca tathā śubhe .. 3 ..
1.42.d:
जंघे मनोहरे शुभ्रे स्पष्टे लोमविवर्जिते ॥
गृहसंध्यस्थिके श्लक्ष्णे जानुनी च तथा शुभे ॥ 3 ॥
1.42.m: Her shanks were captivating, fair, well-proportioned, free of hair, / with smooth bones hidden at the joints, and her knees likewise were auspicious.

1.42.s:
ūrū karikarākārau kadalīdalakomalau ..
ghanamābhogi jaghanaṃ madhyaṃ kuliśasannibham .. 4 ..
1.42.d:
ऊरू करिकराकारौ कदलीदलकोमलौ ॥
घनमाभोगि जघनं मध्यं कुलिशसन्निभम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.42.m: Her thighs were shaped like an elephant's trunk, tender as plantain leaves; / her hips were plump and expansive, and her waist resembled a thunderbolt.

1.42.s:
trivalītripathādhārinābhīpuṣkaramaṃḍitam ..
gūḍhasphike same pārśve samaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ manoramam .. 5 ..
1.42.d:
त्रिवलीत्रिपथाधारिनाभीपुष्करमंडितम् ॥
गूढस्फिके समे पार्श्वे समं पृष्ठं मनोरमम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.42.m: She was adorned with a lotus-like navel holding the three folds [of the belly] like three streams; / her buttocks were concealed, her flanks symmetrical, and her back even and charming.

1.42.s:
samau susaṃhatau pīnau komalāvagracūcukau ..
ābhoginau maṇḍalinau stanau kanakasannibhau .. .. 6 ..
1.42.d:
समौ सुसंहतौ पीनौ कोमलावग्रचूचुकौ ॥
आभोगिनौ मण्डलिनौ स्तनौ कनकसन्निभौ ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
1.42.m: Her breasts were even, closely set, plump, tender, with prominent nipples, / expansive, rounded, and golden in hue.

1.42.s:
mṛṇālasadṛśau bāhū karau komalakomalau ..
kambutulyaṃ śubhaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ connatā ca kṛkāṭikā .. 7 ..
1.42.d:
मृणालसदृशौ बाहू करौ कोमलकोमलौ ॥
कम्बुतुल्यं शुभं कण्ठं चोन्नता च कृकाटिका ॥ 7 ॥
1.42.m: Her arms resembled lotus stalks, and her hands were exceedingly tender; / her throat was auspicious and conch-like, and the nape of her neck was elevated.

1.42.s:
mukhaṃ pūrṇendusaṃkāśaṃ dvijāḥ kundasamaprabhāḥ ..
adharau vidrumākārau nāsā spaṣṭamanoramā .. 8 ..
1.42.d:
मुखं पूर्णेन्दुसंकाशं द्विजाः कुन्दसमप्रभाः ॥
अधरौ विद्रुमाकारौ नासा स्पष्टमनोरमा ॥ 8 ॥
1.42.m: Her face resembled the full moon, her teeth shone like jasmine flowers, / her lips had the shape of coral, and her nose was prominent and charming.

1.42.s:
madhūkapuṣpasaṃkāśau kapolau lalitāvubhau ..
bhrūyugmaṃ kāmacāpāntasadṛśaṃ sumanoharam .. 9 ..
1.42.d:
मधूकपुष्पसंकाशौ कपोलौ ललितावुभौ ॥
भ्रूयुग्मं कामचापान्तसदृशं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.42.m: Both her cheeks were lovely, resembling madhūka blossoms; / her pair of eyebrows, resembling the tips of the bow of Kāma, was exceedingly alluring.

1.42.s:
nātipralambau śravaṇau nātyacārū ca kuṇḍalau ..
cibukaṃ ca manohāri lalāṭaṃ śaśisuprabham .. 1.42.10 ..
1.42.d:
नातिप्रलम्बौ श्रवणौ नात्यचारू च कुण्डलौ ॥
चिबुकं च मनोहारि ललाटं शशिसुप्रभम् ॥ 1.42.10 ॥
1.42.m: Her ears were not overly long, her earrings were exceedingly beautiful, / her chin was captivating, and her forehead had the fair radiance of the moon.

1.42.s:
kṛṣṇamadhye suraktānte nayane śvetabhūmike ..
nīlotpaladalākāre dīrghe cā'timanorame .. 11 ..
1.42.d:
कृष्णमध्ये सुरक्तान्ते नयने श्वेतभूमिके ॥
नीलोत्पलदलाकारे दीर्घे चाऽतिमनोरमे ॥ 11 ॥
1.42.m: Her eyes had black centres, bright red corners, and white sclera; / shaped like blue lotus petals, they were long and exceedingly charming.

1.42.s:
kokilā'likulākāraṃ bhinnāñjanacayaprabham ..
keśapāśaṃ tathā kiṃciddadhāra kuṭilaṃ śubham .. 12 ..
1.42.d:
कोकिलाऽलिकुलाकारं भिन्नाञ्जनचयप्रभम् ॥
केशपाशं तथा किंचिद्दधार कुटिलं शुभम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.42.m: She bore an auspicious mass of hair that was slightly curly, / having the hue of a cuckoo or a swarm of bees, and glowing like crushed collyrium.

1.42.s: candraraśmiprakāśena vastrayugmena bhūṣitā .. 13
1.42.d: चन्द्ररश्मिप्रकाशेन वस्त्रयुग्मेन भूषिता ॥ 13
1.42.m: She was adorned with a pair of garments shining like moonbeams.

1.42.s:
rūpeṇāpratimā rājansarvālaṃkārabhūṣitā ..
yatrayatra padanyāsaṃ karoti gajagāminī .. 14 ..
1.42.d:
रूपेणाप्रतिमा राजन्सर्वालंकारभूषिता ॥
यत्रयत्र पदन्यासं करोति गजगामिनी ॥ 14 ॥
1.42.m: Incomparable in beauty, O king, and adorned with every ornament, / wherever that woman who walked like an elephant placed her foot,

1.42.s:
tatra tatraiva vasudhā sapadmevopalakṣyate ..
yatrayatrā'timadhurāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ kṣipati bhāmini .. 15 ..
1.42.d:
तत्र तत्रैव वसुधा सपद्मेवोपलक्ष्यते ॥
यत्रयत्राऽतिमधुरां दृष्टिं क्षिपति भामिनि ॥ 15 ॥
1.42.m: there indeed the earth appeared as though covered with lotuses; / and wherever that lovely woman cast her exceedingly sweet glance,

1.42.s:
sitāsitotpalaistatra kiratīva vasuṃdharām ..
yatrayatra sthitā bhāti deśe kanakavarṇinī .. 16 ..
1.42.d:
सितासितोत्पलैस्तत्र किरतीव वसुंधराम् ॥
यत्रयत्र स्थिता भाति देशे कनकवर्णिनी ॥ 16 ॥
1.42.m: there she seemed to strew the earth with white and blue lotuses; / and in whatever place that golden-complexioned woman stood shining,

1.42.s:
tatra tatraiva sauvarṇaṃ sā karoti nabhastalam ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṃgī manmathāviṣṭacetasaḥ .. 17 ..
1.42.d:
तत्र तत्रैव सौवर्णं सा करोति नभस्तलम् ॥
तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वांगी मन्मथाविष्टचेतसः ॥ 17 ॥
1.42.m: there indeed she turned the vault of the sky golden. / Seeing her whose every limb was beautiful, their minds overcome by desire,

1.42.s:
prahlādarahitāḥ sarve babhūvurdānavāstadā ..
pādayoḥ pṛthivīṃ tasyā dhṛtiṃ devīṃ ca jaṅghayoḥ ..18..
1.42.d:
प्रह्लादरहिताः सर्वे बभूवुर्दानवास्तदा ॥
पादयोः पृथिवीं तस्या धृतिं देवीं च जङ्घयोः ॥18॥
1.42.m: all the Dānavas then became devoid of joy [except Prahlāda]. / Prahlāda saw the earth in her two feet, the goddess Dhṛti in her shanks,

1.42.s:
jānubhyāṃ ca tathā kṣāntiṃ kāntimūruyuge śubhe ..
āyatiṃ niyatiṃ lakṣmīṃ velāṃ tu jaghane tathā ..19..
1.42.d:
जानुभ्यां च तथा क्षान्तिं कान्तिमूरुयुगे शुभे ॥
आयतिं नियतिं लक्ष्मीं वेलां तु जघने तथा ॥19॥
1.42.m: and likewise Kṣānti in her knees, beauty in her two auspicious thighs, / Āyati, Niyati, Lakṣmī, and Velā in her hips,

1.42.s:
madhye vāhāṃ satīṃ pṛṣṭhe pārśvayośca sudhāṃ mukhe ..
ratiṃ prītiṃ kucayuge kaṇṭhe vāṇīṃ tathaiva ca .. 1.42.20 ..
1.42.d:
मध्ये वाहां सतीं पृष्ठे पार्श्वयोश्च सुधां मुखे ॥
रतिं प्रीतिं कुचयुगे कण्ठे वाणीं तथैव च ॥ 1.42.20 ॥
1.42.m: Vāhā in her waist, Satī on her back, nectar in her cheeks and mouth, / Rati and Prīti upon her pair of breasts, and speech in her throat;

1.42.s:
jayāṃ ca vijayāṃ caiva karayorbhujayostathā ..
śobhāṃ prabhāṃ vakṣasi ca śriyaṃ devīṃ manoramām .. 21 ..
1.42.d:
जयां च विजयां चैव करयोर्भुजयोस्तथा ॥
शोभां प्रभां वक्षसि च श्रियं देवीं मनोरमाम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.42.m: Jayā and Vijayā in her hands and arms, / Śobhā, Prabhā, and the charming goddess Śrī upon her chest;

1.42.s:
arundhatīṃ ca cibuke jihvāyāṃ ca sarasvatīm ..
jyotsnāṃ kapolayordevīṃ nidrāṃ netrayuge tathā .. 22 ..
1.42.d:
अरुन्धतीं च चिबुके जिह्वायां च सरस्वतीम् ॥
ज्योत्स्नां कपोलयोर्देवीं निद्रां नेत्रयुगे तथा ॥ 22 ॥
1.42.m: Arundhatī on her chin, Sarasvatī on her tongue, / the goddess Jyotsnā on her cheeks, and Nidrā in her pair of eyes;

1.42.s:
keśapāśe tathā rātriṃ diśaṃ śrotrayuge tathā ..
bhadrakālīṃ lalāṭe ca nāsāyāṃ ca tathā śacīm .. 23 ..
1.42.d:
केशपाशे तथा रात्रिं दिशं श्रोत्रयुगे तथा ॥
भद्रकालीं ललाटे च नासायां च तथा शचीम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.42.m: Night in her mass of hair, the directions in her pair of ears, / Bhadrakālī on her forehead, and Śacī on her nose;

1.42.s:
sarvāṅgasandhigā nadyo lomasvatha vanaspatim ..
pārśvayoḥ parvatāścaiva daityeśaḥ sarvadevatāḥ .. 24 ..
1.42.d:
सर्वाङ्गसन्धिगा नद्यो लोमस्वथ वनस्पतिम् ॥
पार्श्वयोः पर्वताश्चैव दैत्येशः सर्वदेवताः ॥ 24 ॥
1.42.m: rivers in all the joints of her limbs, trees in her body hairs, / and mountains on her flanks—that lord of the Daityas [saw] all the deities.

1.42.s:
dṛṣṭavānstrītanuṃ tatra prahlādo'rikulāntakaḥ ..
viśvarūpadharāṃ dṛṣṭvā prahlādastāśca yoṣitam .. 25 ..
1.42.d:
दृष्टवान्स्त्रीतनुं तत्र प्रह्लादोऽरिकुलान्तकः ॥
विश्वरूपधरां दृष्ट्वा प्रह्लादस्ताश्च योषितम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.42.m: Prahlāda, the slayer of hosts of foes, saw that female form; / seeing that woman who bore the universal form, Prahlāda...

1.42.s:
viṣṇuṃ matvā viśālākṣīṃ jñātvā caivā'mṛtārthinīm ..
kāmārttadaityānumataḥ prahlādo daityasattama .. 26 ..
1.42.d:
विष्णुं मत्वा विशालाक्षीं ज्ञात्वा चैवाऽमृतार्थिनीम् ॥
कामार्त्तदैत्यानुमतः प्रह्लादो दैत्यसत्तम ॥ 26 ॥
1.42.m: Recognising that wide-eyed one as Viṣṇu and knowing she desired the nectar, / approved by the lust-afflicted daityas, Prahlāda, best of daityas,

1.42.s:
pradadāvamṛtaṃ tasyai praṇipatya prasādya ca ..
strīrūpamāsthitaidevaistrailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 27 ..
1.42.d:
प्रददावमृतं तस्यै प्रणिपत्य प्रसाद्य च ॥
स्त्रीरूपमास्थितैदेवैस्त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.42.m: bowed down, propitiated her, and gave the nectar to her. / Taking on a female form, by the gods the three worlds with mobile and immobile beings

1.42.s:
strīceṣṭamabhavatsarvaṃ tasminkāla upasthite ..
uvāca sā strī prahrādaṃ daitya tvamamṛtaṃ vinā .. 28 ..
1.42.d:
स्त्रीचेष्टमभवत्सर्वं तस्मिन्काल उपस्थिते ॥
उवाच सा स्त्री प्रह्रादं दैत्य त्वममृतं विना ॥ 28 ॥
1.42.m: all became moved by the woman, when that time arrived. / That woman spoke to Prahlāda: "O daitya, even without the nectar,

1.42.s:
brāhmamekamaha saumya jīvitānna vimokṣyase ..
yoddhumabhyuditā daityadevairditijakāraṇāt .. 29 ..
1.42.d:
ब्राह्ममेकमह सौम्य जीवितान्न विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
योद्धुमभ्युदिता दैत्यदेवैर्दितिजकारणात् ॥ 29 ॥
1.42.m: you will not be parted from life for one single day of Brahmā, gentle one. / The daityas have risen up to fight with the gods on account of Diti’s sons;

1.42.s:
na prabodhyāstamoyuktāstvayā daitya janārdanā ..
bhaktosi me sadā vatsa sadaiva vijitendriyaḥ .. 1.42.30 ..
1.42.d:
न प्रबोध्यास्तमोयुक्तास्त्वया दैत्य जनार्दना ॥
भक्तोसि मे सदा वत्स सदैव विजितेन्द्रियः ॥ 1.42.30 ॥
1.42.m: engrossed in darkness, they must not be awakened by you, O daitya Janārdana! / You are always devoted to me, my child, and forever self-controlled.

1.42.s:
tena te darśitā saumya prakṛtiryā parā mama ..
ityevamuktvā prahlādaṃ somamādāya satvarā .. 31 ..
1.42.d:
तेन ते दर्शिता सौम्य प्रकृतिर्या परा मम ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा प्रह्लादं सोममादाय सत्वरा ॥ 31 ॥
1.42.m: Therefore my supreme nature has been revealed to you, gentle one." / Having thus spoken to Prahlāda and swiftly taken the soma,

1.42.s:
kāmārttānditijām̐styaktvā jagāma suramandiram ..
strīrūpaṃ tatra saṃtyajya devarūpamupāśritaḥ .. 32 ..
1.42.d:
कामार्त्तान्दितिजाम्̐स्त्यक्त्वा जगाम सुरमन्दिरम् ॥
स्त्रीरूपं तत्र संत्यज्य देवरूपमुपाश्रितः ॥ 32 ॥
1.42.m: she abandoned the passion-stricken sons of Diti and went to the dwelling of the gods. / Renouncing the female form there, adopting the divine form,

1.42.s:
pāyayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ surānsarvānsamāhitān ..
mayā'pi madhye devānāṃ pītaṃ tatsūryarūpiṇā .. 33 ..
1.42.d:
पाययामास तत्सर्वं सुरान्सर्वान्समाहितान् ॥
मयाऽपि मध्ये देवानां पीतं तत्सूर्यरूपिणा ॥ 33 ॥
1.42.m: he made all the gods drink it entirely, attentive [in their ranks]. / In the midst of the gods it was drunk by me as well, assuming the form of the sun.

1.42.s:
ādityarūpe daityo'yaṃ jñāto'haṃ śaśibhāskaraiḥ ..
niveditaśca devāya tenā'pi laghukāriṇā .. 34 ..
1.42.d:
आदित्यरूपे दैत्योऽयं ज्ञातोऽहं शशिभास्करैः ॥
निवेदितश्च देवाय तेनाऽपि लघुकारिणा ॥ 34 ॥
1.42.m: "This is a daitya in the form of the sun!"—I was recognized by the moon and the sun, / and reported to the god, who was swift to act.

1.42.s:
cakreṇa pātitaṃ vatsa sabhujaṃ mastakaṃ mama ..
amṛtaprāśanātprāṇairna viyukto'smi dānava .. 35 ..
1.42.d:
चक्रेण पातितं वत्स सभुजं मस्तकं मम ॥
अमृतप्राशनात्प्राणैर्न वियुक्तोऽस्मि दानव ॥ 35 ॥
1.42.m: With his discus, my child, my head along with my arms was struck down. / Because I had tasted the nectar, I was not separated from my life, O dānava.

1.42.s:
na me kaṇṭhādadhobhāgamāgataṃ mama cakriṇā ..
śiracchinnaṃ mahārāja tatra prāṇāstataḥ sthitāḥ .. 36 ..
1.42.d:
न मे कण्ठादधोभागमागतं मम चक्रिणा ॥
शिरच्छिन्नं महाराज तत्र प्राणास्ततः स्थिताः ॥ 36 ॥
1.42.m: It had not descended below my throat when my head was severed / by the Discus-bearer, O great king; therefore my vital breaths remained there.

1.42.s:
śirasaśchedanāddīnaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā madhusūdanaḥ ..
jātānukampo bhagavānidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 37 ..
1.42.d:
शिरसश्छेदनाद्दीनं मां दृष्ट्वा मधुसूदनः ॥
जातानुकम्पो भगवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 37 ॥
1.42.m: Seeing me wretched from the severing of my head, Madhusūdana, / the blessed Lord, filled with compassion, spoke these words:

1.42.s:
pītāmṛtasya daityasya maraṇaṃ nā'sti karhicit ..
mama hastavinaṣṭānāṃ gatirbhavati śobhanā .. 38 ..
1.42.d:
पीतामृतस्य दैत्यस्य मरणं नाऽस्ति कर्हिचित् ॥
मम हस्तविनष्टानां गतिर्भवति शोभना ॥ 38 ॥
1.42.m: "For a daitya who has drunk the nectar there is never death; / and those slain by my hand attain an auspicious destiny.

1.42.s:
amaratvaṃ tvamāsādya varaṃ varaya kāṃkṣitam ..
tato mayokto bhagavānpraṇamya madhusūdanaḥ .. .. 39 ..
1.42.d:
अमरत्वं त्वमासाद्य वरं वरय कांक्षितम् ॥
ततो मयोक्तो भगवान्प्रणम्य मधुसूदनः ॥ ॥ 39 ॥
1.42.m: Having attained immortality, choose the boon you desire!" / Then the blessed Madhusūdana was addressed by me with a bow:

1.42.s:
labheyātāṃ hi somārkau matto deva parābhavam ..
pūjāñca prārthaye lokādgrahatvañca janārdana .. 1.42.40 ..
1.42.d:
लभेयातां हि सोमार्कौ मत्तो देव पराभवम् ॥
पूजाञ्च प्रार्थये लोकाद्ग्रहत्वञ्च जनार्दन ॥ 1.42.40 ॥
1.42.m: "May the moon and sun suffer defeat at my hands, O Lord! / And I request worship from the world, and the status of a planet, O Janārdana!"

1.42.s:
evamuktaḥ sa bhagavānmāmuvāca tadā hariḥ ..
grahatvaṃ bhavitā daitya pūjāṃ caivopalapsyase .. 41 ..
1.42.d:
एवमुक्तः स भगवान्मामुवाच तदा हरिः ॥
ग्रहत्वं भविता दैत्य पूजां चैवोपलप्स्यसे ॥ 41 ॥
1.42.m: Thus addressed, the blessed Lord Hari then said to me: / "The status of a planet will be yours, O daitya, and you shall obtain worship.

1.42.s: parvakāle ca saṃprāpte candrārkau chādayiṣyati .. 42 ..
1.42.d: पर्वकाले च संप्राप्ते चन्द्रार्कौ छादयिष्यति ॥ 42 ॥
1.42.m: And when the time of the syzygy arrives, you will overshadow the moon and the sun.

1.42.s:
tamo mūrttiradṛśyaśca viparītaṃ cariṣyasi..
bhūmicchāyāgataścandraṃ candrago'rkaṃ ca dānavaḥ ..43..
1.42.d:
तमो मूर्त्तिरदृश्यश्च विपरीतं चरिष्यसि॥
भूमिच्छायागतश्चन्द्रं चन्द्रगोऽर्कं च दानवः ॥43॥
1.42.m: A form of darkness and invisible, you will move in reverse: / entering the earth’s shadow [you will eclipse] the moon, and going to the moon [you will eclipse] the sun, O dānava.

1.42.s:
yasyodayiṣyasi yadā tadā bhāgamavāpsyasi ..
snāne jāpye tathā home dāne śrāddhe surārcane .. 44 ..
1.42.d:
यस्योदयिष्यसि यदा तदा भागमवाप्स्यसि ॥
स्नाने जाप्ये तथा होमे दाने श्राद्धे सुरार्चने ॥ 44 ॥
1.42.m: Whichever [luminary] you rise against and when, then you will receive your share / during bathing, chanting of mantras, fire sacrifices, gift-giving, ancestral rites, and worship of the gods.

1.42.s:
puṇyaḥ sa kālo bhavitā nityamevā'sureśvara ..
evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstatraivāntaradhīyata ..45..
1.42.d:
पुण्यः स कालो भविता नित्यमेवाऽसुरेश्वर ॥
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥45॥
1.42.m: That time will always be auspicious, O lord of the asuras." / Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord vanished right there.

1.42.s:
pīta śeṣamathādāya saumaṃ suragaṇeśvaraḥ ..
suraloke sannihitaṃ cakāra balavṛtrahā..46..
1.42.d:
पीत शेषमथादाय सौमं सुरगणेश्वरः ॥
सुरलोके सन्निहितं चकार बलवृत्रहा॥46॥
1.42.m: Then taking the remainder of the soma that had been drunk, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, / the lord of the hosts of gods, placed it safely in the realm of the gods.

1.42.s:
macchīrṣapātābhivivṛddhakopā hṛtā'mṛtā daityagaṇāḥ samastāḥ ..
vyarthabhramā devagaṇānnihantuṃ sannaddhasainyāḥ prayayustadānīm ..47..
1.42.d:
मच्छीर्षपाताभिविवृद्धकोपा हृताऽमृता दैत्यगणाः समस्ताः ॥
व्यर्थभ्रमा देवगणान्निहन्तुं सन्नद्धसैन्याः प्रययुस्तदानीम् ॥47॥
1.42.m: Their fury heightened by the falling of my head, deprived of the nectar, their delusion in vain, / all the hosts of daityas, with their armies arrayed, then marched out to slay the hosts of gods.

1.43.s:
.. rāhuruvāca ..
balibāṇamahākūrma śambarāvartabhīṣaṇam ..
anuhrādamahāgrāhaṃ kālakeyamahājalam .. 1 ..
1.43.d:
॥ राहुरुवाच ॥
बलिबाणमहाकूर्म शम्बरावर्तभीषणम् ॥
अनुह्रादमहाग्राहं कालकेयमहाजलम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.43.m: Rāhu said: / With Bali and Bāṇa as its great turtles, terrifying with Śambara as its whirlpool, / with Anuhrāda as its great sea monster, with the Kālakeyas as its vast waters,

1.43.s:
hiraṇyākṣamahāratnaṃ prahrādācalaniścalam ..
tathā namucikallolaṃ hrādasaṃhrādaśabdavat ..2..
1.43.d:
हिरण्याक्षमहारत्नं प्रह्रादाचलनिश्चलम् ॥
तथा नमुचिकल्लोलं ह्रादसंह्रादशब्दवत् ॥2॥
1.43.m: with Hiraṇyākṣa as its great jewel, motionless with Prahlāda as its mountain, / with Namuci as its wave, resounding with the cries of Hrāda and Saṃhrāda,

1.43.s:
hiraṇyakaśipūdyotaṃ kālanemibalāhakam ..
amṛtāharaṇakṣubdhaṃ tadā daityamahārṇavam 3 ..
1.43.d:
हिरण्यकशिपूद्योतं कालनेमिबलाहकम् ॥
अमृताहरणक्षुब्धं तदा दैत्यमहार्णवम् 3 ॥
1.43.m: with Hiraṇyakaśipu as its splendor, with Kālanemi as its cloud— / thus agitated by the theft of the nectar was the great ocean of the daityas.

1.43.s:
kṣubdhaṃ daityārṇavaṃ śrutvā nirgataṃ samarāya ca ..
niryayustridaśāḥ sarve sannaddhā yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ .. 4 ..
1.43.d:
क्षुब्धं दैत्यार्णवं श्रुत्वा निर्गतं समराय च ॥
निर्ययुस्त्रिदशाः सर्वे सन्नद्धा युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ 4 ॥
1.43.m: Hearing that the ocean of daityas was stirred and had set forth for battle, / all the thirty gods came out in full armor, longing for war.

1.43.s:
tataḥ pravartate yuddhaṃ ghoraṃ bhīrubhayaṃkaram ..
devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca parasparavadhaiṣiṇām..5..
1.43.d:
ततः प्रवर्तते युद्धं घोरं भीरुभयंकरम् ॥
देवानां दानवानां च परस्परवधैषिणाम्॥5॥
1.43.m: Then began a fierce battle, terrifying to cowards, / between the gods and the dānavas, who sought to slay one another.

1.43.s:
pātyamāneṣu śastreṣu kavaceṣu mahātmanām..
devānāṃ dānavānāñca hyutpeturjvalanārciṣaḥ ..6..
1.43.d:
पात्यमानेषु शस्त्रेषु कवचेषु महात्मनाम्॥
देवानां दानवानाञ्च ह्युत्पेतुर्ज्वलनार्चिषः ॥6॥
1.43.m: As weapons fell upon the armor of the great-souled / gods and dānavas, flames of fire indeed flew up.

1.43.s:
gajavājikhurakṣuṇṇamuttasthau sumahadrajaḥ ..
yugāntānaladhūmābhaṃ trailokasyeva dahyataḥ .. 7 ..
1.43.d:
गजवाजिखुरक्षुण्णमुत्तस्थौ सुमहद्रजः ॥
युगान्तानलधूमाभं त्रैलोकस्येव दह्यतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.43.m: A vast dust arose, pounded up by the hooves of elephants and horses, / resembling the smoke of the fire at the end of the aeon, as if the three worlds were burning.

1.43.s:
tasminpravṛtte rajasi ghore bhīrubhayaṃkare ..
nirmaryādamabhūdyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha..8..
1.43.d:
तस्मिन्प्रवृत्ते रजसि घोरे भीरुभयंकरे ॥
निर्मर्यादमभूद्युद्धं देवानां दानवैः सह॥8॥
1.43.m: When that terrifying dust arose, striking fear into the faint-hearted, / an unrestricted battle took place between the gods and the dānavas.

1.43.s:
tato daityasamutthena tathā devodbhavena ca ..
rudhireṇa mahī vyāptā praśāntañca rajaḥ kṣaṇāt..9..
1.43.d:
ततो दैत्यसमुत्थेन तथा देवोद्भवेन च ॥
रुधिरेण मही व्याप्ता प्रशान्तञ्च रजः क्षणात्॥9॥
1.43.m: Then with the blood pouring from the daityas as well as that arising from the gods, / the earth was covered, and the dust was quelled in an instant.

1.43.s:
dhvaje cchatre rathe nāge cāmare vyajane haye..
sarvatra dṛśyate daityaraktaṃ lākṣārasaprabham ..1.43.10 ..
1.43.d:
ध्वजे च्छत्रे रथे नागे चामरे व्यजने हये॥
सर्वत्र दृश्यते दैत्यरक्तं लाक्षारसप्रभम् ॥1.43.10 ॥
1.43.m: On banners, parasols, chariots, elephants, chowries, fans, and horses, / everywhere was seen the blood of the daityas, radiant as liquid red lac.

1.43.s:
tasminyuddhe mahāraudre daityadānavanāśane ..
babhramuḥ kuñjarā mattā mahāmātrapracoditāḥ ..11..
1.43.d:
तस्मिन्युद्धे महारौद्रे दैत्यदानवनाशने ॥
बभ्रमुः कुञ्जरा मत्ता महामात्रप्रचोदिताः ॥11॥
1.43.m: In that most dreadful battle, which brought destruction to daityas and dānavas, / rutting elephants roamed about, urged on by their mahouts.

1.43.s:
hatairvīraistathai vā'nyaiḥ kuñjarāḥ parvatopamāḥ ..
kurvantaḥ svānyanīkāni dṛśyante śataśo raṇe .. 12 ..
1.43.d:
हतैर्वीरैस्तथै वाऽन्यैः कुञ्जराः पर्वतोपमाः ॥
कुर्वन्तः स्वान्यनीकानि दृश्यन्ते शतशो रणे ॥ 12 ॥
1.43.m: By other heroes slain, mountain-like elephants / were seen by the hundreds on the battlefield, throwing their own battle ranks into disorder.

1.43.s:
chinnadantā bhinnadhvajā vihastacaraṇāstathā ..
śailābhāpatitāstatra śobhayanto raṇājiram .. 13 ..
1.43.d:
छिन्नदन्ता भिन्नध्वजा विहस्तचरणास्तथा ॥
शैलाभापतितास्तत्र शोभयन्तो रणाजिरम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.43.m: With broken tusks, shattered banners, and severed trunks and feet, / fallen there like mountains, they adorned the field of battle.

1.43.s:
babhramuḥ sādibhirhīnā hayāḥ sūryahayopamāḥ ..
mṛtāśca śataśastatra dṛśyante vikṛtānanāḥ .. 14 ..
1.43.d:
बभ्रमुः सादिभिर्हीना हयाः सूर्यहयोपमाः ॥
मृताश्च शतशस्तत्र दृश्यन्ते विकृताननाः ॥ 14 ॥
1.43.m: Horses resembling the horses of the sun wandered stripped of their riders, / and dead ones were seen there by the hundreds with disfigured faces.

1.43.s:
āgulphamavasīdanti daityāḥ śoṇitakardame ..
rathibhirnihatā nāgā nāgaiśca nihatā rathāḥ .. 15 ..
1.43.d:
आगुल्फमवसीदन्ति दैत्याः शोणितकर्दमे ॥
रथिभिर्निहता नागा नागैश्च निहता रथाः ॥ 15 ॥
1.43.m: The daityas sank ankle-deep in the mire of blood; / elephants were slain by charioteers, and chariots were smashed by elephants.

1.43.s:
hayāśca viddhā nāgaistu sādibhiḥ kuñjarā hatāḥ ..
rathasādigajārohairnihatāśca padātayaḥ ..16..
1.43.d:
हयाश्च विद्धा नागैस्तु सादिभिः कुञ्जरा हताः ॥
रथसादिगजारोहैर्निहताश्च पदातयः ॥16॥
1.43.m: Horses were pierced by elephants, and elephants were slain by horsemen; / and foot soldiers were slain by charioteers, horsemen, and elephant riders.

1.43.s:
pattinā mahatā sādī kuñjaro ratha eva ca ..
tataḥ prāvartata nadī rudhiraughataraṅgiṇī ..17..
1.43.d:
पत्तिना महता सादी कुञ्जरो रथ एव च ॥
ततः प्रावर्तत नदी रुधिरौघतरङ्गिणी ॥17॥
1.43.m: A horseman, an elephant, and even a chariot [were brought down] by a single mighty foot soldier. / Then there surged forth a river undulating with torrents of blood,

1.43.s:
astragrāhā dhanurmīnā cakrakūrmā mahāsvarā ..
chatrahaṃsā nāgavatī keśaśaivalaśādvalā .. 18 ..
1.43.d:
अस्त्रग्राहा धनुर्मीना चक्रकूर्मा महास्वरा ॥
छत्रहंसा नागवती केशशैवलशाद्वला ॥ 18 ॥
1.43.m: with missiles for crocodiles, bows for fish, and discuses for tortoises, roaring loudly, / with parasols for swans, elephants for banks, and hair for moss and water-grass,

1.43.s:
daityaśīrṣopalā raudrā tathā bhīrubhayāvahā ..
bāhusarpā mahāvartā śarāṇāṃ harṣavarddhinī .. 19 ..
1.43.d:
दैत्यशीर्षोपला रौद्रा तथा भीरुभयावहा ॥
बाहुसर्पा महावर्ता शराणां हर्षवर्द्धिनी ॥ 19 ॥
1.43.m: with daitya heads for stones, terrible and terrifying to the faint-hearted, / with arms for serpents, great whirlpools, gladdening [the wielders] of arrows,

1.43.s:
apāragamyā pattīnāṃ phenapuñjasamākulā ..
tasminyuddhe mahāghore tumule lomaharṣaṇe .. 1.43.20 ..
1.43.d:
अपारगम्या पत्तीनां फेनपुञ्जसमाकुला ॥
तस्मिन्युद्धे महाघोरे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे ॥ 1.43.20 ॥
1.43.m: impassable to foot soldiers, crowded with masses of foam, / in that battle exceedingly terrible, chaotic, and hair-raising.

1.43.s:
ākīrṇā vasudhā bhāti vadanaiḥ kamalopamaiḥ ..
vivṛttaiśca mahādaṃṣṭairdānavānāṃ mahātmanām .. 21 ..
1.43.d:
आकीर्णा वसुधा भाति वदनैः कमलोपमैः ॥
विवृत्तैश्च महादंष्टैर्दानवानां महात्मनाम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.43.m: The earth shone strewn with faces resembling lotuses / and with rolled-back eyes and huge fangs of the great-souled dānavas,

1.43.s:
bāhubhiścāṅgadaiścaiva raktacandanarūṣitaiḥ ..
hastihastairmahāprāsairasibhiśca mahādhanaiḥ .. 22 ..
1.43.d:
बाहुभिश्चाङ्गदैश्चैव रक्तचन्दनरूषितैः ॥
हस्तिहस्तैर्महाप्रासैरसिभिश्च महाधनैः ॥ 22 ॥
1.43.m: and with arms wearing armlets and smeared with red sandalwood, / with elephant trunks, huge spears, swords, and magnificent bows.

1.43.s:
tālavṛntaistathā chatraiścāmarairyaṣṭibhistathā..
mukuṭaiḥ kuṇḍalaiścaiva śuśubhe bhūrvibhūṣitā ..23..
1.43.d:
तालवृन्तैस्तथा छत्रैश्चामरैर्यष्टिभिस्तथा॥
मुकुटैः कुण्डलैश्चैव शुशुभे भूर्विभूषिता ॥23॥
1.43.m: With palm-leaf fans and umbrellas, with chowries and poles, / and with diadems and ear-rings, the earth shone adorned.

1.43.s:
tataste dānavāḥ kruddhāḥ svayuddhena dievepsavaḥ ..
abhidravanti deveśaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ puraṃdaram..24..
1.43.d:
ततस्ते दानवाः क्रुद्धाः स्वयुद्धेन दिएवेप्सवः ॥
अभिद्रवन्ति देवेशं सहस्राक्षं पुरंदरम्॥24॥
1.43.m: Then those Dānavas, enraged and desiring to conquer heaven in their own combat, / rushed against the lord of the gods, the thousand-eyed Puraṃdara.

1.43.s:
daityānāṃ patatāṃ dṛṣṭvā prahrādaṃ devasūdanam..
pratyudyayau gajenā ''jau devarājo mahābalaḥ .. 25 ..
1.43.d:
दैत्यानां पततां दृष्ट्वा प्रह्रादं देवसूदनम्॥
प्रत्युद्ययौ गजेना 'ऽजौ देवराजो महाबलः ॥ 25 ॥
1.43.m: Seeing Prahrāda, the destroyer of gods, rushing forth among the charging Daityas, / the king of the gods, of great might, advanced on an elephant in battle.

1.43.s:
hutāśano'pi namucimanuhrādaṃ tathā śaśī..
varuṇaśca tathā bāṇaṃ yamo devastathā balim ..26..
1.43.d:
हुताशनोऽपि नमुचिमनुह्रादं तथा शशी॥
वरुणश्च तथा बाणं यमो देवस्तथा बलिम् ॥26॥
1.43.m: Fire [advanced] against Namuci, and the Moon likewise against Anuhrāda, / Varuṇa likewise against Bāṇa, and the god Yama against Bali.

1.43.s:
hiraṇyakaśipuṃ rudro vāyurvṛtrāsuraṃ raṇe ..
virūpākṣaṃ tathā śaṃbhurhiraṇyākṣaṃ dhaneśvaraḥ ..27..
1.43.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुं रुद्रो वायुर्वृत्रासुरं रणे ॥
विरूपाक्षं तथा शंभुर्हिरण्याक्षं धनेश्वरः ॥27॥
1.43.m: Rudra against Hiraṇyakaśipu, Vāyu against the asura Vṛtra in battle, / Śaṃbhu likewise against Virūpākṣa, and the lord of wealth against Hiraṇyākṣa.

1.43.s:
anye ca daityāḥ śataśaḥ saṃyuktā devatāgaṇaiḥ ..
dvandvayuddhasahasreṣu teṣvavartata dānavaiḥ .. 28 ..
1.43.d:
अन्ये च दैत्याः शतशः संयुक्ता देवतागणैः ॥
द्वन्द्वयुद्धसहस्रेषु तेष्ववर्तत दानवैः ॥ 28 ॥
1.43.m: And hundreds of other Daityas were joined with the hosts of deities; / among thousands of single combats it went on with the Dānavas.

1.43.s:
prāyaśo vijitā devā yayurbhagnā diśo daśa ..
dānavāśca jayaṃ labdhvā devānanuyayurbalāt ..29 ..
1.43.d:
प्रायशो विजिता देवा ययुर्भग्ना दिशो दश ॥
दानवाश्च जयं लब्ध्वा देवाननुययुर्बलात् ॥29 ॥
1.43.m: For the most part, the conquered gods fled broken in the ten directions; / and having gained victory, the Dānavas pursued the gods by force.

1.43.s:
te bhagnāstridaśāḥ sarve dānavaiścāpyabhidrutā ..
trāṇārthamatha saṃprāptā naranārāyaṇāśramam .. 1.43.30 ..
1.43.d:
ते भग्नास्त्रिदशाः सर्वे दानवैश्चाप्यभिद्रुता ॥
त्राणार्थमथ संप्राप्ता नरनारायणाश्रमम् ॥ 1.43.30 ॥
1.43.m: All those broken thirty [gods], pursued by the Dānavas, / then reached the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa for protection.

1.43.s:
devānāmabhayaṃ dattvā naranārāyaṇau tadā ..
śaṃkhacakrāyudhadharau yuddhāya samavasthitau .. 31 ..
1.43.d:
देवानामभयं दत्त्वा नरनारायणौ तदा ॥
शंखचक्रायुधधरौ युद्धाय समवस्थितौ ॥ 31 ॥
1.43.m: Having granted safety to the gods, Nara and Nārāyaṇa then, / bearing the weapons of conch and discus, stood ready for battle.

1.43.s:
naranārāyaṇau dṛṣṭvā tatkṣubdhaṃ daityasāgaram ..
sarvāyudhavisargeṇa tayoryuddhaṃ vyavasthitam .. 32 ..
1.43.d:
नरनारायणौ दृष्ट्वा तत्क्षुब्धं दैत्यसागरम् ॥
सर्वायुधविसर्गेण तयोर्युद्धं व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.43.m: Seeing Nara and Nārāyaṇa, that ocean of Daityas was agitated; / their battle was engaged with the discharge of all manner of weapons.

1.43.s:
gajābhrajālasaṃchannaṃ śaradhāraughavarṣaṇam ..
calankhaḍgalatāvidyuddaityadurdinamābabhau .. 33 ..
1.43.d:
गजाभ्रजालसंछन्नं शरधारौघवर्षणम् ॥
चलन्खड्गलताविद्युद्दैत्यदुर्दिनमाबभौ ॥ 33 ॥
1.43.m: Covered by a mass of cloud-like elephants, raining down a torrent of streams of arrows, / with flashing sword-creepers as lightning, the foul weather of Daityas shone forth.

1.43.s:
tataḥ śarai rukmavibhūṣitāgraiḥ sunetrapuṃkhairjvalanārkavarṇaiḥ ..
bibheda gātrāṇi naro ripūṇāṃ jahāra śīrṣāṇi sakuṇḍalāni .. 34 ..
1.43.d:
ततः शरै रुक्मविभूषिताग्रैः सुनेत्रपुंखैर्ज्वलनार्कवर्णैः ॥
बिभेद गात्राणि नरो रिपूणां जहार शीर्षाणि सकुण्डलानि ॥ 34 ॥
1.43.m: Then, with arrows tipped with gold, well-feathered, with the color of fire and the sun, / Nara pierced the limbs of the enemies and cut off their heads adorned with ear-rings.

1.43.s:
nārāyaṇopyuttamavīryatejāścakreṇa cakre ditinandanānām ..
vidārayāmāsa mahānubhāvastasminraṇe ghoratare tadānīm .. 35 ..
1.43.d:
नारायणोप्युत्तमवीर्यतेजाश्चक्रेण चक्रे दितिनन्दनानाम् ॥
विदारयामास महानुभावस्तस्मिन्रणे घोरतरे तदानीम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.43.m: And Nārāyaṇa, of supreme heroism and majesty, with his discus rent the sons of Diti; / the high-souled one tore them asunder in that most terrible battle then.

1.43.s:
vīryaṃ tayorapratimaṃ nirīkṣya te dānavā bhagnanikṛttayodhāḥ ..
hatāmṛtā jīvitamātraśeṣā vegena yātā varuṇādhivāsam ..36 ..
1.43.d:
वीर्यं तयोरप्रतिमं निरीक्ष्य ते दानवा भग्ननिकृत्तयोधाः ॥
हतामृता जीवितमात्रशेषा वेगेन याता वरुणाधिवासम् ॥36 ॥
1.43.m: Beholding their peerless heroism, those Dānavas, their warriors broken and cut down, / their dead left behind, with life alone remaining, swiftly fled to the dwelling of Varuṇa.

1.43.s:
labdhvā jayaṃ devapatirmahātmā prahrādamājau ca tathā vijitya ..
saṃpūjayāmāsa mahānubhāvau dharmātmajau tāpasasaṃghamukhyau .. 37 ..
1.43.d:
लब्ध्वा जयं देवपतिर्महात्मा प्रह्रादमाजौ च तथा विजित्य ॥
संपूजयामास महानुभावौ धर्मात्मजौ तापससंघमुख्यौ ॥ 37 ॥
1.43.m: Having obtained victory and likewise conquered Prahrāda in battle, the high-souled lord of gods / worshipped the two noble sons of Dharma, the foremost of the assembly of ascetics.

1.43.s:
saṃpūjya tau dharmasutau jitārirdevaiḥ prahṛṣṭairanuyāsyamānaḥ ..
jagāma nākaṃ tridaśapradhānaḥ sukhī babhūvātha gatajvaraśca .. 38 ..
1.43.d:
संपूज्य तौ धर्मसुतौ जितारिर्देवैः प्रहृष्टैरनुयास्यमानः ॥
जगाम नाकं त्रिदशप्रधानः सुखी बभूवाथ गतज्वरश्च ॥ 38 ॥
1.43.m: Having worshipped those two sons of Dharma, his enemies conquered, followed by the delighted gods, / the chief of the thirty [gods] went to heaven and became happy, free of sorrow.

1.43.s:
evaṃ prabhāvo bhagavānsa viṣṇurvairaṃ na me rocati tena nityam ..
sandhiṃ kuruṣvā''tmahitāya rājañchakreṇa tenāriniṣūdanena .. 39 ..
1.43.d:
एवं प्रभावो भगवान्स विष्णुर्वैरं न मे रोचति तेन नित्यम् ॥
सन्धिं कुरुष्वा'ऽत्महिताय राजञ्छक्रेण तेनारिनिषूदनेन ॥ 39 ॥
1.43.m: Such is the power of the blessed Viṣṇu; enmity with him does not ever please me. / Make peace, O king, for your own welfare, with Śakra, that destroyer of enemies.

1.44.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
evamuktastadā sālvo rāhuṇā bhīmavikramaḥ ..
jagāda bhrātaraṃ vākyaṃ sārabhūtamahetumat .. 1 ..
1.44.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा साल्वो राहुणा भीमविक्रमः ॥
जगाद भ्रातरं वाक्यं सारभूतमहेतुमत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.44.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed at that time by Rāhu, Sālva of terrible prowess / spoke to his brother words of essential truth, free from irrationality:

1.44.s:
sālva uvāca ..
asāre graha saṃsāre nitye satatayāyini ..
bhavakṣaye matiḥ kāryā rujopakaraṇeṣu vā ..
jantavastrividhā loke tridhā yeṣāṃ viceṣṭitam .. 2 ..
1.44.d:
साल्व उवाच ॥
असारे ग्रह संसारे नित्ये सततयायिनि ॥
भवक्षये मतिः कार्या रुजोपकरणेषु वा ॥
जन्तवस्त्रिविधा लोके त्रिधा येषां विचेष्टितम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.44.m:
Sālva said:
In this worthless saṃsāra, O planet, which is continuous and ever passing away, / one's mind should be directed either to the cessation of existence or to the means for [overcoming] suffering. / Living beings in the world are of three kinds, whose behavior is threefold:

1.44.s:
tāmasārājasāścaiva sāttvikāśca graheśvara ..
bhavakṣaye ye vimukhā bhavopakaraṇeṣu ca .. 3 ..
1.44.d:
तामसाराजसाश्चैव सात्त्विकाश्च ग्रहेश्वर ॥
भवक्षये ये विमुखा भवोपकरणेषु च ॥ 3 ॥
1.44.m: Tāmasic, rājasic, and sāttvic, O lord of planets. / Those who are averse to the cessation of existence and also to the means of existence,

1.44.s:
lokadvitayavibhraṣṭāstāmasāste prakītitāḥ ..
bhavakṣayamatibhraṣṭā bhavopakaraṇe sthitāḥ .. 4 ..
1.44.d:
लोकद्वितयविभ्रष्टास्तामसास्ते प्रकीतिताः ॥
भवक्षयमतिभ्रष्टा भवोपकरणे स्थिताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.44.m: fallen from both worlds, are proclaimed as tāmasic. / Those fallen from the resolution for the cessation of existence and fixed on the means of existence,

1.44.s:
rājasāste vinirdiṣṭā madhyasthāḥ sarvajantuṣu ..
bhavopakaraṇe daitya matiyerṣāṃ na vidyate .. 5 ..
1.44.d:
राजसास्ते विनिर्दिष्टा मध्यस्थाः सर्वजन्तुषु ॥
भवोपकरणे दैत्य मतियेर्षां न विद्यते ॥ 5 ॥
1.44.m: are designated as rājasic, standing in the middle among all living beings. / Those who have no concern for the means of existence, O Daitya,

1.44.s:
bhavakṣaye matiryeṣāṃ sāttvikāste prakīrtitāḥ ..
tāmasatvānmayā daitya matiḥ pūrvaṃ bhavakṣaye .. 6 ..
1.44.d:
भवक्षये मतिर्येषां सात्त्विकास्ते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
तामसत्वान्मया दैत्य मतिः पूर्वं भवक्षये ॥ 6 ॥
1.44.m: and whose mind is set on the cessation of existence, are proclaimed as sāttvic. / Because of my tāmasic nature, O Daitya, previously my mind on the cessation of existence

1.44.s:
na kṛtā tena tapyāmi rājyatantramanuṣṭhitam ..
manvantare'pi sampūrṇe mṛtiryeṣāṃ grahottama .. 7 ..
1.44.d:
न कृता तेन तप्यामि राज्यतन्त्रमनुष्ठितम् ॥
मन्वन्तरेऽपि सम्पूर्णे मृतिर्येषां ग्रहोत्तम ॥ 7 ॥
1.44.m: was not set; therefore I grieve, having administered the system of kingship. / Even at the completion of a manvantara, those who must die, O best of planets,

1.44.s:
udvijantyeva te mṛtyormahanmṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam ..
avaśyaṃ daitya marttavyaṃ sarveṇeha śarīriṇā .. 8 ..
1.44.d:
उद्विजन्त्येव ते मृत्योर्महन्मृत्युकृतं भयम् ॥
अवश्यं दैत्य मर्त्तव्यं सर्वेणेह शरीरिणा ॥ 8 ॥
1.44.m: tremble before death; great is the fear caused by death. / Inevitably, O Daitya, death must be undergone by every embodied being here.

1.44.s:
so'haṃ mokṣaparibhraṣṭaḥ kāmaye keśavādvadham ..
iṣṭaṃ yajñaistapastaptaṃ ripūṇāṃ mūrdhani sthitam .. 9 ..
1.44.d:
सोऽहं मोक्षपरिभ्रष्टः कामये केशवाद्वधम् ॥
इष्टं यज्ञैस्तपस्तप्तं रिपूणां मूर्धनि स्थितम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.44.m: I, who have fallen from liberation, desire death at the hands of Keśava. / Sacrifices have been offered, austerities practiced, and I have stood on the heads of enemies.

1.44.s:
