marttavye ca dhruve gamānmaraṇaṃ kāmayāmyaham ..
saṃprāpya keśavānmṛtyuṃ gatiṃ prāpsyāmyanuttamām .. 1.44.10 ..
1.44.d:
मर्त्तव्ये च ध्रुवे गमान्मरणं कामयाम्यहम् ॥
संप्राप्य केशवान्मृत्युं गतिं प्राप्स्याम्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 1.44.10 ॥
1.44.m: And when death is certain, I desire death through an encounter [with him]. / Having met death from Keśava, I shall attain an unsurpassed state.

1.44.s:
bhūyo rājyamavāpsyāmi nākabhraṣṭo grahottama ..
vivāsya vāsavaṃ svargātparibhūya punaḥpunaḥ .. 11 ..
1.44.d:
भूयो राज्यमवाप्स्यामि नाकभ्रष्टो ग्रहोत्तम ॥
विवास्य वासवं स्वर्गात्परिभूय पुनःपुनः ॥ 11 ॥
1.44.m: Having fallen from heaven, O best of planets, I shall regain kingship once more, / after exiling Vāsava from heaven and humiliating him again and again.

1.44.s:
kathaṃ sandhiṃ kariṣyāmi tenā'haṃ jīvitapriyaḥ ..
praṇāmaṃ deva rājasya keśavānmaraṇaṃ varam ...12..
1.44.d:
कथं सन्धिं करिष्यामि तेनाऽहं जीवितप्रियः ॥
प्रणामं देव राजस्य केशवान्मरणं वरम् ॥.12॥
1.44.m: How can I, fond of life, make peace with him? / Rather than bowing to the king of the gods, death from Keśava is better.

1.44.s:
samīkṣya sādhu paśyāmi keśavānmaraṇaṃ raṇe ..
śakreṇa kṛtasandhānaṃ pātālanilayaṃ tathā .. 13 ..
1.44.d:
समीक्ष्य साधु पश्यामि केशवान्मरणं रणे ॥
शक्रेण कृतसन्धानं पातालनिलयं तथा ॥ 13 ॥
1.44.m: Considering properly, I see death from Keśava in battle as excellent. / Having made an alliance with Śakra and dwelling in the netherworld,

1.44.s:
tyakṣanti māṃ daityagaṇā vṛddhaṃ patimivā'ṅganāḥ ..
divi bhūmau tathā svarge pātāle gagane jale..14..
1.44.d:
त्यक्षन्ति मां दैत्यगणा वृद्धं पतिमिवाऽङ्गनाः ॥
दिवि भूमौ तथा स्वर्गे पाताले गगने जले॥14॥
1.44.m: the hosts of Daityas would abandon me like women an aged husband. / In heaven, on earth, in paradise, in the netherworld, in the sky, or in water,

1.44.s:
dehināṃ mṛtyurabhyeti tasya nā'sti palāyanam ..
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ..15..
1.44.d:
देहिनां मृत्युरभ्येति तस्य नाऽस्ति पलायनम् ॥
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः॥15॥
1.44.m: death approaches embodied beings; there is no running away from it. / All accumulations end in depletion; all lofty rises end in a fall;

1.44.s:
saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam ..
avaśyabhāvinyarthe'sminsarveṣāṃ graha sarvadā .. 16 ..
1.44.d:
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम् ॥
अवश्यभाविन्यर्थेऽस्मिन्सर्वेषां ग्रह सर्वदा ॥ 16 ॥
1.44.m: all unions end in separation; for life ends in death. / In this matter which is unavoidable for everyone at all times, O planet,

1.44.s:
puṇyabhājo hi maraṇaṃ saṃgrāme yadi jāyate ..
so'haṃ kṣatriyadharmeṇa saṃpūjya samare harim .. 17..
1.44.d:
पुण्यभाजो हि मरणं संग्रामे यदि जायते ॥
सोऽहं क्षत्रियधर्मेण संपूज्य समरे हरिम् ॥ 17॥
1.44.m: death is indeed for the meritorious if it happens in battle. / Therefore, worshipping Hari in battle according to the duty of a kṣatriya,

1.44.s:
tasmānmṛtyumanuprāpya gatiṃ prāpsyāmi śobhanām..
naivedyaiḥ puppadhūpādyairna tathā pūjito hariḥ ..18..
1.44.d:
तस्मान्मृत्युमनुप्राप्य गतिं प्राप्स्यामि शोभनाम्॥
नैवेद्यैः पुप्पधूपाद्यैर्न तथा पूजितो हरिः ॥18॥
1.44.m: and attaining death from him, I shall reach an auspicious state. / Hari is not so pleased by offerings of food, flowers, incense, and the like,

1.44.s:
toṣamāyāti daityendra sa dharmeṇa yathā nṛṇām ..
bhrātrā jyeṣṭhena yadvācyaṃ suhṛdā hitamicchatā ..19..
1.44.d:
तोषमायाति दैत्येन्द्र स धर्मेण यथा नृणाम् ॥
भ्रात्रा ज्येष्ठेन यद्वाच्यं सुहृदा हितमिच्छता ॥19॥
1.44.m: as he attains satisfaction, O lord of Daityas, through the [proper] duty of men. / What ought to be said by an elder brother, a friend wishing for one's welfare,

1.44.s:
tadukto'smi tvayā nātha devāttanme na rocate ..
sa tvaṃ gaccha mahābhāga dividraṣṭāsi māṃ punaḥ .. 1.44.20 ..
1.44.d:
तदुक्तोऽस्मि त्वया नाथ देवात्तन्मे न रोचते ॥
स त्वं गच्छ महाभाग दिविद्रष्टासि मां पुनः ॥ 1.44.20 ॥
1.44.m: that has been spoken by you to me, O master; yet because of destiny it does not please me. / Therefore go, O fortunate one; you shall see me again in heaven,

1.44.s:
dehāntaramanuprāptaṃ graha divyena cakṣuṣā ..
..mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
ityeva sālvasya niśamya vākyaṃ kālānurūpaṃ ca tathā viditvā..
na kiñciduktvaiva jagāma rāhurdivaṃ mahātmā jagatāṃ pradhānaḥ ..21..
1.44.d:
देहान्तरमनुप्राप्तं ग्रह दिव्येन चक्षुषा ॥
॥मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
इत्येव साल्वस्य निशम्य वाक्यं कालानुरूपं च तथा विदित्वा॥
न किञ्चिदुक्त्वैव जगाम राहुर्दिवं महात्मा जगतां प्रधानः ॥21॥
1.44.m:
having attained another body, O planet, with your divine eye.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having thus heard the words of Sālva, and recognizing them as suited to the time, / high-souled Rāhu, chief among the worlds, departed for heaven without saying anything at all.

1.45.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
rāhau divamasaṃprāpte sālve rājñi sabhāṃ gate ..
rāmeṇa preṣito dūtaḥ saṃprāptastvakṛtavraṇaḥ .. 1 ..
1.45.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
राहौ दिवमसंप्राप्ते साल्वे राज्ञि सभां गते ॥
रामेण प्रेषितो दूतः संप्राप्तस्त्वकृतव्रणः ॥ 1 ॥
1.45.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Before Rāhu had reached heaven, when King Sālva entered his assembly,
a messenger sent by Rāma arrived, named Akṛtavraṇa.

1.45.s:
sa praviṣṭaḥ sabhāṃ ramyāṃ sālvarājñā ca pūjitaḥ ..
pādyārghyācamanīyādyairniṣaṇṇo vākyamabravīt .. 2 ..
1.45.d:
स प्रविष्टः सभां रम्यां साल्वराज्ञा च पूजितः ॥
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयाद्यैर्निषण्णो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 2 ॥
1.45.m:
Having entered the splendid assembly and been honored by King Sālva
with water for the feet, guest-offering, water for sipping, and other respects, he sat down and spoke these words:

1.45.s:
akṛtavraṇa uvāca ..
dūto'haṃ preṣitaḥ sālva rāmeṇā'kliṣṭakarmmaṇā..
śrutvā rāmasya vacanaṃ tataḥ kuru yathepsitam ..3..
1.45.d:
अकृतव्रण उवाच ॥
दूतोऽहं प्रेषितः साल्व रामेणाऽक्लिष्टकर्म्मणा॥
श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं ततः कुरु यथेप्सितम् ॥3॥
1.45.m:
Akṛtavraṇa said:
I have been sent as a messenger, O Sālva, by Rāma of untiring deeds.
Having heard the words of Rāma, then do as you wish.

1.45.s:
āha tvāṃ bhārgavo rāmastryambakeṇa visarjitaḥ..
tvayā yuddhāya daityendra saṃgrāme kriyatāṃ kṣaṇam..4..
1.45.d:
आह त्वां भार्गवो रामस्त्र्यम्बकेण विसर्जितः॥
त्वया युद्धाय दैत्येन्द्र संग्रामे क्रियतां क्षणम्॥4॥
1.45.m:
Rāma, the descendant of Bhṛgu, dispatched by Tryambaka, says to you:
‘O lord of Daityas, grant a moment in battle for a fight with you.

1.45.s:
vivāsya vāsavaṃ svargāddevāñjitvā sadā''have..
anayasyā'sya ghorasya phalaṃ prāpnuhi durmate ..5..
1.45.d:
विवास्य वासवं स्वर्गाद्देवाञ्जित्वा सदा'ऽहवे॥
अनयस्याऽस्य घोरस्य फलं प्राप्नुहि दुर्मते ॥5॥
1.45.m:
Having driven Vāsava from heaven and always conquered the gods in battle,
receive the fruit of this terrible injustice, O evil-minded one!

1.45.s:
nāhaṃ pramatte viśvaste praharāmi kadācana..
tena te preṣito dūtastasmādyuddhe sthiro bhava ..6..
1.45.d:
नाहं प्रमत्ते विश्वस्ते प्रहरामि कदाचन॥
तेन ते प्रेषितो दूतस्तस्माद्युद्धे स्थिरो भव ॥6॥
1.45.m:
I never strike one who is off-guard or trusting.
Therefore a messenger has been sent to you; hence be steadfast in battle.’

1.45.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktastadā sālvo brāhmaṇaṃ vākyamabravīt ..
nā'haṃ rāmakṛte brahmansannahyāmi kadācana .. 7 ..
1.45.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा साल्वो ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
नाऽहं रामकृते ब्रह्मन्सन्नह्यामि कदाचन ॥ 7 ॥
1.45.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed, Sālva then said to the brahmin:
‘I will never arm myself on account of Rāma, O brahmin.

1.45.s:
kintu sainyena sarveṇa sannaddhena varūthinā ..
mahādevaṃ vijeṣyāmi yena rāmo visarjitaḥ .. 8 ..
1.45.d:
किन्तु सैन्येन सर्वेण सन्नद्धेन वरूथिना ॥
महादेवं विजेष्यामि येन रामो विसर्जितः ॥ 8 ॥
1.45.m:
Rather, with my entire army armed and organized in chariots,
I shall conquer Mahādeva, by whom Rāma was dispatched.

1.45.s:
sannaddhasainyasahitaṃ mahādevajayaiṣiṇam ..
yadi māṃ yotsyate rāmo hantāsmi tamahaṃ mṛdhe .. 9..
1.45.d:
सन्नद्धसैन्यसहितं महादेवजयैषिणम् ॥
यदि मां योत्स्यते रामो हन्तास्मि तमहं मृधे ॥ 9॥
1.45.m:
If Rāma fights me while I am accompanied by an armed army
and seeking to conquer Mahādeva, I shall kill him in battle.

1.45.s:
sa tvaṃ gaccha yathākāmaṃ rāmāya vinivedaya ..
etadvacanamādāya sālvasya sa mahātmanaḥ .. 1.45.10 ..
1.45.d:
स त्वं गच्छ यथाकामं रामाय विनिवेदय ॥
एतद्वचनमादाय साल्वस्य स महात्मनः ॥ 1.45.10 ॥
1.45.m:
Go as you please and report [this] to Rāma.’
Taking these words of the great-souled Sālva,

1.45.s:
jagāma rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ sālvavākyaniveditaḥ ..
gatvā śaśaṃsa rāmāya saiṃhikeyaviceṣṭitam .. 11 ..
1.45.d:
जगाम रामं धर्मज्ञं साल्ववाक्यनिवेदितः ॥
गत्वा शशंस रामाय सैंहिकेयविचेष्टितम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.45.m:
he went to Rāma, who knows dharma, having the words of Sālva to report.
Having gone, he reported the conduct of the son of Siṃhikā to Rāma.

1.45.s:
tena vākyena rāmo'pi roṣāddaityapuraṃ yayau ..
rāmadūte gate tasmin daityānsālvaḥ pracodayat .. 12 ..
1.45.d:
तेन वाक्येन रामोऽपि रोषाद्दैत्यपुरं ययौ ॥
रामदूते गते तस्मिन् दैत्यान्साल्वः प्रचोदयत् ॥ 12 ॥
1.45.m:
At those words, Rāma too went in anger to the city of the Daityas.
When that messenger of Rāma had departed, Sālva urged the Daityas:

1.45.s:
sannahyadhvaṃ vijeṣyāmaḥ sagaṇaṃ bhagasūdanam ..
tataste dānavāḥ sarve sālvavākyapracoditāḥ .. 13 ..
1.45.d:
सन्नह्यध्वं विजेष्यामः सगणं भगसूदनम् ॥
ततस्ते दानवाः सर्वे साल्ववाक्यप्रचोदिताः ॥ 13 ॥
1.45.m:
‘Arm yourselves! We shall conquer the destroyer of Bhaga along with his host!’
Then all those Dānavas, urged by the words of Sālva,

1.45.s:
sannaddhā svagṛhebhyastu rājadvāramupāgatāḥ..
kuñjarāṇāṃ ninādena śaṅkhabherīraveṇa ca..14..
1.45.d:
सन्नद्धा स्वगृहेभ्यस्तु राजद्वारमुपागताः॥
कुञ्जराणां निनादेन शङ्खभेरीरवेण च॥14॥
1.45.m:
armed themselves and went from their homes to the royal gate.
With the roaring of elephants and the sound of conches and drums,

1.45.s:
rājadvāre mahāñchabdastumulaḥ samapadyata..
hutvā hutāśanaṃ snātaḥ sālva saṃpūjya ca dvijān .. 15 ..
1.45.d:
राजद्वारे महाञ्छब्दस्तुमुलः समपद्यत॥
हुत्वा हुताशनं स्नातः साल्व संपूज्य च द्विजान् ॥ 15 ॥
1.45.m:
a great and tumultuous noise arose at the royal gate.
Having offered oblations into the fire, bathed, and honored the twice-born, Sālva

1.45.s: āruroha gajaṃ mattaṃ śailāgraṃ savitā yathā .. 16 ..
1.45.d: आरुरोह गजं मत्तं शैलाग्रं सविता यथा ॥ 16 ॥
1.45.m: mounted an elephant in rut, like the sun mounting a mountain summit.

1.45.s:
vinirgataṃ daityapatiṃ samīkṣya daityeśvarāḥ kālasamānadarpāḥ ..
ūcustadā taṃ samareṣvajeyama jayasva śambhuṃ yudhi saṃpragṛhya ..17..
1.45.d:
विनिर्गतं दैत्यपतिं समीक्ष्य दैत्येश्वराः कालसमानदर्पाः ॥
ऊचुस्तदा तं समरेष्वजेयम जयस्व शम्भुं युधि संप्रगृह्य ॥17॥
1.45.m:
Beholding the lord of Daityas set out, the Daitya chiefs, equal in arrogance to Kāla,
then said to him, invincible in battles: ‘Conquer Śambhu in combat, seizing him!’

1.46.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vyaspandatā'tha sālvasya rājanbāhuradakṣiṇaḥ ..
hadayañca tathā pṛṣṭhaṃ nayanañcāpya dakṣiṇam ..1..
1.46.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
व्यस्पन्दताऽथ साल्वस्य राजन्बाहुरदक्षिणः ॥
हदयञ्च तथा पृष्ठं नयनञ्चाप्य दक्षिणम् ॥1॥
1.46.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, O king, Sālva’s left arm throbbed,
as did his chest, back, and his left eye.

1.46.s:
śūnyacittaśca vimanāḥ kampate ca muhurmuhuḥ .
papāta nāyakaścā'pi kirīṭāttārakaprabhaḥ..2..
1.46.d:
शून्यचित्तश्च विमनाः कम्पते च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
पपात नायकश्चाऽपि किरीटात्तारकप्रभः॥2॥
1.46.m:
Absent-minded and dejected, he trembled again and again,
and the central gem, bright as a star, fell from his diadem.

1.46.s:
ākramanti gajāḥ pādaṃ tathā vāmena dakṣiṇam ..
kareṇa veṣṭayanti sma tathā dantamadakṣiṇam ..
madaṃ tyajanti ye mattāsturagāśca muhurmuhuḥ .. 3 ..
1.46.d:
आक्रमन्ति गजाः पादं तथा वामेन दक्षिणम् ॥
करेण वेष्टयन्ति स्म तथा दन्तमदक्षिणम् ॥
मदं त्यजन्ति ये मत्तास्तुरगाश्च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 3 ॥
1.46.m:
Elephants crossed their right leg over their left,
twined their trunk around their left tusk,
and those in rut repeatedly lost their temporal discharge; and the horses

1.46.s:
saṃspṛśanti tathā vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ prothena vāmunā..
vṛkāḥ śṛgālāḥ śārdūlā viḍālā gardabhāḥ śaśāḥ ..4..
1.46.d:
संस्पृशन्ति तथा वामं पार्श्वं प्रोथेन वामुना॥
वृकाः शृगालाः शार्दूला विडाला गर्दभाः शशाः ॥4॥
1.46.m:
touched their left flank with their snouts.
Wolves, jackals, tigers, cats, donkeys, and hares,

1.46.s:
vāmībhūtvā dānavānāṃ yānti dakṣiṇatastataḥ ..
eṇā varāhāḥ pṛṣato yānti teṣāñca vāmataḥ..5..
1.46.d:
वामीभूत्वा दानवानां यान्ति दक्षिणतस्ततः ॥
एणा वराहाः पृषतो यान्ति तेषाञ्च वामतः॥5॥
1.46.m:
standing on the left of the Dānavas, then moved to the right;
stags, boars, and spotted deer moved to their left.

1.46.s:
dīptāyāṃ diśi vāśanti mṛgāsteṣāmapasvanam ..
tailapaṅkaguḍāṅgāracarmakeśatṛṇāni ca.6..
1.46.d:
दीप्तायां दिशि वाशन्ति मृगास्तेषामपस्वनम् ॥
तैलपङ्कगुडाङ्गारचर्मकेशतृणानि च.6॥
1.46.m:
In the blazing direction birds and beasts shrieked discordant cries before them;
and oil, mud, molasses, charcoal, skin, hair, and grass

1.46.s:
dānavānāṃ prayātānāṃ saṃbhavantyagratastathā ..
evaṃvidhā durnimittā jātāḥ sālvasya paśyataḥ ..7..
1.46.d:
दानवानां प्रयातानां संभवन्त्यग्रतस्तथा ॥
एवंविधा दुर्निमित्ता जाताः साल्वस्य पश्यतः ॥7॥
1.46.m:
appeared before the marching Dānavas.
Such ill omens arose before Sālva's eyes.

1.46.s:
matiḥ suniścitaivā''sīnmaraṇaṃ prati yādava ..
sa yayau saha sainyena mahatā caturaṅgiṇā...
kailāsaparvataṃ yoddhuṃ mahādevena śūlinā .. 9 ..
1.46.d:
मतिः सुनिश्चितैवा'ऽसीन्मरणं प्रति यादव ॥
स ययौ सह सैन्येन महता चतुरङ्गिणा॥।
कैलासपर्वतं योद्धुं महादेवेन शूलिना ॥ 9 ॥
1.46.m:
His mind was firmly set on death, O descendant of Yadu.
He marched with a vast fourfold army
to Mount Kailāsa to fight Mahādeva, the trident-wielder.

1.46.s:
yuddhotsuke daityapatau prayāte vyadṛśyatāgrecaracaṇḍavegaḥ ..
rāmaḥ pravālāruṇakomalena dīptapratāpena virājamānaḥ .. 1.46.10 ..
1.46.d:
युद्धोत्सुके दैत्यपतौ प्रयाते व्यदृश्यताग्रेचरचण्डवेगः ॥
रामः प्रवालारुणकोमलेन दीप्तप्रतापेन विराजमानः ॥ 1.46.10 ॥
1.46.m:
As the Daitya lord, eager for battle, set out, there appeared before him one of fierce speed:
Rāma, shining with blazing splendor, tender like a coral sprout.

1.47.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vahnijvālāgravarṇena jaṭājūṭena rājitam ..
gaganārddhamivā''rūḍhaṃ nidāghe ravimaṇḍalam .. 1 ..
1.47.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वह्निज्वालाग्रवर्णेन जटाजूटेन राजितम् ॥
गगनार्द्धमिवा'ऽरूढं निदाघे रविमण्डलम् ॥ 1 ॥

1.47.s:
ādhāraṃ sarvadevānāṃ tapasā dyotitaprabham ..
sevamānamavasanaṃ pītagātramarindamam .. 2 ..
1.47.d:
आधारं सर्वदेवानां तपसा द्योतितप्रभम् ॥
सेवमानमवसनं पीतगात्रमरिन्दमम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.47.m:
the refuge of all gods, his splendor glowing with ascetic heat,
clothed in tree bark, with a yellow body, the subduer of enemies;

1.47.s:
ekamekākinaṃ vīraṃ sahasraśatamaṇḍitam ..
piṇḍitaṃ sakalaṃ dhāma brahmakṣatriyatejasām .. 3 ..
1.47.d:
एकमेकाकिनं वीरं सहस्रशतमण्डितम् ॥
पिण्डितं सकलं धाम ब्रह्मक्षत्रियतेजसाम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.47.m:
solitary, a lone hero adorned as if by a hundred thousand,
the concentrated mass of all the fiery splendor of brahmins and kṣatriyas;

1.47.s:
kṛṣṇājinottarāsaṅgabhrājamānaṃ baloddhatam ..
snigdhayā rañjitamiva prāyeṇa pārvatīdṛśā .. 4 ..
1.47.d:
कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासङ्गभ्राजमानं बलोद्धतम् ॥
स्निग्धया रञ्जितमिव प्रायेण पार्वतीदृशा ॥ 4 ॥
1.47.m:
shining with an upper garment of black antelope skin, haughty with strength,
as though continuously gladdened by Pārvatī's affectionate glance;

1.47.s:
virājamānaṃ dordaṇḍarukmadaṇḍena bhāsvatā..
paraśvadhena tīkṣṇena vimalākāśavarcasā .. 5 ..
1.47.d:
विराजमानं दोर्दण्डरुक्मदण्डेन भास्वता॥
परश्वधेन तीक्ष्णेन विमलाकाशवर्चसा ॥ 5 ॥
1.47.m:
resplendent with an arm staff holding a radiant, golden-shafted
sharp axe that possessed the brilliance of a spotless sky;

1.47.s:
tapasvinamanādṛśyaṃ yamakālāntakopamam ..
kampamānaṃ padanyāsairvasudhāṃ sakalāṃ tathā ..6..
1.47.d:
तपस्विनमनादृश्यं यमकालान्तकोपमम् ॥
कम्पमानं पदन्यासैर्वसुधां सकलां तथा ॥6॥
1.47.m:
an ascetic dreadful to behold, resembling Yama the ender, Kāla,
shaking the entire earth with the placing of his feet;

1.47.s:
muṣṇantaṃ sarvatejāṃsi prabhāte ravimaṇḍalam..
prāṃśuṃ kanakavarṇāṅgaṃ sitayajñopavītinam ..7..
1.47.d:
मुष्णन्तं सर्वतेजांसि प्रभाते रविमण्डलम्॥
प्रांशुं कनकवर्णाङ्गं सितयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ॥7॥
1.47.m:
eclipsing all brilliance like the solar orb at dawn,
tall, with limbs of golden hue, wearing a white sacrificial thread,

1.47.s:
gaṅgāyāḥ pravaheṇaiva meruśṛṃgaṃ virājitam..
tejasā dahanākāraṃ prajāsaṃhārakārakam .. 8 ..
1.47.d:
गङ्गायाः प्रवहेणैव मेरुशृंगं विराजितम्॥
तेजसा दहनाकारं प्रजासंहारकारकम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.47.m:
like the peak of Meru adorned by the flow of the Gaṅgā,
having the appearance of a fire by his splendor, the cause of the destruction of creatures,

1.47.s:
viṣamaṃ pramatheśasya tṛtīyamiva locanam ..
aprasahyamanāvāryaṃ durlaṅghyaṃ jīvitacchidam .. 9 ..
1.47.d:
विषमं प्रमथेशस्य तृतीयमिव लोचनम् ॥
अप्रसह्यमनावार्यं दुर्लङ्घ्यं जीवितच्छिदम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.47.m:
terrible, like the third eye of the lord of Pramathas,
unbearable, irresistible, impassable, cutting off life,

1.47.s:
kāleneva bhujaṃ savyaṃ daityahetoḥ prasāritam ..
rāme dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpte dānavānāṃ samantataḥ .. 1.47.10 ..
1.47.d:
कालेनेव भुजं सव्यं दैत्यहेतोः प्रसारितम् ॥
रामे दृष्टिपथं प्राप्ते दानवानां समन्ततः ॥ 1.47.10 ॥
1.47.m:
like the left arm of Kāla extended for the sake of the Daityas—
when Rāma came into the range of vision of the Dānavas on all sides,

1.47.s:
hāhākāro mahānāsīttamekaṃ nighnatāṃ raṇe ..
śastradhāraṇavibhraṣṭabrāhmaṇyaṃ svapathāccyutam .. 11 ..
1.47.d:
हाहाकारो महानासीत्तमेकं निघ्नतां रणे ॥
शस्त्रधारणविभ्रष्टब्राह्मण्यं स्वपथाच्च्युतम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.47.m:
there arose a great clamor as they sought to kill that lone one in battle:
‘One fallen from his brahminhood by bearing weapons, strayed from his own path!

1.47.s:
ghātayadhvaṃ durācāramenamūcuḥ parasparam ..
evamādravatāṃ teṣāṃ bahūnāmātatāyinām .. 12 ..
1.47.d:
घातयध्वं दुराचारमेनमूचुः परस्परम् ॥
एवमाद्रवतां तेषां बहूनामाततायिनाम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.47.m:
Kill this evil-doer!’ they shouted to one another.
As they, numerous assailants, rushed forward in this way,

1.47.s:
jagrāha vegaṃ sarveṣāṃ marutāmiva parvataḥ ..
sa hanyamāno nārācaistomarairmuśalaistathā ..13..
1.47.d:
जग्राह वेगं सर्वेषां मरुतामिव पर्वतः ॥
स हन्यमानो नाराचैस्तोमरैर्मुशलैस्तथा ॥13॥
1.47.m:
he checked the momentum of them all, like a mountain checking the winds.
Struck with iron arrows, javelins, and clubs,

1.47.s:
gadābhirasibhiḥ pāśairbhuśuṇḍībhirayoguḍaiḥ ..
paṭṭiśairbhindipālaiśca hutaiḥ śūlaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ ..14..
1.47.d:
गदाभिरसिभिः पाशैर्भुशुण्डीभिरयोगुडैः ॥
पट्टिशैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च हुतैः शूलैः परश्वधैः ॥14॥
1.47.m:
maces, swords, nooses, bhuśuṇḍīs, iron balls,
paṭṭiśas, bhindipālas, thrown tridents, and axes,
the immeasurable-souled one did not waver, like a mountain before the winds.

1.47.s:
saṃveṣṭitaṃ sarvata eva sainyairadṛṣṭayuddho'pi raṇe mahātmā..
daityārṇavaṃ goṣpadatulyamātramamanyatā''jau raṇacaṇḍavegaḥ ..16 ..
1.47.d:
संवेष्टितं सर्वत एव सैन्यैरदृष्टयुद्धोऽपि रणे महात्मा॥
दैत्यार्णवं गोष्पदतुल्यमात्रममन्यता'ऽजौ रणचण्डवेगः ॥16 ॥
1.47.m: Surrounded on all sides by armies, though he had never witnessed [such] battle before, that great-souled one, furious in speed of combat, / considered the ocean of Daityas in the fight as merely equal to a cow's footprint.

1.48.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
siṃhikāputrasainyena hanyamānastadā raṇe ..
gocarābhyāgatānsarvānrāmo ninye yamakṣayama .. 1 ..
1.48.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सिंहिकापुत्रसैन्येन हन्यमानस्तदा रणे ॥
गोचराभ्यागतान्सर्वान्रामो निन्ये यमक्षयम ॥ 1 ॥
1.48.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Struck then in battle by the army of the son of Siṃhikā, / Rāma dispatched all who came into range to the abode of Yama.

1.48.s:
tena kṛttāḥ paraśunā yathā paraśunā mṛgāḥ ..
āliṅgya śerate kṣoṇīṃ dānavāste madoddhatāḥ ..2..
1.48.d:
तेन कृत्ताः परशुना यथा परशुना मृगाः ॥
आलिङ्ग्य शेरते क्षोणीं दानवास्ते मदोद्धताः ॥2॥
1.48.m: Cut down by his axe as wild beasts by an axe, / those Dānavas, haughty with pride, lay embracing the earth.

1.48.s:
tīkṣṇadhārāgraduṣprekṣyakuṭhāracchinnamastakaiḥ ..
ātatāra tadā bhūmiṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare .. 3 ..
1.48.d:
तीक्ष्णधाराग्रदुष्प्रेक्ष्यकुठारच्छिन्नमस्तकैः ॥
आततार तदा भूमिं कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे ॥ 3 ॥
1.48.m: With their heads severed by his axe, dreadful to behold with its sharp edge, / he then strewed the ground as with kuśa grass at a sacrifice.

1.48.s:
paraśvadhāgrasaṃbhinnadaityadehasamudbhavam ..
prasusrāva tadā raktaṃ yenā''sītkardamaṃ mahat .. 4 ..
1.48.d:
परश्वधाग्रसंभिन्नदैत्यदेहसमुद्भवम् ॥
प्रसुस्राव तदा रक्तं येना'ऽसीत्कर्दमं महत् ॥ 4 ॥
1.48.m: Blood, flowing from the bodies of the Daityas pierced by the edge of his battle-axe, / gushed out then, producing a great mire.

1.48.s:
te hanyamānā rāmeṇa rāmamevā'bhidudruvuḥ ..
paripūrṇe yathā kāle śalabhā jātavedasam .. 5 ..
1.48.d:
ते हन्यमाना रामेण राममेवाऽभिदुद्रुवुः ॥
परिपूर्णे यथा काले शलभा जातवेदसम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.48.m: Struck by Rāma, they rushed straight towards Rāma, / as moths to a fire when their time is fulfilled.

1.48.s:
rāmasya pramukhe daityāstadā tiṣṭhanti ye nṛpa ..
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa te prayānti yamakṣayam .. 6 ..
1.48.d:
रामस्य प्रमुखे दैत्यास्तदा तिष्ठन्ति ये नृप ॥
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ते प्रयान्ति यमक्षयम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.48.m: Whatever Daityas then stood before Rāma, O king, / departed to the abode of Yama in mere the blink of an eye.

1.48.s:
kuñjarasturagaḥ pattirnājau yādava dṛśyate ..
dvitīyaṃ pradadau yasya prahāraṃ bhṛgunandanaḥ .. 7 ..
1.48.d:
कुञ्जरस्तुरगः पत्तिर्नाजौ यादव दृश्यते ॥
द्वितीयं प्रददौ यस्य प्रहारं भृगुनन्दनः ॥ 7 ॥
1.48.m: No elephant, horse, or foot-soldier was seen in battle, O Yādava, / upon whom the descendant of Bhṛgu struck a second blow.

1.48.s:
ekaprahārābhigatāndānavānparvatopamān..
apaśyāma raṇe tatra brahmaṇā sahitā vayam ..8..
1.48.d:
एकप्रहाराभिगतान्दानवान्पर्वतोपमान्॥
अपश्याम रणे तत्र ब्रह्मणा सहिता वयम् ॥8॥
1.48.m: Together with Brahmā, we saw in that battle / Dānavas resembling mountains felled by a single blow.

1.48.s:
rāmeṇa hanyamānānāṃ dānavānāṃ muhurmuhuḥ ..
ārāvaḥ śrūyate ghoro vanānāmiva dahyatām .. 9 ..
1.48.d:
रामेण हन्यमानानां दानवानां मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
आरावः श्रूयते घोरो वनानामिव दह्यताम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.48.m: Of the Dānavas continuously struck by Rāma, / a terrible roar was heard, like that of burning forests.

1.48.s:
ākramya padbhyāṃ tarasā rathasthānāmathāharat ..
śīrṣāṇi tena tīkṣṇena tathā paraśunā raṇe .. 1.48.10 ..
1.48.d:
आक्रम्य पद्भ्यां तरसा रथस्थानामथाहरत् ॥
शीर्षाणि तेन तीक्ष्णेन तथा परशुना रणे ॥ 1.48.10 ॥
1.48.m: Having swiftly stepped upon the chariot-warriors with his feet, he then took / their heads with that sharp battle-axe in battle.

1.48.s:
rāmeṇā''kramyamāṇeṣu ratheṣu rathayūthapāḥ ..
bhūmau niviṣṭamūrddhānastatyajurjīvitaṃ hayāḥ .. 11 ..
1.48.d:
रामेणा'ऽक्रम्यमाणेषु रथेषु रथयूथपाः ॥
भूमौ निविष्टमूर्द्धानस्तत्यजुर्जीवितं हयाः ॥ 11 ॥
1.48.m: As the chariots were stepped upon by Rāma, the commanders of the chariot divisions / and their horses, their heads bowed to the earth, abandoned their lives.

1.48.s:
niṣpipeṣa rathasthānāṃ dārayankuñjarānraṇe ..
babhrame tatra tatraikaḥ kālotsṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ .. 12 ..
1.48.d:
निष्पिपेष रथस्थानां दारयन्कुञ्जरान्रणे ॥
बभ्रमे तत्र तत्रैकः कालोत्सृष्ट इवान्तकः ॥ 12 ॥
1.48.m: Crushing chariot-warriors and tearing apart elephants in battle, / he wandered here and there alone, like Death unleashed at the end of time.

1.48.s:
vicchindanyodhaśīrṣāṇi raṇe rāmo rathādratham ..
vrajanbhāti viśālākṣo vṛkṣādavṛkṣamivā'ṇḍaja .. 13 ..
1.48.d:
विच्छिन्दन्योधशीर्षाणि रणे रामो रथाद्रथम् ॥
व्रजन्भाति विशालाक्षो वृक्षादवृक्षमिवाऽण्डज ॥ 13 ॥
1.48.m: Severing the heads of warriors in battle as he went from chariot to chariot, / the large-eyed Rāma shone like a bird [flying] from tree to tree.

1.48.s:
sa śarāñcitasarvāṅgaḥ śoṇitena samukṣitaḥ ..
rarāja rāmaḥ samare raśmimāniva bhāskaraḥ .. 14 ..
1.48.d:
स शराञ्चितसर्वाङ्गः शोणितेन समुक्षितः ॥
रराज रामः समरे रश्मिमानिव भास्करः ॥ 14 ॥
1.48.m: With his whole body bristling with arrows, sprinkled with blood, / Rāma shone in combat like the sun endowed with rays.

1.48.s:
daityabāhuvinirmuktānāyudhāñchataśastathā ..
paraśvadhāgreṇa raṇe ciccheda raṇakarkaśaḥ .. 15 ..
1.48.d:
दैत्यबाहुविनिर्मुक्तानायुधाञ्छतशस्तथा ॥
परश्वधाग्रेण रणे चिच्छेद रणकर्कशः ॥ 15 ॥
1.48.m: Fierce in combat, he cleaved in battle with the tip of his battle-axe / hundreds of weapons hurled from the arms of the Daityas.

1.48.s:
teṣāṃ saṃchidyamānānāṃ prādurāsīddhutāśanaḥ ..
yena tāneva tarasā kṣitau cakre sa bhasmasāt .. 16 ..
1.48.d:
तेषां संछिद्यमानानां प्रादुरासीद्धुताशनः ॥
येन तानेव तरसा क्षितौ चक्रे स भस्मसात् ॥ 16 ॥
1.48.m: As they were being cleaved, a blazing fire burst forth, / with which he swiftly reduced them to ashes on the ground.

1.48.s:
bahutvāddaityayodhānāṃ rāmassaṃchādito raṇe ..
hetipuñjena mahatā śailābhena na dṛśyate .. 17 ..
1.48.d:
बहुत्वाद्दैत्ययोधानां रामस्संछादितो रणे ॥
हेतिपुञ्जेन महता शैलाभेन न दृश्यते ॥ 17 ॥
1.48.m: Because of the great number of Daitya warriors, Rāma was covered in battle; / he was not seen beneath the vast, mountain-like heap of weapons.

1.48.s:
hetipuñjaṃ vidhūyogramabhrapuñjaṃ yathā raviḥ ..
punardarśanamāyāti saṃharttā daityatejasām .. 18 ..
1.48.d:
हेतिपुञ्जं विधूयोग्रमभ्रपुञ्जं यथा रविः ॥
पुनर्दर्शनमायाति संहर्त्ता दैत्यतेजसाम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.48.m: Shaking off the fierce mass of weapons as the sun scatters a mass of clouds, / the destroyer of the Daityas' splendour came into view again.

1.48.s:
brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārddhamṛṣibhiśca mahātmabhiḥ ..
pūjayāmāsa tadyuddhaṃ sādhuvādena yādava .. 19 ..
1.48.d:
ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्द्धमृषिभिश्च महात्मभिः ॥
पूजयामास तद्युद्धं साधुवादेन यादव ॥ 19 ॥
1.48.m: Brahmā, together with the hosts of gods and the great-souled sages, / honoured that combat with acclamations of praise, O Yādava.

1.48.s:
dṛṣṭavantaśca dhanuṣā yuddhāni ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
tathaivā''ścaryabhūtāni lokānāṃ khaḍgacarmaṇā .. 1.48.20 ..
1.48.d:
दृष्टवन्तश्च धनुषा युद्धानि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
तथैवा'ऽश्चर्यभूतानि लोकानां खड्गचर्मणा ॥ 1.48.20 ॥
1.48.m: “And we have seen battles with bows again and again, / as well as those with sword and shield that were wonders to the worlds;

1.48.s:
apūrva eṣa saṃgrāmo rāmasya bahubhiḥ saha ..
paraśvadhāyudhasyogra iti devāstathā'bruvan .. 21 ..
1.48.d:
अपूर्व एष संग्रामो रामस्य बहुभिः सह ॥
परश्वधायुधस्योग्र इति देवास्तथाऽब्रुवन् ॥ 21 ॥
1.48.m: unprecedented is this battle of Rāma with so many, / fierce with his battle-axe as weapon,” so indeed spoke the gods.

1.48.s:
pūjyamānaḥ sa rāmo'pi devapuṣpotkaraistadā ..
ciccheda yudhi daityānāṃ śirāṃsi śataśo raṇe .. 22 ..
1.48.d:
पूज्यमानः स रामोऽपि देवपुष्पोत्करैस्तदा ॥
चिच्छेद युधि दैत्यानां शिरांसि शतशो रणे ॥ 22 ॥
1.48.m: Rāma, even while being worshipped then by showers of flowers from the gods, / severed the heads of the Daityas by the hundreds in the fray.

1.48.s:
daityaśoṇitadigdhāṅgaṃ bhārgavaṃ laghuvikramam ..
alātacakrapratimaṃ tadā paśyati yādava .. 23 ..
1.48.d:
दैत्यशोणितदिग्धाङ्गं भार्गवं लघुविक्रमम् ॥
अलातचक्रप्रतिमं तदा पश्यति यादव ॥ 23 ॥
1.48.m: One saw then the descendant of Bhṛgu, his limbs smeared with Daitya blood, / swift in stride, resembling a whirling firebrand, O Yādava.

1.48.s:
bhramatā'nena raudreṇa raṇe kālāgnivarccasā ..
kṛtāḥ samaraśauṇḍena bhīmā rudhiranimnagāḥ .. 24 ..
1.48.d:
भ्रमताऽनेन रौद्रेण रणे कालाग्निवर्च्चसा ॥
कृताः समरशौण्डेन भीमा रुधिरनिम्नगाः ॥ 24 ॥
1.48.m: RoOption as he wandered in battle, fierce, with the lustre of the cosmic fire at the end of time, / dreadful rivers of blood were made by him who was skilled in war.

1.48.s:
paraśvadhāgravikṣepagatajīvitakuñjaraiḥ ..
pādopalaiśca samare pratastāra sa bhārgavaḥ .. 25 ..
1.48.d:
परश्वधाग्रविक्षेपगतजीवितकुञ्जरैः ॥
पादोपलैश्च समरे प्रतस्तार स भार्गवः ॥ 25 ॥
1.48.m: With elephants whose lives were ended by the stroke of the tip of his axe / and with rocks as footstones, that descendant of Bhṛgu paved [the field] in battle.

1.48.s:
dantidantapadanyāsaprāptaṃ kuñjaramastakam ..
vinighnansa gajārohācchyenavadvicaran laghu .. 26 ..
1.48.d:
दन्तिदन्तपदन्यासप्राप्तं कुञ्जरमस्तकम् ॥
विनिघ्नन्स गजारोहाच्छ्येनवद्विचरन् लघु ॥ 26 ॥
1.48.m: Stepping onto elephant-heads by placing his feet on their tusks, / he struck riders down from elephants, moving lightly like a falcon.

1.48.s:
āruhya kuṃjarañcaikaṃ kuñjarātkuñjarāntaram ..
apaśyāma raṇe rāmaṃ vicarantaṃ yathāsukham .. 27 ..
1.48.d:
आरुह्य कुंजरञ्चैकं कुञ्जरात्कुञ्जरान्तरम् ॥
अपश्याम रणे रामं विचरन्तं यथासुखम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.48.m: Mounting one elephant, and from that elephant to another, / we saw Rāma moving at his ease in the battle.

1.48.s:
bhūyo bhūmigato rāmaḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ paraśvadhā ..
cakāra kadanaṃ ghoraṃ pralayāgnirivotthitaḥ .. 28 ..
1.48.d:
भूयो भूमिगतो रामः कुञ्जराणां परश्वधा ॥
चकार कदनं घोरं प्रलयाग्निरिवोत्थितः ॥ 28 ॥
1.48.m: Returning to the ground, Rāma wrought terrible slaughter / upon the elephants with his axe, like the fire of dissolution arisen.

1.48.s:
chinnāgrahastānviradāndviradāñchoṇitokṣitān ..
kṣitau gatā na paśyāmaḥ śyāmīkṛtadigantarān.. 29 ..
1.48.d:
छिन्नाग्रहस्तान्विरदान्द्विरदाञ्छोणितोक्षितान् ॥
क्षितौ गता न पश्यामः श्यामीकृतदिगन्तरान्॥ 29 ॥
1.48.m: Elephants with severed trunks, smeared with blood, / falling to the earth, darkened the quarters of the sky before our eyes.

1.48.s:
evaṃ hi yudhyatā tena raṇe kālāgnivarcasā ..
hatāni dānavendrāṇāṃ prayutānyarbudāni ca .. 1.48.30 ..
1.48.d:
एवं हि युध्यता तेन रणे कालाग्निवर्चसा ॥
हतानि दानवेन्द्राणां प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ॥ 1.48.30 ॥
1.48.m: By him thus fighting in battle with the lustre of the fire of dissolution, / millions and hundreds of millions of lords of the Dānavas were slain.

1.48.s:
yeṣāṃ prahāraṃ saṃsoḍhuṃ neyaṃ śaktā vasundharā ..
teṣāṃ prahārabhinnāṅgo naiva rāmo vyakampata .. 31 ..
1.48.d:
येषां प्रहारं संसोढुं नेयं शक्ता वसुन्धरा ॥
तेषां प्रहारभिन्नाङ्गो नैव रामो व्यकम्पत ॥ 31 ॥
1.48.m: Though his limbs were struck by the blows of those whose impact / this earth was not able to endure, Rāma did not waver at all.

1.48.s:
dṛṣṭvā prahāravaiklavyaṃ nihatāṃśca mahāsurān ..
pradudruvurdaityagaṇāḥ sālvaṃ śaraṇamāhave .. 32 ..
1.48.d:
दृष्ट्वा प्रहारवैक्लव्यं निहतांश्च महासुरान् ॥
प्रदुद्रुवुर्दैत्यगणाः साल्वं शरणमाहवे ॥ 32 ॥
1.48.m: Seeing the helplessness under his blows and the great asuras slain, / the hosts of Daityas fled in battle to Sālva for refuge.

1.48.s:
alpāvaśiṣṭānditijānpranaṣṭānsaṃvīkṣya sālvaḥ svahite niviṣṭān ..
rāmaṃ yayau tena gajena yuddhe rāmādraṇe yuddhamabhīpsamānaḥ .. 33 ..
1.48.d:
अल्पावशिष्टान्दितिजान्प्रनष्टान्संवीक्ष्य साल्वः स्वहिते निविष्टान् ॥
रामं ययौ तेन गजेन युद्धे रामाद्रणे युद्धमभीप्समानः ॥ 33 ॥
1.48.m: Seeing the remaining few sons of Diti fleeing, intent on saving themselves, / Sālva approached Rāma in battle on that elephant, desiring combat with Rāma in the fight.

1.49.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
tataḥ sālvo mahātejāḥ kuñjareṇa tarasvinā ..
arpayāmāsa dharmajña reṇukānandavardhanam .. 1 ..
1.49.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
ततः साल्वो महातेजाः कुञ्जरेण तरस्विना ॥
अर्पयामास धर्मज्ञ रेणुकानन्दवर्धनम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.49.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then Sālva, of great splendour, attacked the one who increases the joy of Reṇukā / with his swift elephant, O knower of dharma.

1.49.s:
stabdhakarṇo vivṛttākṣaḥ kṛtvā kuṇḍalinaṃ karam ..
grīvāṃ sañcālayannāgo yayau gajamadoddhatam .. 2 ..
1.49.d:
स्तब्धकर्णो विवृत्ताक्षः कृत्वा कुण्डलिनं करम् ॥
ग्रीवां सञ्चालयन्नागो ययौ गजमदोद्धतम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.49.m: With stiffened ears and rolling eyes, curling its trunk / and tossing its neck, the elephant advanced, arrogant with rut.

1.49.s:
dṛṣṭvaivāpatatastasya vegaṃ rāmo'pi taṃ gajam ..
huṃkāramātreṇa raṇe stambhayāmāsa vegitam .. 3 ..
1.49.d:
दृष्ट्वैवापततस्तस्य वेगं रामोऽपि तं गजम् ॥
हुंकारमात्रेण रणे स्तम्भयामास वेगितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.49.m: Seeing the fury of that elephant as it charged, Rāma / halted it in battle in its rush with a mere roar.

1.49.s:
stambhayāmāsa nāgendraṃ śailendraśikharopamam ..
tasthau sa puratastasya sālvasya samarapriyaḥ .. 4 ..
1.49.d:
स्तम्भयामास नागेन्द्रं शैलेन्द्रशिखरोपमम् ॥
तस्थौ स पुरतस्तस्य साल्वस्य समरप्रियः ॥ 4 ॥
1.49.m: Having halted that lord of elephants resembling the peak of a lordly mountain, / he, fond of battle, stood before Sālva.

1.49.s:
paraśuṃ rudhirāktāṅgaṃ sakalaṅkamalaṃ kare ..
dhārayan viṣṇuvadyāti sakalaṃ kamalaṅkare .. 5 ..
1.49.d:
परशुं रुधिराक्ताङ्गं सकलङ्कमलं करे ॥
धारयन् विष्णुवद्याति सकलं कमलङ्करे ॥ 5 ॥
1.49.m: Holding in his hand the axe with its edge stained with blood, free of fault, / he went like Viṣṇu, who holds the complete lotus in his hand.

1.49.s:
dantinā dantinaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ rāmasyā''roḍhumicchataḥ ..
jahāra vegavānvegaṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ .. 6 ..
1.49.d:
दन्तिना दन्तिनः पृष्ठं रामस्या'ऽरोढुमिच्छतः ॥
जहार वेगवान्वेगं शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥ 6 ॥
1.49.m: As Rāma was wishing to mount the back of the elephant from [another] elephant, / the swift [Sālva] checked his momentum with straight-jointed arrows.

1.49.s:
sālvasāyakasaṃghātavimukhīkṛtavikramam ..
rāmaṃ raṇe daityagaṇāśchādayanti varāyudhaiḥ .. 7 ..
1.49.d:
साल्वसायकसंघातविमुखीकृतविक्रमम् ॥
रामं रणे दैत्यगणाश्छादयन्ति वरायुधैः ॥ 7 ॥
1.49.m: When his prowess was turned away by the barrage of Sālva's arrows, / the hosts of Daityas covered Rāma in battle with choice weapons.

1.49.s:
mahatā so'strapuṃjena rāmaḥ saṃchādito raṇe ..
nimīlitākṣaścikṣepa sālvāya paraśuṃ tadā .. 8 ..
1.49.d:
महता सोऽस्त्रपुंजेन रामः संछादितो रणे ॥
निमीलिताक्षश्चिक्षेप साल्वाय परशुं तदा ॥ 8 ॥
1.49.m: Completely covered in battle by that vast mass of missiles, / Rāma, closing his eyes, then hurled his axe at Sālva.

1.49.s:
āgacchamānaṃ vegena sālvastaṃ paraśuṃ raṇe ..
āyudhairvārayāmāsa na śaśāka ca śatruhā .. 9 ..
1.49.d:
आगच्छमानं वेगेन साल्वस्तं परशुं रणे ॥
आयुधैर्वारयामास न शशाक च शत्रुहा ॥ 9 ॥
1.49.m: In the battle, Sālva warded off with weapons that axe coming with speed, / but the slayer of enemies could not [stop it].

1.49.s:
sa sālvāyudhasaṃghātaṃ bhaṅktvā sarvamaśeṣataḥ ..
jahāra śīrṣaṃ sālvasya mukuṭottamabhūṣitam .. 1.49.10 ..
1.49.d:
स साल्वायुधसंघातं भङ्क्त्वा सर्वमशेषतः ॥
जहार शीर्षं साल्वस्य मुकुटोत्तमभूषितम् ॥ 1.49.10 ॥
1.49.m: Having shattered all of Sālva's mass of weapons without exception, / it carried off Sālva's head, adorned with an excellent crown.

1.49.s:
rāmo'pi bhūtalātprāpya gadāṃ hemavibhūṣitām ..
āvidhya nijaghānograṃ sālvaṃ kuñjarasaṃsthitam .. 11 ..
1.49.d:
रामोऽपि भूतलात्प्राप्य गदां हेमविभूषिताम् ॥
आविध्य निजघानोग्रं साल्वं कुञ्जरसंस्थितम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.49.m: Rāma too, seizing a gold-adorned mace from the ground, / swung it and struck down the fierce Sālva who was mounted on his elephant,

1.49.s:
dvāvaṅkuśadharau śreṣṭhau dvau ca carmāsidhāriṇau ..
patākādhāriṇaṃ caikaṃ gajasya jaghane sthitam .. 12 ..
1.49.d:
द्वावङ्कुशधरौ श्रेष्ठौ द्वौ च चर्मासिधारिणौ ॥
पताकाधारिणं चैकं गजस्य जघने स्थितम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.49.m: Two excellent hook-bearers, two shield-and-sword-bearers, / and one banner-bearer who stood on the elephant’s rump,

1.49.s:
dehaṃ ca tasya sālvasya patākāṃ ca manoramām ..
etadādāya sakalamājagāma vasundharām .. 13 ..
1.49.d:
देहं च तस्य साल्वस्य पताकां च मनोरमाम् ॥
एतदादाय सकलमाजगाम वसुन्धराम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.49.m: As well as the body of that Sālva and his charming banner; / having seized all this, he came to the earth.

1.49.s:
siṃhanādena rāmasya vitrasto gajayūthapaḥ ..
ārttanādaṃ mahatkṛtvā pradudrāva narādhipa .. 14 ..
1.49.d:
सिंहनादेन रामस्य वित्रस्तो गजयूथपः ॥
आर्त्तनादं महत्कृत्वा प्रदुद्राव नराधिप ॥ 14 ॥
1.49.m: Terrified by the lion-roar of Rāma, the lord of the elephant herd / uttered a great cry of distress and fled, O ruler of men.

1.49.s:
rāmakarmaṇi vṛtte tu bhūtalātparaśuṃ raṇe ..
jagrāha vegāvānvegāddānavāntacikīrṣayā .. 15 ..
1.49.d:
रामकर्मणि वृत्ते तु भूतलात्परशुं रणे ॥
जग्राह वेगावान्वेगाद्दानवान्तचिकीर्षया ॥ 15 ॥
1.49.m: When Rāma's deed was done, the swift one swiftly seized the axe / from the ground in the battle, desiring to bring about the destruction of the Dānavas.

1.49.s:
dṛṣṭvā saparaśuṃ rāmaṃ sālvaṃ ca vinipātitam ..
hataśeṣāstu te daityāḥ praviṣṭā varuṇālayam ..16..
1.49.d:
दृष्ट्वा सपरशुं रामं साल्वं च विनिपातितम् ॥
हतशेषास्तु ते दैत्याः प्रविष्टा वरुणालयम् ॥16॥
1.49.m: Seeing Rāma holding the axe and Sālva struck down, / the remaining Daityas, who had survived the slaughter, entered the abode of Varuṇa.

1.49.s:
etasminneva kāle tu devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ ..
āyodhanamupājagmuḥ puraskṛtya pitāmaham .. 17 ..
1.49.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवाः सेन्द्रपुरोगमाः ॥
आयोधनमुपाजग्मुः पुरस्कृत्य पितामहम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.49.m: At that very time, the gods, with Indra at their head, / placed the Grandfather in front and approached the battlefield.

1.49.s:
praṇāmamakarotteṣāṃ rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ ..
pūjayitvā tu te rāmaṃ yayurdevāḥ svamālayam .. 18 ..
1.49.d:
प्रणाममकरोत्तेषां रामो रतिकरः पितुः ॥
पूजयित्वा तु ते रामं ययुर्देवाः स्वमालयम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.49.m: Rāma, who brings delight to his father, bowed down to them. / Having worshipped Rāma, the gods went to their own abode.

1.49.s:
śakro'pi labdhvā tridivaṃ rāmabāhuprasādhitam ..
vijahāra divaṃ rājanpālayāno jagattrayam .. 19 ..
1.49.d:
शक्रोऽपि लब्ध्वा त्रिदिवं रामबाहुप्रसाधितम् ॥
विजहार दिवं राजन्पालयानो जगत्त्रयम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.49.m: Śakra, too, having regained heaven, made secure by Rāma's arm, / wandered freely in heaven, O king, protecting the three worlds.

1.49.s:
rathena siṃhayuktena mahādevo'pi bhārgavam..
ādāya prayayau śīghraṃ kailāsaṃ parvatottamam .. 1.49.20 ..
1.49.d:
रथेन सिंहयुक्तेन महादेवोऽपि भार्गवम्॥
आदाय प्रययौ शीघ्रं कैलासं पर्वतोत्तमम् ॥ 1.49.20 ॥
1.49.m: Mahādeva as well, having taken the Bhārgava on his chariot yoked with lions, / departed swiftly for Kailāsa, the foremost of mountains.

1.49.s:
snehena cā'sya gātrāṇāṃ cakre sammārjanaṃ haraḥ ..
yenā''sīdbalavān rāmo nirvraṇaśca mahāśayāḥ .. 21 ..
1.49.d:
स्नेहेन चाऽस्य गात्राणां चक्रे सम्मार्जनं हरः ॥
येना'ऽसीद्बलवान् रामो निर्व्रणश्च महाशयाः ॥ 21 ॥
1.49.m: And out of affection Hara wiped his limbs, / whereby Rāma became strong, woundless, and noble-minded.

1.49.s:
gatavraṇaṃ śriyopetaṃ jayaṃ labdhvā hyupasthitam ..
rāmaṃ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śaṃkaro vākyamabravīt. 22 ..
1.49.d:
गतव्रणं श्रियोपेतं जयं लब्ध्वा ह्युपस्थितम् ॥
रामं प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठं शंकरो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। 22 ॥
1.49.m: To Rāma, whose wounds were gone, endowed with splendour, who had attained victory and was standing before him, / the best among strikers, Śaṅkara spoke these words:

1.49.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
rāmarāma mahābhāga tvayā'haṃ paritoṣitaḥ ..
tasmāttavā'haṃ dāsyāmi cāstragrāmaṃ hyanuttamam .. 23 ..
1.49.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
रामराम महाभाग त्वयाऽहं परितोषितः ॥
तस्मात्तवाऽहं दास्यामि चास्त्रग्रामं ह्यनुत्तमम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.49.m: Śaṅkara said: / "Rāma, Rāma, O highly fortunate one, I am thoroughly pleased by you. / Therefore I shall give you the unsurpassed collection of divine weapons.

1.49.s:
astrāṇāṃ dhāraṇe śaktastvameko bhuvi bhārgava ..
tava dhairyamanaupamyaṃ tava sattvamanuttamam .. 24 ..
1.49.d:
अस्त्राणां धारणे शक्तस्त्वमेको भुवि भार्गव ॥
तव धैर्यमनौपम्यं तव सत्त्वमनुत्तमम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.49.m: You alone on earth, O Bhārgava, are capable of bearing divine weapons. / Your fortitude is incomparable; your strength of character is unsurpassed.

1.49.s:
astrayogamihasthastvaṃ kṛtvā putra śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
sarvāstravittato rāma gantāsi pitaraṃ svakam .. 25 ..
1.49.d:
अस्त्रयोगमिहस्थस्त्वं कृत्वा पुत्र शनैःशनैः ॥
सर्वास्त्रवित्ततो राम गन्तासि पितरं स्वकम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.49.m: Having practiced the yoga of divine weapons right here, my son, gradually / knowing all divine weapons, O Rāma, you shall then go to your own father.

1.49.s:
yaścaiva paraśurdivyaḥ pitrā dattastavā'nagha ..
adya prabhṛti te kṣiptaḥ karaṃ bhūyaḥ sameṣyati .. 26 ..
1.49.d:
यश्चैव परशुर्दिव्यः पित्रा दत्तस्तवाऽनघ ॥
अद्य प्रभृति ते क्षिप्तः करं भूयः समेष्यति ॥ 26 ॥
1.49.m: And the divine axe that was given to you by your father, O sinless one, / from this day onward, when cast, will return back to your hand.

1.49.s:
upalakṣaṇametacca tathā tava bhaviṣyati ..
chetsyāmi te saṃśayāṃśca nirvṛto bhava putraka .. 27 ..
1.49.d:
उपलक्षणमेतच्च तथा तव भविष्यति ॥
छेत्स्यामि ते संशयांश्च निर्वृतो भव पुत्रक ॥ 27 ॥
1.49.m: And this will likewise be a distinguishing mark for you. / I shall also cut away your doubts; be at ease, my dear son."

1.49.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktaḥ paripūrṇakāmo rāmo mahātmā jitasainyanāvaḥ ..
uvāsa tatra pramathaiḥ sametaḥ sarvāṇyathāstrāṇyanuśikṣamāṇaḥ .. 28 ..
1.49.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्तः परिपूर्णकामो रामो महात्मा जितसैन्यनावः ॥
उवास तत्र प्रमथैः समेतः सर्वाण्यथास्त्राण्यनुशिक्षमाणः ॥ 28 ॥
1.49.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been addressed thus, with his desires completely fulfilled, the great-souled Rāma, who had overcome the boat of the [enemy] army, / dwelt there together with the Pramathas, learning all the divine weapons.

1.50.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
brahmāstraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ raudramāgneyamatha vāsavam ..
astrañca nairṛtaṃ yāmyaṃ kauberamatha vāruṇam .. 1 ..
1.50.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रह्मास्त्रं वैष्णवं रौद्रमाग्नेयमथ वासवम् ॥
अस्त्रञ्च नैरृतं याम्यं कौबेरमथ वारुणम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.50.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Brahmā-weapon, the Vaiṣṇava, the Raudra, the Āgneya, and then the Vāsava; / and the Nairṛta weapon, the Yāmya, the Kaubera, and then the Vāruṇa;

1.50.s:
vāyavyamatha saumyañca sauraṃ pārvatameva ca ..
cakrāstramatha vajrāstraṃ pāśāstraṃ sārpameva ca .. 2 ..
1.50.d:
वायव्यमथ सौम्यञ्च सौरं पार्वतमेव च ॥
चक्रास्त्रमथ वज्रास्त्रं पाशास्त्रं सार्पमेव च ॥ 2 ॥
1.50.m: The Vāyavya, and then the Saumya, the Saura, and also the Pārvata; / the Cakra-weapon, and then the Vajra-weapon, the Pāśa-weapon, and also the Sārpa;

1.50.s:
gāndharvaṃ svāpanaṃ bhautaṃ tathā pāśupataṃ śubham ..
aiṣīkaṃ tarjanaṃ prāsaṃ bhāruṇḍaṃ nartanaṃ tathā .. 3 ..
1.50.d:
गान्धर्वं स्वापनं भौतं तथा पाशुपतं शुभम् ॥
ऐषीकं तर्जनं प्रासं भारुण्डं नर्तनं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.50.m: The Gāndharva, the Svāpana, the Bhauta, and the auspicious Pāśupata; / the Aiṣīka, the Tarjana, the Prāsa, the Bhāruṇḍa, and also the Nartana;

1.50.s:
astrarodhanamādityaṃ raivataṃ mānavaṃ tathā ..
akṣisaṃtarjanaṃ bhīmaṃ jṛmbhaṇaṃ rodhanaṃ tathā .. 4 ..
1.50.d:
अस्त्ररोधनमादित्यं रैवतं मानवं तथा ॥
अक्षिसंतर्जनं भीमं जृम्भणं रोधनं तथा ॥ 4 ॥
1.50.m: The Astra-rodhana, the Āditya, the Raivata, and also the Mānava; / the terrifying Akṣi-saṃtarjana, the Jṛmbhaṇa, and also the Rodhana;

1.50.s:
sauparṇamatha pārjanyaṃ rākṣasaṃ mohanaṃ tathā ..
kālāstraṃ dānavāstrañca astraṃ brahmaśirastathā .. 5 ..
1.50.d:
सौपर्णमथ पार्जन्यं राक्षसं मोहनं तथा ॥
कालास्त्रं दानवास्त्रञ्च अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.50.m: The Sauparṇa, and then the Pārjanya, the Rākṣasa, and also the Mohana; / the Kāla-weapon, the Dānava-weapon, and also the Brahmaśiras weapon.

1.50.s:
etānyanyāni cā'nyāni rāmo nivasane tataḥ ..
saprayogarahasyāni sasaṃhārāṇi cāpyatha .. 6 ..
1.50.d:
एतान्यन्यानि चाऽन्यानि रामो निवसने ततः ॥
सप्रयोगरहस्यानि ससंहाराणि चाप्यथ ॥ 6 ॥
1.50.m: These and various others Rāma then, in that abode, / along with their esoteric modes of employment and their withdrawals,

1.50.s:
ājahāra mahādevātprasādasumukhāttataḥ ..
evaṃ hi vasataḥ kālo yayau rāmasya dhīmataḥ .. 7 ..
1.50.d:
आजहार महादेवात्प्रसादसुमुखात्ततः ॥
एवं हि वसतः कालो ययौ रामस्य धीमतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.50.m: Acquired from Mahādeva, who was gracious and well-disposed. / Thus indeed time passed for the wise Rāma as he lived there.

1.50.s:
haraprasādasaṃjātavisrambho bhṛgunandanaḥ ..
dhyānāsaktaṃ haraṃ devaṃ kadācidatha dṛṣṭavān .. 8 ..
1.50.d:
हरप्रसादसंजातविस्रम्भो भृगुनन्दनः ॥
ध्यानासक्तं हरं देवं कदाचिदथ दृष्टवान् ॥ 8 ॥
1.50.m: With trust born of Hara's grace, the descendant of Bhṛgu / once saw the god Hara absorbed in meditation.

1.50.s:
dhyānaprasaktaṃ sa haraṃ samīkṣya rāmastu saṃjātakutūhalena ..
visiṣmiye dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ sa cetasā yādavavaṃśacandra .. 9 ..
1.50.d:
ध्यानप्रसक्तं स हरं समीक्ष्य रामस्तु संजातकुतूहलेन ॥
विसिष्मिये धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः स चेतसा यादववंशचन्द्र ॥ 9 ॥
1.50.m: Seeing Hara deeply engaged in meditation, Rāma, the foremost among upholders of dharma, / was struck with wonder in his mind out of curiosity, O moon of the Yādava dynasty.

1.51.s:
..mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
kailāsaśikhare ramye nānādhātuvicitrite ..
nānādrumalatākīrṇe nānāpakṣininādite .. 1 ..
1.51.d:
॥मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
कैलासशिखरे रम्ये नानाधातुविचित्रिते ॥
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णे नानापक्षिनिनादिते ॥ 1 ॥
1.51.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On the charming peak of Kailāsa, varied with various minerals, / covered with various trees and creepers, resounding with various birds,

1.51.s:
gaṃgānirjharasaṃjāte satataṃ cārunisvane ..
devadevaṃ mahādevaṃ paryapṛcchata bhārgavaḥ .. 2 ..
1.51.d:
गंगानिर्झरसंजाते सततं चारुनिस्वने ॥
देवदेवं महादेवं पर्यपृच्छत भार्गवः ॥ 2 ॥
1.51.m: Which has a continuous, pleasing sound produced by the cascades of the Gaṅgā, / the Bhārgava questioned Mahādeva, the god of gods.

1.51.s:
rāma uvāca ..
devadeva mahādeva gaṃgālulita mūrddhaja ..
śaśāṃkalekhāsaṃyukta jaṭābhārātibhāsvara .. 3 ..
1.51.d:
राम उवाच ॥
देवदेव महादेव गंगालुलित मूर्द्धज ॥
शशांकलेखासंयुक्त जटाभारातिभास्वर ॥ 3 ॥
1.51.m: Rāma said: / "O god of gods, O Mahādeva, whose hair is tossed by the Gaṅgā, / who are joined with the crescent of the moon, exceedingly resplendent with a mass of matted locks,
Who have given half of your body to Pārvatī, destroyer of Kāma, Kāla, and the body [of Smara], / destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga, inconceivable one, crusher of the teeth of Pūṣan!

1.51.s:
tvattaḥ parataraṃ devaṃ nā'nyaṃ paśyāmi kañcana ..
pūjayanti sadā liṃgaṃ tava devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 5 ..
1.51.d:
त्वत्तः परतरं देवं नाऽन्यं पश्यामि कञ्चन ॥
पूजयन्ति सदा लिंगं तव देवाः सवासवाः ॥ 5 ॥
1.51.m: I see no other god higher than you. / The gods, along with Indra, always worship your liṅga.

1.51.s:
stuvanti tvāmṛṣigaṇā dhyāyanti ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
pūjayanti tathā bhaktyā varadaṃ parameśvara .. 6 ..
1.51.d:
स्तुवन्ति त्वामृषिगणा ध्यायन्ति च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
पूजयन्ति तथा भक्त्या वरदं परमेश्वर ॥ 6 ॥
1.51.m: The hosts of sages praise you and meditate upon you again and again; / and with devotion they worship you, the boon-giver, O Supreme Lord.

1.51.s:
jagato'sya samutpattisthitisaṃhārapālane ..
tvāmekaṃ kāraṇaṃ manye tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 7 ..
1.51.d:
जगतोऽस्य समुत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहारपालने ॥
त्वामेकं कारणं मन्ये त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.51.m: In the creation, maintenance, destruction, and protection of this universe, / I consider you the sole cause; everything is established in you.

1.51.s:
kaṃ tvaṃ dhyāyasi deveśa tatra me saṃśayo mahān ..
ācakṣva tanme bhagavanyadyanugrāhyatā mayi .. 8 ..
1.51.d:
कं त्वं ध्यायसि देवेश तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥
आचक्ष्व तन्मे भगवन्यद्यनुग्राह्यता मयि ॥ 8 ॥
1.51.m: Upon whom do you meditate, O lord of the gods? In that regard, I have a great doubt. / Tell that to me, O Lord, if I am worthy of your grace.

1.51.s:
prasādasāṃmukhyatayā mayaitadvisrambhamāsādya jagatpradhāna ..
bhavantamīḍyaṃ praṇipatya mūrdhnā pṛcchāmi saṃjātakutūhalātmā .. 9 ..
1.51.d:
प्रसादसांमुख्यतया मयैतद्विस्रम्भमासाद्य जगत्प्रधान ॥
भवन्तमीड्यं प्रणिपत्य मूर्ध्ना पृच्छामि संजातकुतूहलात्मा ॥ 9 ॥
1.51.m: Having attained confidence through your being inclined to grace, O foremost of the world, / having bowed my head to you who are worthy of praise, I ask you, my mind filled with curiosity."

1.52.s:
.. śaṃkara uvāca ..
tvaduktoyamanupraśno rāma rājīvalocana ..
tvamekaḥ śrotumarho'si matto bhṛgukulodvaha .. 1 ..
1.52.d:
॥ शंकर उवाच ॥
त्वदुक्तोयमनुप्रश्नो राम राजीवलोचन ॥
त्वमेकः श्रोतुमर्होऽसि मत्तो भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥ 1 ॥
1.52.m: Śaṅkara said: / "This question asked by you, O lotus-eyed Rāma— / you alone, O upholder of the Bhṛgu family, are worthy to hear [the answer] from me.

1.52.s:
yattatparamakaṃ dhāma mama bhārgavanandana ..
yattadakṣaramavyaktaṃ paraṃ yasmānna vidyate ..
jñānajñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya cāśritam .. 2 ..
1.52.d:
यत्तत्परमकं धाम मम भार्गवनन्दन ॥
यत्तदक्षरमव्यक्तं परं यस्मान्न विद्यते ॥
ज्ञानज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य चाश्रितम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.52.m: That supreme abode of mine, O son of Bhṛgu, / which is imperishable, unmanifest, than which nothing higher exists, / knowable by knowledge, accessible by knowledge, and seated in the heart of all—

1.52.s:
tvāmahaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ cintayāmi janārdanam ..
etadrāma rahasyaṃ te yathāvatkathitaṃ vacaḥ .. 3 ..
1.52.d:
त्वामहं पुण्डरीकाक्षं चिन्तयामि जनार्दनम् ॥
एतद्राम रहस्यं ते यथावत्कथितं वचः ॥ 3 ॥
1.52.m: I meditate upon you as that lotus-eyed Janārdana. / This secret has been declared to you, O Rāma, as it truly is.

1.52.s:
ye bhaktāstamajaṃ devaṃ na te yānti parābhavam ..
tamīśamajamavyaktaṃ sarvabhūtaparāyaṇam .. 4 ..
1.52.d:
ये भक्तास्तमजं देवं न ते यान्ति पराभवम् ॥
तमीशमजमव्यक्तं सर्वभूतपरायणम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.52.m: Those who are devoted to that unborn God do not suffer defeat. / That Lord, unborn, unmanifest, the refuge of all beings,

1.52.s:
nārāyaṇamanirdeśyaṃ jagatkāraṇakāraṇam ..
sarvataḥ pāṇipādantaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukham .. 5 ..
1.52.d:
नारायणमनिर्देश्यं जगत्कारणकारणम् ॥
सर्वतः पाणिपादन्तं सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.52.m: Nārāyaṇa, indefinable, the cause of the causes of the universe, / with hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,

1.52.s:
sarvataḥ śrutimām̐lloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati ..
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam .. 6..
1.52.d:
सर्वतः श्रुतिमाम्̐ल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ॥ 6॥
1.52.m: with ears everywhere in the world, standing, encompassing all, / reflecting the qualities of all senses, yet devoid of all senses,

1.52.s:
asaktaṃ sarvataścaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca ..
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraścara eva ca .. 7 ..
1.52.d:
असक्तं सर्वतश्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरश्चर एव च ॥ 7 ॥
1.52.m: unattached, indeed everywhere, free of qualities, yet the enjoyer of qualities, / outside and inside of beings, unmoving and moving indeed,

1.52.s:
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntikaṃ ca yat ..
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam ..8..
1.52.d:
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिकं च यत् ॥
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ॥8॥
1.52.m: unknowable because of its subtlety, far away and yet near, / undivided among the divided, and standing as if divided,

1.52.s:
bhūtavartiṃ ca tajjñeyaṃ graśiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ..
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotiḥ tamasāṃ paramucyate ..9..
1.52.d:
भूतवर्तिं च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रशिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिः तमसां परमुच्यते ॥9॥
1.52.m: knowable as the sustainer of beings, devouring and producing them, / the light even of lights, it is said to be beyond darkness,

1.52.s:
anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannā'saducyate ..
prakṛtirvikṛtiryo'sau jagatāṃ bhūtabhāvanaḥ..1.52.10 ..
1.52.d:
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नाऽसदुच्यते ॥
प्रकृतिर्विकृतिर्योऽसौ जगतां भूतभावनः॥1.52.10 ॥
1.52.m: the beginningless supreme brahman, called neither being nor non-being; / he who is the primordial matter and transformation, the creator of beings of the worlds,

1.52.s:
yasmātparataraṃ nāsti taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
icchāmātramidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 11 ..
1.52.d:
यस्मात्परतरं नास्ति तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
इच्छामात्रमिदं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.52.m: than whom nothing is higher—I meditate upon that God. / All this threefold world, with the moving and unmoving, is his mere will—

1.52.s:
yasya devādidevasya taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
yasminsarvaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ yaḥ sarvaṃ sarvataśca yaḥ .. 12 ..
1.52.d:
यस्य देवादिदेवस्य तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
यस्मिन्सर्वं यतः सर्वं यः सर्वं सर्वतश्च यः ॥ 12 ॥
1.52.m: I meditate upon that God of gods, that God / in whom is all, from whom is all, who is all, and who is everywhere,

1.52.s:
yaśca sarvamayo nityastaṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
yogīśvaraṃ padmanābhaṃ viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ jagatpatim .. 13 ..
1.52.d:
यश्च सर्वमयो नित्यस्तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
योगीश्वरं पद्मनाभं विष्णुं जिष्णुं जगत्पतिम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.52.m: and who is eternal and consists of all—I meditate upon that God, / the Lord of Yogins, the lotus-navelled, Viṣṇu, victorious, the Lord of the world,

1.52.s:
jagannāthaṃ viśālākṣaṃ cintayāmi jagadgurum ..
śuciṃ śucipadaṃ haṃsaṃ tatparaṃ parameṣṭhinam .. 14 ..
1.52.d:
जगन्नाथं विशालाक्षं चिन्तयामि जगद्गुरुम् ॥
शुचिं शुचिपदं हंसं तत्परं परमेष्ठिनम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.52.m: Lord of the universe, large-eyed, I meditate upon the Teacher of the universe, / the pure, the holy abode, the Haṃsa, the supreme Parameṣṭhin.

1.52.s:
yuktā sarvātmanā''tmānaṃ taṃ prapadye prajāpatim ..
yasminviśvāni bhūtāni tiṣṭhanti ca viśanti ca .. 15 ..
1.52.d:
युक्ता सर्वात्मना'ऽत्मानं तं प्रपद्ये प्रजापतिम् ॥
यस्मिन्विश्वानि भूतानि तिष्ठन्ति च विशन्ति च ॥ 15 ॥
1.52.m: Disciplined with my whole self, I take refuge in that Self, the Prajāpati / in whom all beings abide and enter,

1.52.s:
guṇabhūtāni bhūteśe sūtre maṇigaṇā iva ..
yasminnitye tate tantau dṛṣṭe khagiva tiṣṭhati .. 16 ..
1.52.d:
गुणभूतानि भूतेशे सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
यस्मिन्नित्ये तते तन्तौ दृष्टे खगिव तिष्ठति ॥ 16 ॥
1.52.m: subordinate in the Lord of beings, like rows of pearls on a thread, / upon which eternal, outstretched thread, once seen, […] stands like a bird,

1.52.s:
sadasadgrathitaṃ viśvaṃ viśvāṃge viśvakarmaṇi ..
hariṃ sahasraśirasaṃ sahasracaraṇekṣaṇam .. 17 ..
1.52.d:
सदसद्ग्रथितं विश्वं विश्वांगे विश्वकर्मणि ॥
हरिं सहस्रशिरसं सहस्रचरणेक्षणम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.52.m: the universe, woven of being and non-being, in the all-limbed maker of all— / Hari, thousand-headed, thousand-footed and -eyed,

1.52.s:
prāhurnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ yaṃ viśvasya parāyaṇam ..
aṇīyasāmaṇīyāṃsaṃ sthaviṣṭhañca sthavīyasām .. 18 ..
1.52.d:
प्राहुर्नारायणं देवं यं विश्वस्य परायणम् ॥
अणीयसामणीयांसं स्थविष्ठञ्च स्थवीयसाम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.52.m: whom they call God Nārāyaṇa, the supreme refuge of the universe, / more subtle than the subtlest, larger than the largest,

1.52.s:
garīyasāṃ gariṣṭhañca śreṣṭhañca śreyasāmapi ..
yaṃ vākeṣvanuvākeṣu niṣatsūpaniṣatsvapi .. 19 ..
1.52.d:
गरीयसां गरिष्ठञ्च श्रेष्ठञ्च श्रेयसामपि ॥
यं वाकेष्वनुवाकेषु निषत्सूपनिषत्स्वपि ॥ 19 ॥
1.52.m: mightier than the mightiest, better than the best, / whom in vākas, in anuvākas, in niṣads and upaniṣads

1.52.s:
gṛṇanti satyakarmāṇaṃ satyaṃ satyeṣu sāmasu ..
caturbhiścaturātmānaṃ sattvasthaṃ sāttvatāṃ patim ..1.52.20..
1.52.d:
गृणन्ति सत्यकर्माणं सत्यं सत्येषु सामसु ॥
चतुर्भिश्चतुरात्मानं सत्त्वस्थं सात्त्वतां पतिम् ॥1.52.20॥
1.52.m: they celebrate as of true action, the Truth among the true Sāman chants, / fourfold in self by the four, abiding in sattva, the Lord of the Sātvatas,

1.52.s:
yaṃ divyairdevamarcanti guhyaiḥ paramanāmabhiḥ ..
yamananyo vyapetāśīrātmānaṃ vītakalmaṣam .. 21 ..
1.52.d:
यं दिव्यैर्देवमर्चन्ति गुह्यैः परमनामभिः ॥
यमनन्यो व्यपेताशीरात्मानं वीतकल्मषम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.52.m: whom as God they worship with divine, secret, supreme names, / whom with undivided mind, rid of desire and freed of stain,

1.52.s:
iṣṭvānantyāya govindaṃ paśyatyātmanyavasthitam ..
purāṇaḥ puruṣaḥ prokto brahmā prokto yugādiṣu .. 22 ..
1.52.d:
इष्ट्वानन्त्याय गोविन्दं पश्यत्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ॥
पुराणः पुरुषः प्रोक्तो ब्रह्मा प्रोक्तो युगादिषु ॥ 22 ॥
1.52.m: having sacrificed to Govinda for the sake of the infinite, one beholds situated in the self; / declared the ancient Cosmic Person, declared Brahmā at the beginning of the ages,

1.52.s:
kṣaye saṃkarṣaṇaḥ proktastamupāsyamupāsmahe ..
yamekaṃ bahudhātmānaṃ prādurbhūtamadhokṣajam .. 23 ..
1.52.d:
क्षये संकर्षणः प्रोक्तस्तमुपास्यमुपास्महे ॥
यमेकं बहुधात्मानं प्रादुर्भूतमधोक्षजम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.52.m: declared Saṃkarṣaṇa at the dissolution—we worship him, the worthy of worship; / whom, the one Self, manifested manifoldly as Adhokṣaja,

1.52.s:
nānyabhaktāḥ kriyāvanto yajante sarvakāmadam ..
yamāhurjagatāṃ kośaṃ yasminsannihitāḥ prajāḥ ..24..
1.52.d:
नान्यभक्ताः क्रियावन्तो यजन्ते सर्वकामदम् ॥
यमाहुर्जगतां कोशं यस्मिन्सन्निहिताः प्रजाः ॥24॥
1.52.m: men of action with no other devotion sacrifice to, the granter of all desires; / whom they call the treasury of the worlds, in whom creatures are placed,

1.52.s:
yasmiṃllokāḥ sphurantīme jāle śakunayo yathā ..
ṛtamekākṣaraṃ brahma yattatsadasataḥ param .. 25 ..
1.52.d:
यस्मिंल्लोकाः स्फुरन्तीमे जाले शकुनयो यथा ॥
ऋतमेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्तत्सदसतः परम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.52.m: in whom these worlds flutter like birds in a net; / the truth, the single-syllabled brahman, which is beyond being and non-being,

1.52.s:
anādimadhyaparyantaṃ na devā narṣayo viduḥ ..
yaṃ surāsuragandharvāssaṃsiddharṣimahoragāḥ..26..
1.52.d:
अनादिमध्यपर्यन्तं न देवा नर्षयो विदुः ॥
यं सुरासुरगन्धर्वास्संसिद्धर्षिमहोरगाः॥26॥
1.52.m: without beginning, middle, or end, whom neither gods nor seers know; / whom gods, asuras, gandharvas, perfected ones, seers, and great serpents,

1.52.s:
prayatā nityamarcanti paramaṃ duḥkhabheṣajam ..
anādinidhanaṃ devamātmayoniṃ sanātanam .. 27 ..
1.52.d:
प्रयता नित्यमर्चन्ति परमं दुःखभेषजम् ॥
अनादिनिधनं देवमात्मयोनिं सनातनम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.52.m: striving, ever worship, the supreme medicine for sorrow; / the God without beginning or end, self-originated, eternal,

1.52.s:
apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum ..
ativāyvindrakarmāṇaṃ cā'tisūryāgnitejasam .. 28 ..
1.52.d:
अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् ॥
अतिवाय्विन्द्रकर्माणं चाऽतिसूर्याग्नितेजसम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.52.m: inconceivable, unknowable, Hari, Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, / whose deeds surpass Vāyu and Indra, whose splendour surpasses the sun and fire,

1.52.s:
atibuddhīndriyagrāmaṃ taṃ prapadye prajāpatim ..
yaṃ vai viśvasya karttāraṃ jagatastasthuṣāṃ patim .. 29 ..
1.52.d:
अतिबुद्धीन्द्रियग्रामं तं प्रपद्ये प्रजापतिम् ॥
यं वै विश्वस्य कर्त्तारं जगतस्तस्थुषां पतिम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.52.m: who transcends the collection of intellect and senses—in that Prajāpati I take refuge; / whom indeed they call the maker of all, the Lord of the moving and unmoving world,

1.52.s:
vadanti jagato'dhyakṣamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ padam ..
yasyāgnirāsyaṃ dyaurmūrdhā khaṃ nābhiścaraṇau kṣitiḥ .. 1.52.30 ..
1.52.d:
वदन्ति जगतोऽध्यक्षमक्षरं परमं पदम् ॥
यस्याग्निरास्यं द्यौर्मूर्धा खं नाभिश्चरणौ क्षितिः ॥ 1.52.30 ॥
1.52.m: the overseer of the world, imperishable, the supreme abode; / whose mouth is fire, whose head is heaven, whose navel is space, whose feet are the earth,

1.52.s:
candrādityau ca nayane taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
yasya trilokī jaṭhare yasya kāṣṭhāśca vāhanāḥ ..31..
1.52.d:
चन्द्रादित्यौ च नयने तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
यस्य त्रिलोकी जठरे यस्य काष्ठाश्च वाहनाः ॥31॥
1.52.m: and whose eyes are the moon and the sun—I meditate upon that God; / in whose belly are the three worlds, whose mounts are the cardinal points,

1.52.s:
yasya śvāsaśca pavanastaṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
viṣaye vartamānānāṃ yaṃ taṃ vaiśeṣikairguṇaiḥ .. 32 ..
1.52.d:
यस्य श्वासश्च पवनस्तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
विषये वर्तमानानां यं तं वैशेषिकैर्गुणैः ॥ 32 ॥
1.52.m: and whose breath is the wind—I meditate upon that God; / whom, for those existing in the realm of sense-objects, through distinguishing qualities

1.52.s:
prāhurviṣayagoptāraṃ taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
paraḥ kālātparo yajñātparassadasataśca yaḥ .. 33 ..
1.52.d:
प्राहुर्विषयगोप्तारं तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
परः कालात्परो यज्ञात्परस्सदसतश्च यः ॥ 33 ॥
1.52.m: they call the protector of sense-objects—I meditate upon that God; / who is beyond time, beyond sacrifice, and beyond being and non-being,

1.52.s:
anādirādirviśvasya taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..
padbhyāṃ yasya kṣitirjātā śrotrābhyāñca tathā diśaḥ ..34..
1.52.d:
अनादिरादिर्विश्वस्य तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥
पद्भ्यां यस्य क्षितिर्जाता श्रोत्राभ्याञ्च तथा दिशः ॥34॥
1.52.m: the beginningless origin of the universe—I meditate upon that God; / from whose feet was born the earth, and likewise from his ears the directions,

1.52.s:
pūrvabhāge divaṃ yasya taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham..
nābhyāṃ yasyāntarikṣasya nāsābhyāṃ pavanasya ca .. 35 ..
1.52.d:
पूर्वभागे दिवं यस्य तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम्॥
नाभ्यां यस्यान्तरिक्षस्य नासाभ्यां पवनस्य च ॥ 35 ॥
1.52.m: from whose upper part [came] heaven—I meditate upon that God; / from whose navel came the atmosphere, and from his nostrils the wind,

1.52.s: prasvedādambhasāṃ janma taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham ..36..
1.52.d: प्रस्वेदादम्भसां जन्म तं देवं चिन्तयाम्यहम् ॥36॥
1.52.m: from whose sweat was the birth of the waters—I meditate upon that God,

1.52.s:
varāhaśīrṣaṃ narasiṃharūpaṃ deveśvaraṃ vāmanarūparūpam..
trailokyanāthaṃ varadaṃ vareṇyaṃ taṃ rāma nityaṃ manasā nato'smi..37..
1.52.d:
वराहशीर्षं नरसिंहरूपं देवेश्वरं वामनरूपरूपम्॥
त्रैलोक्यनाथं वरदं वरेण्यं तं राम नित्यं मनसा नतोऽस्मि॥37॥
1.52.m: who has the head of a boar, the form of Narasiṃha, the Lord of gods, who took the form of the Dwarf, / the Lord of the three worlds, the giver of boons, the choice—to him, O Rāma, I bow down constantly in my mind;

1.52.s:
vāktrādyasya brāhmaṇāssaṃprasūtā yadvakṣasaḥ kṣatriyāḥ saṃprasūtāḥ ..
yasyoruyugmācca tathaiva vaiśyāḥ padbhyāṃ tathā yasya śūdrāḥ prasūtāḥ ..38..
1.52.d:
वाक्त्राद्यस्य ब्राह्मणास्संप्रसूता यद्वक्षसः क्षत्रियाः संप्रसूताः ॥
यस्योरुयुग्माच्च तथैव वैश्याः पद्भ्यां तथा यस्य शूद्राः प्रसूताः ॥38॥
1.52.m: from whose mouth brahmins were born, from whose chest kṣatriyas were born, / from whose pair of thighs likewise vaiśyas, and from whose feet śūdras were born,

1.52.s:
vyāptaṃ tathā yena jagatsamagraṃ vibhūtibhirbhūtabhavodbhavena ..
devādhināthaṃ varadaṃ vareṇyaṃ taṃ rāma nityaṃ manasā nato'smi..39..
1.52.d:
व्याप्तं तथा येन जगत्समग्रं विभूतिभिर्भूतभवोद्भवेन ॥
देवाधिनाथं वरदं वरेण्यं तं राम नित्यं मनसा नतोऽस्मि॥39॥
1.52.m: by whom likewise the entire world was pervaded through his divine powers, the source of what has been and what will be, / the Sovereign of gods, the giver of boons, the choice—to him, O Rāma, I bow down constantly in my mind.

1.53.s:
rāma uvāca ..
varāhaṃ narasiṃhaṃ ca vāmanaṃ ca maheśvara..
tvatto'haṃ śrotumicchāmi prādurbhāvānmahātmanaḥ ..1..
1.53.d:
राम उवाच ॥
वराहं नरसिंहं च वामनं च महेश्वर॥
त्वत्तोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रादुर्भावान्महात्मनः ॥1॥
1.53.m: Rāma said: / The Boar, Narasiṃha, and the Dwarf, O Maheśvara— / I wish to hear from you about these manifestations of the Great Self.

1.53.s:
śaṅkara uvāca..
aditiśca ditiścaiva dve bhārye kaśyapasya ca ..
aditirjanayāmāsa devānindrapurogamān ..2..
1.53.d:
शङ्कर उवाच॥
अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव द्वे भार्ये कश्यपस्य च ॥
अदितिर्जनयामास देवानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् ॥2॥
1.53.m: Śaṅkara said: / Aditi and Diti were the two wives of Kaśyapa. / Aditi gave birth to the gods headed by Indra,

1.53.s:
ditiśca janayāmāsa dvau putrau bhīmavikramau ..
hiraṇyākṣaṃ durādharṣaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ tathā .. 3 ..
1.53.d:
दितिश्च जनयामास द्वौ पुत्रौ भीमविक्रमौ ॥
हिरण्याक्षं दुराधर्षं हिरण्यकशिपुं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.53.m: and Diti gave birth to two sons of terrible prowess: / Hiraṇyākṣa, hard to assail, and likewise Hiraṇyakaśipu.

1.53.s:
tato'bhiṣiktavāñchakraṃ devarājye prajāpatiḥ ..
dānavānāṃ tathā rājye hiraṇyākṣaṃ balotkaṭam .. 4 ..
1.53.d:
ततोऽभिषिक्तवाञ्छक्रं देवराज्ये प्रजापतिः ॥
दानवानां तथा राज्ये हिरण्याक्षं बलोत्कटम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.53.m: Then Prajāpati consecrated Śakra to the kingship over the gods, / and likewise the excessively strong Hiraṇyākṣa to the kingship over the Dānavas.

1.53.s:
abhiṣicya tayoḥ prādātsvargaṃ pātālameva ca..
pātālaṃ śāsati tathā hiraṇyākṣe mahāsure ..5..
1.53.d:
अभिषिच्य तयोः प्रादात्स्वर्गं पातालमेव च॥
पातालं शासति तथा हिरण्याक्षे महासुरे ॥5॥
1.53.m:
Having consecrated them, he gave heaven and the netherworld to the two.
And as the great Asura Hiraṇyākṣa ruled the netherworld,

1.53.s:
dharādhārā dharāṃ tyaktvā khamutpetū rayātpurā..
pakṣavanto mahābhāga nūnaṃ bhāvyarthacoditāḥ .. ..6..
1.53.d:
धराधारा धरां त्यक्त्वा खमुत्पेतू रयात्पुरा॥
पक्षवन्तो महाभाग नूनं भाव्यर्थचोदिताः ॥ ॥6॥
1.53.m:
the mountains formerly abandoned the earth and flew up into the sky with speed,
having wings, O fortunate one, surely impelled by destiny.

1.53.s:
dharādharaparityaktā dharā calanibandhanā ..
yadā tadā daityapuraṃ sakalaṃ vyāptamambhasā .. 7 ..
1.53.d:
धराधरपरित्यक्ता धरा चलनिबन्धना ॥
यदा तदा दैत्यपुरं सकलं व्याप्तमम्भसा ॥ 7 ॥
1.53.m:
When the earth, abandoned by the mountains, lost its stability,
then the entire city of the Daityas was flooded with water.

1.53.s:
dṛṣṭvaiva svapuraṃ vyāptamambhasā ditijottamaḥ ..
sainyamudyojayāmāsa jātaśaṅkaḥ surānprati .. 8 ..
1.53.d:
दृष्ट्वैव स्वपुरं व्याप्तमम्भसा दितिजोत्तमः ॥
सैन्यमुद्योजयामास जातशङ्कः सुरान्प्रति ॥ 8 ॥
1.53.m:
Seeing his own city submerged in water, the foremost of Diti's sons,
aroused with suspicion toward the gods, mobilized his army.

1.53.s:
udyuktena sa sainyena daityānāṃ caturaṃgiṇā ..
vijitya tridaśāñjanye ājahāra triviṣṭapam .. .. 9 ..
1.53.d:
उद्युक्तेन स सैन्येन दैत्यानां चतुरंगिणा ॥
विजित्य त्रिदशाञ्जन्ये आजहार त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ ॥ 9 ॥
1.53.m:
With the prepared fourfold army of the Daityas,
he conquered the thirty [gods] in battle and seized heaven.

1.53.s:
hṛtādhikārāstridaśā jagmuḥ śaraṇamañjasā ..
devarājaṃ puraskṛtya vāsudevamajaṃ vibhum .. 1.53.10 ..
1.53.d:
हृताधिकारास्त्रिदशा जग्मुः शरणमञ्जसा ॥
देवराजं पुरस्कृत्य वासुदेवमजं विभुम् ॥ 1.53.10 ॥
1.53.m:
Deprived of their authority, the thirty [gods] straightaway went for refuge,
placing the king of the gods at their head, to Vāsudeva, the unborn, all-pervading Lord.

1.53.s:
tridaśāñcharaṇaṃ prāptā nhiraṇyākṣavivāsitān..
saṃyojyā'bhayadānena visasarja janārdanaḥ .. 11 ..
1.53.d:
त्रिदशाञ्छरणं प्राप्ता न्हिरण्याक्षविवासितान्॥
संयोज्याऽभयदानेन विससर्ज जनार्दनः ॥ 11 ॥
1.53.m:
Having granted protection to the thirty [gods] who had sought refuge,
exiled by Hiraṇyākṣa, Janārdana dismissed them.

1.53.s:
visṛjya tridaśānsarvāñcintayāmāsa keśavaḥ ..
kinnu rūpamahaṃ kṛtvā ghātayiṣye surārdanam ..12..
1.53.d:
विसृज्य त्रिदशान्सर्वाञ्चिन्तयामास केशवः ॥
किन्नु रूपमहं कृत्वा घातयिष्ये सुरार्दनम् ॥12॥
1.53.m:
Having dismissed all the thirty [gods], Keśava reflected:
'What form should I assume to slay the tormentor of the gods?

1.53.s:
tiryaṅmanuṣyadevānāmavadhyaḥ sa surāntakaḥ ..
brahmaṇo varadānena tasmāttasya vadhepsayā ..13..
1.53.d:
तिर्यङ्मनुष्यदेवानामवध्यः स सुरान्तकः ॥
ब्रह्मणो वरदानेन तस्मात्तस्य वधेप्सया ॥13॥
1.53.m:
That slayer of the gods is invulnerable to animals, men, and gods
by the boon granted by Brahmā; therefore, desiring his death,

1.53.s:
nṛvarāho bhaviṣyāmi na devo na ca mānuṣaḥ ..
tiryagrūpeṇa caivāhaṃ ghātayiṣyāmi taṃ tataḥ .. 14 ..
1.53.d:
नृवराहो भविष्यामि न देवो न च मानुषः ॥
तिर्यग्रूपेण चैवाहं घातयिष्यामि तं ततः ॥ 14 ॥
1.53.m:
I shall become a man-boar—neither god nor human—
and in the form of an animal I shall then slay him.'

1.53.s:
etāvaduktvā saṃgena nṛvarāho'bhavatprabhuḥ ..
cūrṇitāñjanaśailābhastapta jāmbūnadāmbaraḥ .. 15 ..
1.53.d:
एतावदुक्त्वा संगेन नृवराहोऽभवत्प्रभुः ॥
चूर्णिताञ्जनशैलाभस्तप्त जाम्बूनदाम्बरः ॥ 15 ॥
1.53.m:
Having spoken thus, the Lord instantly became a man-boar,
resembling a mountain of powdered collyrium, clad in heated gold,

1.53.s:
yamunāvarttakṛṣṇāṅgaḥ tadāvartatanūruhaḥ ..
tadogha iva durvāryyastatpitrā tejasā samaḥ .. 16 ..
1.53.d:
यमुनावर्त्तकृष्णाङ्गः तदावर्ततनूरुहः ॥
तदोघ इव दुर्वार्य्यस्तत्पित्रा तेजसा समः ॥ 16 ॥
1.53.m:
with dark limbs like the eddies of the Yamunā, his body hair like its whirlpools,
irresistible like its current, equal in splendour to its father [the Sun],

1.53.s:
tatpravāha ivākṣobhyasta tpravāha ivaughavān ..
tatpravāhāmalatanustatpravāhamanoharaḥ .. 17 ..
1.53.d:
तत्प्रवाह इवाक्षोभ्यस्त त्प्रवाह इवौघवान् ॥
तत्प्रवाहामलतनुस्तत्प्रवाहमनोहरः ॥ 17 ॥
1.53.m:
unshakable like its flow, mighty like its rush,
with a spotless body like its stream, delightful like its flow,

1.53.s:
sajalāñjanakṛṣṇāṅgaḥ sajalāmbudasacchaviḥ ..
pītavāsāstadā bhāti savi dyudiva toyadaḥ .. 18 ..
1.53.d:
सजलाञ्जनकृष्णाङ्गः सजलाम्बुदसच्छविः ॥
पीतवासास्तदा भाति सवि द्युदिव तोयदः ॥ 18 ॥
1.53.m:
with limbs dark as wet collyrium, possessing the complexion of a rain-laden cloud;
wearing yellow garments, he then shone like a rain-cloud with lightning.

1.53.s:
urasā dhārayanhāraṃ śaśāṅkasadṛśacchaviḥ ..
śuśubhe sarvabhūtātmā sabalāka ivāmbudaḥ .. 19 ..
1.53.d:
उरसा धारयन्हारं शशाङ्कसदृशच्छविः ॥
शुशुभे सर्वभूतात्मा सबलाक इवाम्बुदः ॥ 19 ॥
1.53.m:
Bearing a necklace on his chest, having a lustre like the moon,
the Self of all beings shone like a cloud accompanied by cranes.

1.53.s:
śaśāṅkalekhāvimale daṃṣṭre tasya virejatuḥ ..
meghāntaritabimbasya dvau bhāgau śaśino yathā .. 1.53.20 ..
1.53.d:
शशाङ्कलेखाविमले दंष्ट्रे तस्य विरेजतुः ॥
मेघान्तरितबिम्बस्य द्वौ भागौ शशिनो यथा ॥ 1.53.20 ॥
1.53.m:
His two tusks gleamed, pure as the crescent moon,
like two parts of the moon whose disk is veiled by clouds.

1.53.s:
karābhyāṃ dhārayanbhāti śaṅkhacakre janārdanaḥ .
candrārkasadṛśe rāma pādacārīva parvataḥ .. 21 ..
1.53.d:
कराभ्यां धारयन्भाति शङ्खचक्रे जनार्दनः ।
चन्द्रार्कसदृशे राम पादचारीव पर्वतः ॥ 21 ॥
1.53.m:
Bearing the conch and discus in his hands, Janārdana shone,
like the moon and the sun, O Rāma, as if a mountain walking on foot,

1.53.s:
mahājīmūtasaṃkāśo mahājīmūtasannibhaḥ ..
mahajīmūtavadvegī mahābalaparākramaḥ .. 22 ..
1.53.d:
महाजीमूतसंकाशो महाजीमूतसन्निभः ॥
महजीमूतवद्वेगी महाबलपराक्रमः ॥ 22 ॥
1.53.m:
resembling a great rain-cloud, looking like a great rain-cloud,
having the speed of a great rain-cloud, endowed with great strength and prowess.

1.53.s:
dānavendravadhākāṅkṣī hiraṇyākṣasabhāṃ yayau ..
hiraṇyākṣo'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛvarāhaṃ janārdanam .. 23 ..
1.53.d:
दानवेन्द्रवधाकाङ्क्षी हिरण्याक्षसभां ययौ ॥
हिरण्याक्षोऽपि तं दृष्ट्वा नृवराहं जनार्दनम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.53.m:
Desiring the death of the lord of the Dānavas, he went to Hiraṇyākṣa’s assembly hall.
And seeing Janārdana as the man-boar, Hiraṇyākṣa

1.53.s:
dānavām̐ścodayāmāsa tiryagjātamapūrvakam ..
gṛhyatāṃ vadhyatāṃ caiva krīḍārthaṃ sthāpyatāṃ tathā .. 24 ..
1.53.d:
दानवाम्̐श्चोदयामास तिर्यग्जातमपूर्वकम् ॥
गृह्यतां वध्यतां चैव क्रीडार्थं स्थाप्यतां तथा ॥ 24 ॥
1.53.m:
urged on the Dānavas against that unprecedented animal-born creature:
'Let it be seized, let it be killed, and let it be kept for sport!'

1.53.s:
ityevamuktaḥ saṃrabdhaḥ pāśahastām̐stu dānavān ..
jighṛkṣamāṇāṃścakreṇa jaghāna śataśo raṇe .. 25 ..
1.53.d:
इत्येवमुक्तः संरब्धः पाशहस्ताम्̐स्तु दानवान् ॥
जिघृक्षमाणांश्चक्रेण जघान शतशो रणे ॥ 25 ॥
1.53.m:
Addressed thus, the furious [Lord] struck down in battle with his discus by the hundreds
those Dānavas with nooses in hand who sought to seize him.

1.53.s:
hanyamāneṣu daityeṣu hiraṇyākṣo'tha dānavān ..
codayāmāsa saṃrabdhānvarāhādhikakāraṇāt .. 26 ..
1.53.d:
हन्यमानेषु दैत्येषु हिरण्याक्षोऽथ दानवान् ॥
चोदयामास संरब्धान्वराहाधिककारणात् ॥ 26 ॥
1.53.m:
As the Daityas were being slain, Hiraṇyākṣa then urged on
the furious Dānavas on account of the extraordinary boar.

1.53.s:
coditā dānavendreṇa dāna vā śastrapāṇayaḥ ..
pravavarṣustathā devaṃ śastravarṣeṇa keśavam .. 27 ..
1.53.d:
चोदिता दानवेन्द्रेण दान वा शस्त्रपाणयः ॥
प्रववर्षुस्तथा देवं शस्त्रवर्षेण केशवम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.53.m:
Urged by the lord of the Dānavas, the Dānavas with weapons in hand
rained down a shower of weapons upon the god Keśava.

1.53.s:
daityāḥ śastranipātena devadevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
naiva śekurvṛthā kartuṃ yatnavanto'pi nirbhayāḥ .. 28 ..
1.53.d:
दैत्याः शस्त्रनिपातेन देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
नैव शेकुर्वृथा कर्तुं यत्नवन्तोऽपि निर्भयाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.53.m:
With their shower of weapons, the Daityas, though striving and fearless,
were entirely unable to render the God of gods, the discus-wielder, ineffectual.

1.53.s:
hanyamāno'pi daityendrairdānavānmadhusūdanaḥ..
jaghāna cakreṇa tadā śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..29..
1.53.d:
हन्यमानोऽपि दैत्येन्द्रैर्दानवान्मधुसूदनः॥
जघान चक्रेण तदा शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥29॥
1.53.m:
Though struck by the leaders of the Daityas, Madhusūdana
then slaughtered the Dānavas with his discus by hundreds and thousands.

1.53.s:
hanyamāneṣu sainyeṣu hiraṇyākṣaḥ svayaṃ tataḥ ..
utthāya dhanuṣā devaṃ pravavarṣa surottamam .. 1.53.30 ..
1.53.d:
हन्यमानेषु सैन्येषु हिरण्याक्षः स्वयं ततः ॥
उत्थाय धनुषा देवं प्रववर्ष सुरोत्तमम् ॥ 1.53.30 ॥
1.53.m:
As his armies were being destroyed, Hiraṇyākṣa himself then
arose and showered arrows from his bow upon the god, the highest of the gods.

1.53.s:
hiraṇyākṣastu tāndṛṣṭvā viphalām̐śca śilī mukhān ..
śilīmukhābhānsaṃpaśyansamapaśyanmahadbhayam .. 31 ..
1.53.d:
हिरण्याक्षस्तु तान्दृष्ट्वा विफलाम्̐श्च शिली मुखान् ॥
शिलीमुखाभान्संपश्यन्समपश्यन्महद्भयम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.53.m:
Hiraṇyākṣa, seeing those arrows rendered futile,
and seeing [arrows] resembling bees, beheld a great terror.

1.53.s:
tato'strairyuyudhe tena devadevena cakriṇā ..
tānyasya phalahīnāni cakāra bhagavān svayam .. 32 ..
1.53.d:
ततोऽस्त्रैर्युयुधे तेन देवदेवेन चक्रिणा ॥
तान्यस्य फलहीनानि चकार भगवान् स्वयम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.53.m:
Then he fought with divine weapons against that God of gods, the wielder of the discus;
the Blessed One himself rendered them all futile.

1.53.s:
tato gadāṃ kāñcanapaṭṭanaddhāṃ vibhūṣitāṃ kiṃkiṇijālasaṃghaiḥ ..
cikṣepa daityādhipatiḥ sa ghorāṃ tāṃ cā'pi devo viphalīcakāra .. 33 ..
1.53.d:
ततो गदां काञ्चनपट्टनद्धां विभूषितां किंकिणिजालसंघैः ॥
चिक्षेप दैत्याधिपतिः स घोरां तां चाऽपि देवो विफलीचकार ॥ 33 ॥
1.53.m:
Then the ruler of the Daityas hurled a terrible mace, bound with golden bands
and adorned with clusters of tinkling bells; and the god rendered that futile as well.

1.53.s:
śaktiṃ tataḥ paṭṭavinaddhamadhyāmulkānalābhāṃ tapanīyacitrām ..
cikṣepa daityassa varāhakāye huṅkāradagdhā nipapāta sā ca.. .. 34 ..
1.53.d:
शक्तिं ततः पट्टविनद्धमध्यामुल्कानलाभां तपनीयचित्राम् ॥
चिक्षेप दैत्यस्स वराहकाये हुङ्कारदग्धा निपपात सा च॥ ॥ 34 ॥
1.53.m:
Then the Daitya hurled a spear, its middle bound with silk bands,
blazing like a meteor's fire and bright with gold, at the boar's body; and consumed by his roar, it fell.

1.53.s:
tatastriśūlaṃ jvalitāgraśūlaṃ sa śīghragaṃ devagaṇasya saṃkhye ..
daityādhipastasya sajarja vegādavekṣitaḥ so'pi jagāma bhūmim .. 35 ..
1.53.d:
ततस्त्रिशूलं ज्वलिताग्रशूलं स शीघ्रगं देवगणस्य संख्ये ॥
दैत्याधिपस्तस्य सजर्ज वेगादवेक्षितः सोऽपि जगाम भूमिम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.53.m:
Then in battle the ruler of the Daityas swiftly hurled at him a trident
with blazing points, swift-flying, [feared by] the host of gods; but when merely looked at, it fell to the earth.

1.53.s:
śaṅkhasvanenā'pi janārdanaśca vidrāvya daityānsakalānmahātmā ..
sakuṇḍalaṃ daityagaṇādhipasya ciccheda cakreṇa śiraḥ prasahya .. 36 ..
1.53.d:
शङ्खस्वनेनाऽपि जनार्दनश्च विद्राव्य दैत्यान्सकलान्महात्मा ॥
सकुण्डलं दैत्यगणाधिपस्य चिच्छेद चक्रेण शिरः प्रसह्य ॥ 36 ॥
1.53.m:
And routing all the Daityas with the blast of his conch,
the great-souled Janārdana forcibly cut off the earringed head of the ruler of the Daitya hosts with his discus.

1.53.s:
nipātite daityapatau sa devaḥ saṃpūjitaḥ śakrapitāmahābhyām ..
mayā ca sarvaistridaśaiḥ sametaijargāma kāṣṭhāṃ manasā tvabhīṣṭām .. 37 ..
1.53.d:
निपातिते दैत्यपतौ स देवः संपूजितः शक्रपितामहाभ्याम् ॥
मया च सर्वैस्त्रिदशैः समेतैजर्गाम काष्ठां मनसा त्वभीष्टाम् ॥ 37 ॥
1.53.m:
When the ruler of the Daityas was struck down, that god, worshipped by Śakra and the Grandfather,
and by me together with all the thirty [gods], departed to the region desired in his heart.

1.53.s:
śakropi labdhvā tridivaṃ mahātmā ciccheda pakṣāndharaṇīdharāṇām ..
rarakṣa cemāṃ sakalāṃ trilokīṃ dharmeṇa dharmajñabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ .. 38 .. ..
1.53.d:
शक्रोपि लब्ध्वा त्रिदिवं महात्मा चिच्छेद पक्षान्धरणीधराणाम् ॥
ररक्ष चेमां सकलां त्रिलोकीं धर्मेण धर्मज्ञभृतां वरिष्ठः ॥ 38 ॥ ॥
1.53.m:
Śakra too, the great-souled, having regained heaven, severed the wings of the mountains
and protected all these three worlds with dharma, foremost among upholders of dharma.

1.54.s:
.. śaṅkara uvāca ..
hiraṇyākṣe hate daitye bhrātā tasya mahātmanaḥ ..
hiraṇyakaśipurnāma cakārograṃ mahattapaḥ .. 1 ..
1.54.d:
॥ शङ्कर उवाच ॥
हिरण्याक्षे हते दैत्ये भ्राता तस्य महात्मनः ॥
हिरण्यकशिपुर्नाम चकारोग्रं महत्तपः ॥ 1 ॥
1.54.m:
Śaṅkara said:
When the Daitya Hiraṇyākṣa was slain, the brother of that great-souled one,
named Hiraṇyakaśipu, performed severe and great austerities.

1.54.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca ..
japopavāsanirataḥ snānamaunāśritavrataḥ .. 2 ..
1.54.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च ॥
जपोपवासनिरतः स्नानमौनाश्रितव्रतः ॥ 2 ॥
1.54.m:
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years,
devoted to chanting and fasting, maintaining the vow of bathing and silence,

1.54.s:
tapaḥśamadamābhyāṃ ca brahmacaryeṇa cā'nagha ..
brahmā prītamanāstasya svayamāgatya bhārgava .. .. 3 ..
1.54.d:
तपःशमदमाभ्यां च ब्रह्मचर्येण चाऽनघ ॥
ब्रह्मा प्रीतमनास्तस्य स्वयमागत्य भार्गव ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
1.54.m:
through austerity, tranquility, self-restraint, and celibacy, O sinless one;
Brahmā, pleased in his heart, came in person to him, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

1.54.s:
vimānenā'rkavarṇena haṃsayuktena bhāsvatā ..
ādityaissahitaḥ sādhyaissahito marudaśvibhiḥ .. 4 ..
1.54.d:
विमानेनाऽर्कवर्णेन हंसयुक्तेन भास्वता ॥
आदित्यैस्सहितः साध्यैस्सहितो मरुदश्विभिः ॥ 4 ॥
1.54.m:
in a brilliant aerial chariot having the colour of the sun and yoked with swans,
accompanied by the Ādityas, the Sādhyas, the Maruts, and the Aśvins,

1.54.s:
rudrairviśvasahāyaiśca yakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ ..
digbhirvidigbhiśca tathā khecaraiśca mahāgrahaiḥ ..5 ..
1.54.d:
रुद्रैर्विश्वसहायैश्च यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः ॥
दिग्भिर्विदिग्भिश्च तथा खेचरैश्च महाग्रहैः ॥5 ॥
1.54.m:
along with the Rudras and the Viśvedevas, the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas,
the directions, intermediate directions, celestial wanderers, and great planets,

1.54.s:
nimnagābhiḥ samudraiśca māsartvayanasaṃdhibhiḥ ..
nakṣatraiśca muhūrttaiśca kālasyāvayavaistathā .. 6 ..
1.54.d:
निम्नगाभिः समुद्रैश्च मासर्त्वयनसंधिभिः ॥
नक्षत्रैश्च मुहूर्त्तैश्च कालस्यावयवैस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
1.54.m:
the rivers and oceans, the junctures of months, seasons, and solstices,
the lunar mansions, muhūrtas, and divisions of time,

1.54.s:
devarṣibhiḥ puṇyatamaiḥ siddhaiḥ saptarṣibhistathā ..
rājarṣibhiḥ puṇyatamairgandharvairapsarogaṇaiḥ .. 7 ..
1.54.d:
देवर्षिभिः पुण्यतमैः सिद्धैः सप्तर्षिभिस्तथा ॥
राजर्षिभिः पुण्यतमैर्गन्धर्वैरप्सरोगणैः ॥ 7 ॥
1.54.m:
the most holy divine seers, the Siddhas, and the seven seers,
the most holy royal seers, the Gandharvas, and the hosts of Apsarases.

1.54.s:
carācaraguruḥ śrīmānvṛtaḥ sarverdivaukasaiḥ ..
brahmā brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭho daityaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 8 ..
1.54.d:
चराचरगुरुः श्रीमान्वृतः सर्वेर्दिवौकसैः ॥
ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठो दैत्यं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 8 ॥
1.54.m: Surrounded by all the gods, the glorious teacher of the moving and unmoving, / Brahmā, the foremost of the knowers of Brahman, spoke these words to the Daitya:

1.54.s:
brahmovāca .. prītosmi tava bhaktasya tapasā'nena suvrata ..
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yatheṣṭaṃ kāmamāpnuhi .. 9 ..
1.54.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥ प्रीतोस्मि तव भक्तस्य तपसाऽनेन सुव्रत ॥
वरं वरय भद्रं ते यथेष्टं काममाप्नुहि ॥ 9 ॥
1.54.m: Brahmā said: / I am pleased with this penance of yours, [my] devotee, O you of noble vows! / Choose a boon, good fortune to you! Obtain your desire as you wish!

1.54.s:
hiraṇyakaśipuruvāca .. na devāsuragandharvā na yakṣoragarākṣasāḥ ..
na mānuṣāḥ piśācā vā hanyurmāṃ devasattama ..1.54.10..
1.54.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुरुवाच ॥ न देवासुरगन्धर्वा न यक्षोरगराक्षसाः ॥
न मानुषाः पिशाचा वा हन्युर्मां देवसत्तम ॥1.54.10॥
1.54.m: Hiraṇyakaśipu said: / May neither gods, Asuras, nor Gandharvas, nor Yakṣas, Uragas, nor Rākṣasas, / nor humans, nor Piśācas slay me, O best of the gods!

1.54.s:
ṛṣayopi na māṃ śāpaṃ kruddhā lokapitāmaha ..
śapeyustapasā yuktā varametadvṛṇomyaham .. 11 ..
1.54.d:
ऋषयोपि न मां शापं क्रुद्धा लोकपितामह ॥
शपेयुस्तपसा युक्ता वरमेतद्वृणोम्यहम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.54.m: Nor may the sages endowed with penance curse me when enraged, O grandfather of the worlds! / This is the boon I choose.

1.54.s:
na śastreṇa na cāstreṇa giriṇā pādapena ca ..
na śuṣkena na cā''rdreṇa vadhaṃ me syātkathañcana .. 12 ..
1.54.d:
न शस्त्रेण न चास्त्रेण गिरिणा पादपेन च ॥
न शुष्केन न चा'ऽर्द्रेण वधं मे स्यात्कथञ्चन ॥ 12 ॥
1.54.m: May my death not come by weapon or missile, by mountain or tree, / nor by what is dry, nor by what is moist, in any manner whatever!

1.54.s:
bhaveyamahamevārkaḥ somo vāyurhutāśanaḥ ..
salilaṃ cā'ntarikṣañca nakṣatrāṇi diśo daśa .. 13 ..
1.54.d:
भवेयमहमेवार्कः सोमो वायुर्हुताशनः ॥
सलिलं चाऽन्तरिक्षञ्च नक्षत्राणि दिशो दश ॥ 13 ॥
1.54.m: May I alone become the sun, the moon, the wind, the sacrificial fire, / the water, the intermediate space, the lunar mansions, and the ten directions!

1.54.s:
ahaṃ krodhaśca kāmaśca varuṇo vāsavo yamaḥ ..
dhanadaśca tathādhyakṣo yakṣaḥ kiṃpuruṣādhipaḥ .. 14 ..
1.54.d:
अहं क्रोधश्च कामश्च वरुणो वासवो यमः ॥
धनदश्च तथाध्यक्षो यक्षः किंपुरुषाधिपः ॥ 14 ॥
1.54.m: May I be anger and desire, Varuṇa, Vāsava, Yama, / Kubera, the superintendent, the Yakṣa, and the lord of the Kiṃpuruṣas!

1.54.s:
brahmovāca ..
ete divyavarāstāta mayā dattāstavādbhutāḥ ..
sarvānkāmānimām̐stasmātprāpsyasi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 15 ..
1.54.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
एते दिव्यवरास्तात मया दत्तास्तवाद्भुताः ॥
सर्वान्कामानिमाम्̐स्तस्मात्प्राप्स्यसि त्वं न संशयः ॥ 15 ॥
